messages.text: Do Not Use
Nothing else seems to happen.
What is it you would like to do?
This worn out sign reads: "Cove Hold - Trade caravan waystation". The sign also points to the northeast for Tanirith, and to the west for Wailsrond and Sparklestone.
This worn out sign reads: "Tanirith - Farmlands". The sign also points to the northeast for Tanirith, and to the south for Wailsrond and Spaklestone.
This worn out sign reads: "Tanirith - Farmlands". It also points to the east for Tanirith, and to the west for Wailsrond.
This worn out sign reads: "Tanirith - Farmlands". It also points to the north and to the northeast for Tanirith's grapevine yards, and to the east for Tanirith proper.
This worn out sign points to the south for Tanirith, and to the northeast for Arvoranaan and Lantharond.

(Please answer the following question truthfully, since it is meant simply to allow this scenario to adjust itself for your better enjoyment. Answering one way or the other will in no way take away anything from this scenario. Thank you, and have fun!)
Did you previously complete Part One of the Sword Lands Trilogy, "Trouble in the Sword Lands"?
YEA
NAY

Nearly six full moons have passed since your heroic adventuring band brought down a trio of self-styled Overlords which, as part of a secretive Inner Council of nine, conspired to weaken the Sword Lands in order to conquer this rich and lush region.

But the Overlords' designs went beyond simple conquest; indeed, their aim was to turn the Sword Lands into a vast power base from which they would enslave all of the Realmz continent, and establish a new empire ruled by psionic beings like themselves.

For the Overlords are, as you had found out, of the race of humans known as Keryndorhyans, a reclusive people who live hiden somewhere on the far-away eastern continent of Anarym. And these folks are themselves descendants of the fabled Lankharhans,

the race of psionic humans that established and ruled the legendary Empire of Lankharh, which fell some nine millennia past. Thus, the Inner Council of Overlords sought nothing less than to bring about a second Lankharhan Empire on the Realmz continent.

So it was understandable when everyone breathed a sigh of relief once you had defeated the trio of Overlords that operated in the Sword Lands. From the simple peasant to the most powerful Merchant Lord, all rejoiced and sung praises to you and the Fates.

And all were quite content to go back to their normal lives, as they were. But you, and your adventurer's instincts, knew better. You could not forget the fateful words of a fourth Overlord you had spoken to after the final battle with the Overlord trio,

which promised the coming of an all-out war in the Sword Lands. Since you had found out already that the Warlord of Sharranth, the last known ally of the Overlords in the Sword Lands, was building a large army poised to march out and sweep the area,

you felt certain that the Overlord Conspiracy was far from over. Yet, no one would listen to you, not even the High Council of Tanirith.  Hence, you had taken upon yourselves to secretly watch Sharranth and its army for any signs of dangerous activity.

A mere sevenday ago, you were sadly proven right: with deadly efficiency, Sharranth's army swarmed into the Heartlands through the town of Aranys, rapidly overtaking the mining town of Sparklestone. And now, it is already laying siege to Wailsrond.
After days of evading and fighting sharranthine patrols, you have finally made it back to the Eastern lands, near the great city of Tanirith. Bloodied and tired, only one thing drives you:
To your dismay, one of Sharranth's pursuing patrols have caught up with you, seeking to prevent you from warning Tanirith of the invasion!
You manage to flee for your lives!!!
To your relief, a passing patrol of knights of the Flame rides fast to your help!

After the clash, the commander of the knight patrol comes up to you smiling: "Well fought, Heroes! We're honored to have been of help to you! Just who are those hoodlums who've attacked you? And I noticed that they be mixed in with minotaurs and ogres?"

You explain to him that this band was but a sample of Sharranth's mercenary army which has invaded the Heartlands. Only then does the commander see your caked wounds and dirtied vestments. "By Tyr!" He whispers, a look of devastation crossing his face.

"You were right all along, as High Commander Fireblade had told us!" He adds. You can't help but smile at the mention of your former comrade, who is now leading the Knighthood of the Flame. "Let us heal you, brave ones" offers the commander,

Nearly six full moons have passed since a dire conspiracy, which threatened all of the Sword Lands, was exposed and undone.  As natives of the area, you had heard all about the mysterious Overlords which, as part of a secretive Inner Council of nine,

had sought to weaken the Sword Lands in order to conquer them, helped with traitorous accomplices whom had been promised positions of power once the lands were taken. But thanks to a heroic band of adventurers from Bywater, these plans had been foiled.

For the Overlords are, as you came to understand, of the race of humans known as Keryndorhyans, a people who live hidden somewhere on the far-away eastern continent of Anarym. And these folks are themselves descendants of the fabled Lankharhans,

So it was understandable when everyone breathed a sigh of relief once the trio of Overlords operating in the Sword Lands was defeated, despite all the troubles they had caused. From the peasant to the richest Merchant Lord, all sung praises to the Fates.

And all were quite content to go back to their normal lives. But you, and your adventurer's instincts, knew better. Indeed, six other Overlords remained out there, somewhere. And having heard numerous tavern rumors that the Warlord of Sharranth,

who is the last known ally of the Overlords in your lands, was building a large army poised to march out, you felt certain that the Overlord Conspiracy was in truth far from over. But no one would listen to you, let alone the Lord Paladine,

or the High Council, of Tanirith. Hence, you had bravely taken upon yourselves to go to the Western region of your Sword Lands, in order to secretly watch the city of Sharranth and its army for any signs of suspicious or dangerous activity.

After the clash, the commander of the knight patrol comes up to you: "Well fought, strangers! Although our sworn duty dictates it, we're always glad to help! Just who are these hoodlums who've attacked you? And they be mixed in with minotaurs and ogres?"

"Our High Commander, Lord Fireblade, told us about you and your warnings: you were right all along, as he suspected!" You can't help but smile at the thought that someone important like the leader of the knighthood of the Flame WAS listening after all.

You further explain quickly to the commander what you saw and what Sharranth's army has already accomplished. The commander and his knights make no efforts to hide the respect they have for you: "Let us heal you, brave ones" offers the commander,
(Thank you for having played Trouble in the Sword Lands! We hope you'll enjoy this second installment of the Sword Lands Trilogy!)

As usual, there is a lot of coming and going through the gates of Tanirith. However, you notice more soldiers and knights than normal moving about the battlements, as if making defensive preparations. Looks like the knight commander was quick indeed!
All sorts of people move in and out through Tanirith's gates, as usual.

However, and aside the increased number of soldiers and knights on watch, you notice that make-shift tents have been pitched around and about the gates. You then realize that these are used by refugees from the Heartlands who fled from the invaders.

You cross the gates of the part of Tanirith known as "High Town", where the richest people of the city live, including its rulers. You notice numerous guards eyeing you suspiciously, but you are otherwise left alone.

The gates to Tanirith's old cemetary are closed. A sign hanging upon them reads: "Closed until further notice. Danger! Stay away! If desired, seek further information at the home office of Adventurers Inc."
This is a temple of Agrah, Goddess of Agriculture, Abundance, and Harvests. You notice numerous disciples and priests plowing and working fields near the temple. Do you enter?
This temple is dedicated to Codan, God of Law and Order.
This temple is consecrated to Lharishar, Goddess of Life.

These are the famous Scholar Halls of Tanirith. A temple dedicated to Erond, the God of Thought, Crafts and Knowledge, is also on these grounds; this is not surprising since priests of Erond function as teachers and caretakers of the Scholar Halls.

A priest approaches you: "Greetings, good visitors. Only students enrolled in the Scholar Halls may enter them; however, anyone may of course enter Erond's House."  Do you want to go to Erond's temple?
This is a temple of Ukkor, God of the Seas.

The estates of Jarad Noll are as beautiful as ever. One of the guards nod to you in recognition: "Greetings, Heroes! If ye are to see High Councillor Noll, me have to tell ye that he's busy at ta High Council."  With a polite nod, you leave.

The estates of the late, unlamented Golam Thrall appear to belong to someone else now. Mercenary guards on watch call out to you from the battlements: "Hey, ye! This be Shalla Thrall's private property! No one's allowed, so begone!"
This looks like a bank.
You knock and knock, but no one answers. You realize that this establishment must be closed at this time.

A priest approaches you, his lantern shining bright in the darkness: "My apologies, good visitors, but the Scholar Halls, as well as Erond's House, are closed. Come back in the early morning until early evening." With a nod, you leave.
This temple is consecrated to Tyr, God of Honor, Chivalry and Justice.
This is a temple dedicated to Danuur, God of Commerce, Riches and Luxuries.
Having killed one of Tlarantale's chosens, the angry Goddess sends one of her Handmaidens to punish you!
Monstrous versions of nature's denizens eye you for their meal!
Hungry rats attack!
Monstrous spiders attack you!
Angered boars attack, percieving you as a threat!
You have disturbed some snakes!
Natural denizens of the area attack you, percieving you as a threat!
A pack of wolves on the hunt have chosen you as their prey!
Marauders decide to rob you of your valuables!
Up to no good adventurers decide to relieve you of your valuables!
A raiding band of humanoids make the jump on you!
Wandering Hags eye you as easy prey!
Trolls make the jump on you!
A pride of hunting great cats make the jump on you!
Giants make the jump on you!
Monstrous scorpions eye you as meal!
A hunting band of yetis make the jump on you!
Primitive beast men attack!
Wyrms eye you as their next meal!
You are under attack by a warband of Sharranth!
Some of the sewers' dwellers attack you!
Dwellers of these desert wastes eye you as easy prey!
Dwellers of these forests eye you as easy prey!
Dwellers of the Underearth eye you as easy prey!
Creatures of the sea attack you!
You have sailed into the path of fearsome sea serpents!!!
You are boarded by pirates!!!
You have sailed into the path of terrible Moby Whales!!!
Upon its death, the creature releases a cloud of choking spores!
Upon its death, the creature releases a gusting poisonous cloud!
A backlash of mental energies is released upon your opponent's death!
Feeling the pangs of empty stomachs, each member of your party grabs a quick snack from the rations carried in your backpacks.
Without any rations with you, your weakened bodies suffer the effects of lack of food!
This is a temple of Agrah, Goddess of Agriculture, Abundance, and Harvests. Do you enter?
A sign hanging above the door of this small house reads: "Thalya's Street Corner Shop".
This Central Market of the city is closed.
This is a Central Market. Numerous folks, merchants, artisans, farmers, and fishermen are already in the premises, busy at buying, looking or bartering. Do you enter?
A sign hanging above the door of this building reads: "Harbor Master - Central Port West". There are numerous sailors and mariners about; nothing much of interest to you.
A sign above the door of this building reads: "Harbor Master - Central Port East". There are numerous sailors and mariners about; nothing much of interest to you.
A beautifully wrought sign of iron reads: "Ephaestor's Armors and Weapons".
Do you want to enter?
You can hear the loud sounds of hammers hitting against anvils coming from within. Do you enter?
A sign hanging above the door of this rustic shop reads: "Schaxam's Little Shop of Magics".
The sign hanging above the door to this little shop reads: "Tanirith's Exotic Imports".
A sign hanging above the door of this artisan's shop reads: "Dungarh's Leatherworks".
An old, worn-out sign hanging above the door of this shop reads: "The Mariner's Toolbox".
This Bazaar of the city appears to be closed at this time.

This is a Bazaar where the well-off and wealthy come to shop. Numerous folks are already walking around and about stands of produces, craftworks, and exotic items, busy at buying, looking or bartering. Do you enter?
A sign hanging above the door of this little shop reads: "Rhondo's General Store".
This is the crypt where Ptaraz, founder and first king of Tanirith, lies buried. Despite searching around and about the ancient structure, you find no way to enter it.
The secret passage leading to the Portal of Graaz'z has been collapsed, making it impossible to clear the rubble and use the passage anymore. You wonder who might have been responsible for this ...

Inside this cave, you notice that tons of rubble are blocking what appears to have been a secret passage going deeper into the mountains. It is now hopelessly blocked. You wonder who did this, and why ...
To your surprise, you see that the passage behind this secret door has been hopelessly collapsed, making it impossible to use. You wonder who did this and why ...

To your astonishment, the pass leading to the forgotten temple of Graaz'z is hopelessly blocked by tons of rubble, snow and ice.  From where you are, you can't even see whether the old crumbling temple is still standing or not.

Was this due to an avalanche or earthquake, or did someone cause this on purpose? You are left wondering... Feeling with certainty that the Overlords would never be foolish enough to hide in the same place twice anyhow, you get on your way.
This cave is empty.
You are under attack!

As you enter this cavern, you see a twelve foot-tall, six-armed golem barring your way. Its eyes illuminated by an eerie glow of red light, it speaks to you although its mouth does not move: "NO ONE IS ALLOWED TO PASS HERE. BEGONE OR BE DESTROYED!"
Do you leave?

"THEN, AS DECREED BY MY MASTERS, YOU MUST BE DESTROYED!" Intones the golem, as it starts moving its six arms -each holding a sword- faster and faster. You can't help but be surprised by its unatural agility. At that, the golem bears down on you!
You quench your thirst with the water in your waterskins.
Without water with you, dehydration takes its toll!
This looks like the marketplace of this village. No one is about at this time, and all the stands are closed or empty.
This is the marketplace of this village. Although small, many villagers are about buying and bartering goods. Do you go in?
You see on this tree large coconuts. These would make not only good rations but would help quench your thirst. Do you pick some of the fruit?
Who volunteers?
In a dry and searing landscape such as the one you find yourselves in, one cannot have enough fresh water. Do you take some for your travels?
On this tree, you see plump, round fruits which look tasty and fullfilling. These would make great rations for your travels. Do you pick some?
On this bush, you spot numerous berries which look very tasty. These would make excellent rations for your travels. Do you pick some?
The water is poisoned! Your party member, having drank some of it while filling a waterskin, falls to its ill effects!
The berries are poisonous! Your party member, having gulped many of them while picking enough to make rations, falls to their ill effect!
Do you take some water from the well, for your travels?
Thanks to your spell, you manage to float harmlessly over this patch of quicksand.
You walk right into a large patch of quicksand! Those that weren't paying attention sink deep and fast!
Without ropes or any kind help, death comes a-calling ...
With the help of ropes, all those in this predicament are rescued ... but not without being hurt from lack of air before being taken out of the quicksand.
Deadly rays shoot forth from the top of the Stone Towers, reducing you to nothing but ashes!
Just as the Stone Stowers gather power to activate themselves, the Pearl of Asturia begins to pulse loudly. Immediately, the Towers power down and remain silent, granting you safe passage.
This strange building appears dedicated to Quanthaas, God of Time, Longevity, Infinity and Eternity. Do you enter?
Hot boiling lava pit! Those of your party which were not paying attention slip into this pit; not enough to fall all the way in, but more than enough to be seared gravely by the lava!
Hot, boiling lava pit! But thanks to your spell, every member of your party is spared from slipping or falling into it.
Hot, choking volcanic gases spurt out of the lava pit! Those who are not vigilant enough breathe in the noxious mixture!
Hot, volcanic gases spurt out of the lava pit! But thanks to your spell, none of you was caught by surprise and breathed any of the the noxious mixture.
You see in the distance threatening creatures coming your way. Do you confront them?
Avalanche!!!
Those of your party who don't react quickly enough get hopelessly buried under tons of ice and snow!
Thanks to your spell, you all manage to evade the terrible onslaught of tons of ice and snow!
Unknowingly, you have been walking upon a thin crust of hardened ice, and now it cracks open right under your feet, collapsing because of your weight!
Those of your party that are not quick enough fall into the seemingly bottomless chasm that has just been revealed!
Thanks to your spell, you manage to float harmlessly over the gnawing chasm that just opened, allowing you to move on.
Flash blizzard!
To your amazement, you notice that an invisible bridge stands right in front of you, spanning the surface of the lake and leading to the other side!
Earthquake!
Those of your party who do not react quickly enough are buried under tons of rocks and volcanic ash!
Thanks to your spell, you manage to float harmlessly away from the quaking earth under you!
Those of your party that are not quick enough are swallowed up by the quaking earth, ripping itself open under your feet!
The earth rips open, releasing hot, toxic volcanic gases!
Those of your party that do not react quickly enough breathe in the burning, noxious, deadly gases!
Thanks to your spell, you all manage to evade the noxious, deadly gases!
The volcanic activity and earthquakes of the Rockies cause a tsunami, which is coming your way!
In no time, you and your ship are swallowed up by the gargantuan waves of the tsunami!
Thanks to your vigilance, you manage to maneuver you ship out of harm's way!
Sandstorm! You are forced to make camp in order to protect yourselves. After long hours of the violent rushes of winds and sand, the sandstorm finally dissipates, allowing you to resume your journey.
You have walked into a sink hole! Those of your party who do not react quickly enough are swallowed up by the sinking sands!
Sandworms!

Panting and tired after the battle, you notice that a few gemstones are encrusted into the bodies of these creatures.  Smiling to each other for your good fortune, you take good care at removing these gems for your own use.
Shantiles living in this cave react aggressively to your intrusion!
Strange trees attack you!
You stumble upon frost giants engaged in a bloody clash with beastmen. Do you jump into the fray?
Wisely, you walk away.
Eagerly, you join the fray!
Panting and tired, you wonder why neither side would accept your help.
The area here climbs steeply, going as high as 100 feet, effectively preventing you from going on further. What would you like to do?
After a good start of climbing, your party member loses footing on the slippery rocks, taking a hurting fall back down.
But thanks to your spell, your party member floats harmlessly, managing to climb back to safety. However, the rest of you are still stuck.
Success! You all end up on the top of the climb!
The area here drops to a steep 100 feet down, effectively preventing you from going on further. What do you want to do?

The descent of your party member begins well, but soon enough your comrade loses footing on the slippery rocks. Thanks to the rope, you manage to bring your party member back up, but not without severe bruises and bumps.
Success! You all get down safely and effortlessly.
After securely fastening your rope, you all manage to climb down safely.
A sudden squall bears down on your ship!
In no time, your ship is turned over by the raging waves, being blasted to pieces by their pounding and the blowing winds, leaving you to drown amidst the tempest.
Thanks to your vigilance, you maneuver your ship quickly enough to evade the raging tempest, which dies down as suddenly as it had been born.
You spot in the distance a caravelle fast approaching.  Guessing that this might be a pirate ship on the prowl, you maneuver your ship to evade it; but try as you might, it catches up with you!
You spot in the distance a caravelle fast approaching. Guessing that this must be a pirate ship on the prowl, you maneuver your ship quickly enough to evade it.
You spot a merchant ship being under attack by a pirate ship. Do you sail fast to help the merchant ship?
You eagerly join the fray!

The pirates defeated, the captain and the merchant come up to you, smiling: "Our thanks, strangers! Please accept this token of our gratitude". After setting the pirate ship afire and thanking them for their gift, you part sails with the merchant ship.
You sail on, leaving the merchant vessel to its fate.
Sailors, mariners and harbor workers are busy at loading and unloading merchandise and foodstuffs from the vessels.
You notice that someone, or something, is lurking in the shadows along the buildings, obviously stalking you. Do you turn around to ambush the would-be stalkers?
Seeing that they have been found out, the would-be cutthroats run off deeper into the side-streets and away from you, leaving you alone.
Just as you continue on your way, the stalkers make their move!
Cutthroats seize their chance and make the jump on you!

After the clash, you wonder if there is any militia patrol around, and how is it they do not appear to do their duty as they ought. Then you realize that patrols must be scarcer at this time of the night.
You get bumped by someone as you walk amidst the crowd. Only to late, you notice that your money pouches feel lighter.
Your vigilance allows you to spot underwater creatures fast approaching your ship. Do you maneuver your ship to sail forth and meet them head on?
In no time, you are upon them!
You spot in the distance a caravelle fast approaching. Your instincts tell you that these are pirates on the hunt. Do you maneuver your ship to sail forth and take the fight to them?
You manage to sail away safely from the danger.
A wench stops you: "Ye are not allowed here!" she chides you sternly. Embarassed, you leave.
A burly barkeeper grins at you: "Greetings, gents! What can I serve ye?"
A sour-looking barkeeper eyes you with annoyance: "Oy! Whot do ye want?"
A barkeep smiles at you shyly: "Greetings, good gents. How may I serve ye?"
What do you answer?
"Food for all of ye will cost 6 golds total. Which one of ye will pay?"
"If ye don't have enough gold, or don't want to spend any, then don't waste me time!" At that, you walk away.
"Sorry, but ye shouldn't ask for anything if ye won't spend the gold, or if ye don't have enough gold to spend." At that, you walk away.
"Come back when ye want to spend yer gold, or when ye'll have enough to pay." At that, you walk away.
"Go take a seat and a drudge will bring yer servings."
Soon enough, you are brought large, steaming bowls of stew with boar and vegetables. Although average in preparation and taste, it still hits the spot.
"Drinks will cost 6 golds total. Who'll pay?"
Soon enough, you are brought large mugs of some local mead. Somewhat bitter, it is however quite strong and refreshing.
"Food and drinks for all of ye will cost 15 golds. Which one of ye will pay?"

Soon enough, you are brought your servings. The meal consists of steaming bowls of boar and vegetable stew, along with mugs of locally-brewed mead. The stew is average but hits the spot well, while the mead is bitter but quite refreshing and strong.
You decide to review your options further for a later time.
A storekeeper smiles at you: "Greetings! Do ye need to buy something?"
"Ah, well; come back if ye need anything, then." Shrugs the storekeeper, as he turns away from the counter to do some paperwork.
"Here's what we have available."
"Welcome!" An innkeeper greets you. "Rooms are 2 golds per person. Do ye want a room for the night?"
"Come back whenever ye want." The innkeeper replies, before going over some paperwork.
"Who will pay?"

The innkeeper then takes you to your room: "Have a good rest, gents. Tomorrow, feel free to leave when ye want: we'll take care of servicing the room after." With a parting wink, the innkeeper leaves you.

As you get back downstairs, you come across the innkeeper: "Ah! Had a good rest? Good. Safe journeys, good gents!" At that, the innkeeper goes about cleaning your room and preparing it for other patrons.
A sign above the door of this establishment reads: "Cove Hold Waystation". This place looks like a store as well as an inn.
Do you leave?
This man, obviously a half-elf minstrel, is playing music for the patrons. From their reaction, they are quite enjoying his songs, which he plays with zest and mastery.
As he finishes his last song, and collects the generous donations from the appreciative patrons, the half-elf minstrel turns to you as if expecting to receive a donation from you as well.

But instead of asking you for a donation, he stops dead in his tracks, gawking at you in surprise: "Ye Gods! Could it be?" He exclaims, half-smiling, half-unbelieving. "Do I, Riel Moonsong, humble minstrel by excellence and tale-spinner grandiose,

have the most fortunate and serendipitous honor of being in the presence of the acclaimed Heroes of the Sword lands?" Somewhat dumbfounded by his glibness, you simply nod in reply. "Then praise be the all-knowing and unfathomable Fates!" He exclaims.

He then leans closer to you, as if mindful of being overheard: "You see," he whispers in a conspirational manner, "I have been looking for you, oh famous gents, so that mayhaps I could join your jolly band and write epic ballads of your heroic deeds."

"The muses have left me" he adds, feigning distress and despair, "and thus, of late, I can play naught but old songs over and over, until my poor soul dries out of distraught." Smiling mischeviously with a wink in his eye, he opens his arms

with flourish and dramatic flair: "So, what say you, noble ones? May I join yon jolly band, so new songs of daring deeds and heroic bravery be composed by this minstrel master?" Do you accept Riel Moonsong into your group?

"Splendid!" Riel exclaims, feigning relief as if being saved from the jaws of death themselves. "I may be saved from those moody muses yet!" He adds with another wink, as he gathers his travel gear to join you.
"Ah, well." Replies Riel, exagerating disapointment in his voice and manner. "I suppose I shall have to play those old songs until I die of sheer boredom." At that, you move on.
Riel Moonsong is once again entertaining patrons. "We meet once more, oh adventurous ones!" He says with a wink, after finishing his song. Do you reconsider and accept Riel into your ranks?
You go on your way, as Riel begins another song.

But instead of asking you for a donation, he stops, examining you with interest: "Say, good gents!" He exclaims, "You lot seem of most noble and daring stock indeed! How fortunate that I, Riel Moonsong, humble minstrel by excellence and grandiose

raconteur, find myself in the presence of esteemed individuals such as yourselves! Am I correct in assuming that you be adventurers?" Dumbfounded by his glibness, you simply nod in reply. "Splendid! The all-knowing and unfathomable Fates be praised!"

He then leans closer to you, as if mindful of being overheard: "You see, I have been looking for adventurous folks such as yourselves, so that mayhaps I could join such a grand group and write epic ballads of heroic deeds and foolhardy travails."
Local fishermen are busy at unloading their catches and gutting them, while others are repairing fishing nets and mending their fishing caravelle.
A sign here reads: "Memorial City Park". It points to the east.
A sign here reads: "Memorial City Park". It points to the north.
A woman, holding her two young babes, approaches you. Obviously, she is homeless. "Please, good gents. Could ye spare a gold piece fer me children?" She asks, fearful of your reaction.
A young, dishiveled scamp runs up to you: "Oy, me good gents! Could ye spare a gold fer little me?" He asks, grinning with a boyish face.
Do you give the gold piece?
You cross paths with a militia patrol.
Without money to spare, you go on your way while ignoring the beggar.
Which one of you does the honors?
"Thank ye, good gents." The beggar replies with heartfelt gratitude, before walking away.
A bronze wrought sign hanging above the door of this place reads: "The Journey's End".
Just as you are about to go through this door, the innkeeper stops you: "My apologies, good gents, but no one's allowed through there."
A sign hanging above the door of this place reads: "Inn of the Sea Trader".
"Welcome!" An innkeeper greets you. "Rooms are 10 gold pieces per person; do ye want a room for the night?"
Just as you are about to take those stairs, the innkeeper stops you: "Sorry, good gents, but only patrons who have paid for a room are allowed to go upstairs."
A sign hanging above the door of this place reads: "The Captain's Inn".
This sign reads: "Riverside - Trade Caravan Waystation". It also points North for Sparklestone, and South for Wailsrond and Tanirith.
A sign hanging above the door of this establishment reads: "Riverside Waystation". This place looks like a store as well as an inn.
This sign reads: "Creek Dale - Trade Caravan Waystation". It also points to the North for Lantharond, and to the South for Arvoranaan and Tanirith.
The sign hanging above the door of this place reads: "Creek Dale Waystation". This establishment appears to be a store as well as an inn.
This sign-post reads: "Rock Forest - Trade Caravan Waystation".
The sign hanging above the door of this place reads: "Rock Forest Waystation". This establishment looks like a store as well as an inn.
This sign points to the North-West for Bywater, to the North-East for Aranys, and to the South for Sharranth.
This sign points to the East for Sharranth, and to the South for Mountainside.
This sign points to the West for Mountainside, to the South for Cedar Cove, and to the South-East for Sharranth.
This old, worn out sign reads: "Cedar Cove".
This old, worn out sign reads: "Barony of Mountainside".
This old sign points to the West for Bywater, and to the East for the Sword Lands.
This battered sign points to the North for Sparklestone, to the West for Wailsrond, and to the East for Tanirith.
This battered sign points to the East for Sparklestone, and to the West for Aranys.
This sign-post reads: "Aranys". It also points to the North-West for Sharranth, to the East for Sparklestone, and to the South for Dagger Keep and Wailsrond.
This battered sign points to the North for Aranys, to the East for Dagger Keep, and to the South for Wailsrond.
This battered sign reads: "Wailsrond". It also points to the East for Wailsrond's Farmlands, and to the North for Dagger Keep and Aranys.
This battered sign reads: "Azure Cove". It also points to the West for Wailsrond, and to the East for Sparklestone and Aranys.
You refill your waterskins.

You come into the entrance of an enormous, dome-shaped cave. The ceiling is lined with glowing fungi of all colors, illuminating the entire area as if you were on the surface at dawn, but with unsettling shades of purple, lavender, turquoise and lilac.
There is no doubt that you have entered the great cavern of Naaz'Tzaraneen, the undercity of the shadow elves!
You leave the eery light of Naaz'Tzaraneen and enter the darkness of the underearth once more.
You find a secret door to a small tunel going within the rock to the west. Do you go in?
You find a secret door leading to an area filled with water, to the east. Do you go?
This cave has collapsed, hopelessly blocking the way to the underground complex you explored months ago.
This cave is empty.
Opening this unlocked trap door, you see that rock and mud are now hopelessly blocking the access to where it used to lead.
Opening this unlocked trap door, you see that the shaft it opens to is now hopelessly filled with rock and mud. You wonder what used to be under there ...
The secret entrance leading to the compound of the defunct, unlamented Rogue Lord Doran Ghall has been sealed shut with rock and mud.
The entrance to this mine has been collapsed, and therefore remains unaccessible.
This secret tunnel has been collapsed. You wonder who did this and why.
The restless undead attack, longing for your living flesh!
Your alertness allows you to spot a group of undead coming your way. Do you take the fight to them and help Tanirith get rid of such a dark menace?
You find that one of the graves has been dug up, with the remains of the person laid to rest here stolen. You wonder who  -or what-  would do such a thing, and why.
As you move to evade the marauding undead, you run right into another group of undead -likewise on the hunt!
You are suddenly ambushed by a warband bearing the banners of Sharranth!
After taking care of your wounded and taking possession of whatever gear deemed useful from your fallen enemies, you gather your troops and move on.
You spot a warband bearing the banners of Sharranth coming in your general direction. Do you wait to ambush them?
Lying in wait in the underbrush, you jump onto the marching warband as it passes your way!
A warband bearing the banners of Sharranth comes your way. Thanks to your magical disguises, you are not paid any attention, except for a few critical stares.
Scouts from your warband come back in earnest, bringing news that they have spotted a warband bearing the banners of Sharranth coming in your general direction. Do you lie in wait to ambush them?
Deftly organizing your warband to lie in ambush, you wait until the Sharranth warband passes in front of you and give the signal to attack!
You lie securely hidden in the underbrush until the warband is well far away from you.
You direct your warband in a long detour, taking you and your troops well away from the Sharranth warband.

Looking over the strange cards, you notice that this deck holds a subset of sixteen cards which are adorned by figures of shadow elves, lowly peasants, dark dwarves, or jesters, or which are just plain blank. Which type of card do you use?

Holding card firmly, a strange magical aura begins to envelop all of you. In an instant, all those of your party that were not shadow elves have their features altered to look like one! Why, all of you together could pass like a shadow elf party!

Holding the peasant card firmly, a strange magical aura begins to envelop every member of your party. In an instant, all your features are altered in a way to make you look like lowly, dirty, and smelly peasants!
Not certain what to do and wishing to review your options for a latter time, you carefully replace the deck of cards in your packsack.

Holding the dark dwarf card firmly, a strange magical aura begins to envelop every member of your party. In an instant, the features of each and everyone of you is altered to that of a grimy, gruffy, shadow dwarf!

Holding the jester card firmly, a strange magical aura begins to envelop every member of your party. In an instant, all your features are altered to make you look like a theatrical troop of jesters, jugglers, and entertainers!
Consequently, the card dissipates ... leaving your deck one card less.
Holding the blank card firmly, a strange magical aura envelops all of you ... but nothing happens. Consequently, the card dissipates, leaving your deck one card short.
Holding the blank card firmly, a strange magical aura begins to envelop each member of your party. In an instant, your disguises are removed and you are back to your old selves!
You return to the surface.
Deep inside this cave, you notice that the back-wall has crumbled, revealing a narrow tunnel leading deeper underground. Do you walk into the tunnel?
You enter a large cave which is currently unoccupied. You are certain that you could rest safely here.
You leave the safe cave.
The ceiling of this cave has collapsed, hopelessly blocking its entrance.
The tunnel has been collapsed at this junction; you suspect the dwarves of Dwarven Halls did this to prevent any further shadow elf incursions into their territory.
You enter a part of the cave complex which is filled with underground water.
You disturb some mushmen poddlings that are resting among this patch of huge fungi!
You run into a group of mushmen; feeling threatened, they attack!
You spot in the distance a group of mushmen foraging about. Do you charge ahead to attack them?
Charging ahead, the mushmen hear you and scamper away, disappearing into patches of fungi here and there.
You disturb a group of shantiles who have taken shelter here!
A hunting party of troglodytes attacks!
Troglodytes living in this cave attack the intruders that you are!
Among the troglodytes' sparse (but filthy) belongings, you find a few baubles of value.
This cave is inhabited by the tribe chief of the troglodytes; suffice it to say that he's not very happy by your intrusion!
The tribe chief and his last followers now take matters into their own hands!
You make your own the belongings of the tribe chief, which are most likely things found here and there in the caves and brought to him by his subservient peers.
This large cave is filled with cobwebs of various sizes and shapes, from floor to ceiling. You can't help but have a bad feeling about this.
You disturb the occupants of this cave!
You are ambushed!!!
Your alertness allows you to spot a party of shadow elves lying in wait to ambush you. Do you rush ahead to attack them?
Wisely, you alter your course to evade the would-be ambushers.
You run into a colony of monstrous spiders. Thanks to your disguises, they allow you passage without harm!
You run into a group of shadow elf arachnians. Thanks to your disguises, they not only leave you alone, but bow respectfully (and with fear) as you go on your way!
Earth gnomes are busy working their mines, while others transport the ores and stones to the processing warehouses across the street.
This old monument is dedicated to Jasper Flameheart, the founder of the Order of the Knighthood of the Flame.
You find a small button protruding at the base of the monument. Do you press this button?
One of the marble slabs at the base of the monument slides, revealing an opening with stairs which appear to lead to the sewers of the city. Do you go in the sewers?
After a few moments, the slab of marble slides back in place.
This passage is filled with rocks, bricks and rubble. It would appear that the walls and ceiling here collapsed, hopelessly blocking the way further.
This iron door is hopelessly jammed, having accumulated centuries of grime and rust.
These crumbling stairs are useless since they are blocked with rubble and debris.
Some of the newly created undead rise up to defend their masters!
Upon Zeghor's destruction, all of his lower creations turn to dust!!!

You come upon a gruesome laboratory where some sort of sorcerers are pumping foul concoctions into corpses. As you come in, one of these sorcerers shouts an alarm, activating huge guardian golems made of flesh!
This door is locked.
The door stubbornly refuses to give way!
Your party member is smarting from the attempt.
Success!
The lock is too stubborn.
You hear strange moanings and shufflings from behind the door.
The door is opened!
The trap appears to have been disabled.
You find a trap!
Your search reveals a small lever at the base of one of the tombstones here. Pulling it, the tombstone slides to the right, revealing a ladder going down.
A guard stops you: "I'm sorry, good gents, but a warrior group of your size cannot be allowed within the city."
Realizing that you can't walk around with your warband everywhere, you order your warband captain to establish camp just outside the southwest gate, until you return to pick them up again.

You find yourselves near a large camp of soldiers and warriors, their tents flying the colors of Sharranth. Numerous patrols come and go within the perimeter of the camp.  It would seem that you have not been spotted yet.
You enter a corridor with walls that have been patiently, and carefully smoothed. You wonder who, or what, did this. And why.
With your best war cries, you rush ahead to overtake the camp! Initially taken aback, the Sharranth warriors manage to mount up a semblance of defense.
More warriors from the camp join the fray!
You try to flee for your lives, but you are quickly and mercilessly cut down!
Ransacking the camp, you collect any valuables that you can find.
You approach unseen near the camp, then suddenly rush to sack it! Taken by surprise, the warriors scramble to meet your attack.

As you get on your way, one of the soldiers on guard at the camp shouts: "It's them! It's those Heroes!" At that, the camp's captain rushes out of his tent: "Get these enemies of the Warlord!" he orders. Immediately, numerous warriors scramble to attack!

As you get on your way, a soldier on guard at the camp shouts: "Adventurers!" At that, the camp's captain rushes out of his tent: "You know the orders of our Warlord! Get these miscreants!" Immediately, Sharranth warriors scramble to attack!

At the order of your warband captain, all the footmen charge into the camp. Initially surprised, the Sharranth warriors scramble as best as they can to meet the attack. Immediately after, you cavalry in turn rushes ahead, with you not far behind.

At the order of your warband cavalry officer, your cavalry charges into the camp. Initially surprised, the Sharranth warriors scramble to meet the charge. Immediately after, your footmen in turn rush ahead, with you not far behind.
Just as you are about to give the order to move out, you are ambushed by Sharranth warriors from the camp! It would seem that you and your warband had been spotted after all!!!
With your best war cry, you storm into the camp. Initially surprised, the Sharranth warriors scramble to meet your attack. Immediately after, your warband in turn joins the fray!
After positioning your troops, you give the signal to storm into the camp!

Thanks to your disguises, you are not bothered. To your surprise, you see that the Sharranth warriors are breaking camp, probably having received orders to relocate to another position. Soon enough, they are packed and on the march.
With your war party along with you, it would be impossible to go in there. It would be better to come back another time, and without your warband.

As you get on your way, a soldier on watch shouts: "Intruders! They must be spies!" Immediately, the rest of the warriors scramble to attack you! It would appear that your disguises did not help you this time.
More warriors join the battle!!!

As you approach Wailsrond, you see that a contingent of Sharranth's army is undertaking an assault of the city's battlements. Soldiers from Wailsrond seem hard pressed to repel the invaders. Do you rush into the battle to help Wailsrond's soldiers?
Your warband storms into the battle, with you not far behind it!
You walk away, but not without feeling a bit of guilt about your decision. The fading sounds of battle compound that lingering guilt.
In addition, you can't help but notice that members of your warband are glancing at you with reproach, visibly unapproving of your decision.
You storm into the battle, with your warband not far behind you.
You position your troops, then give the signal to engage the enemy!
After the battle, a wailsrondese lieutenant walks up to you. Although tired and bloodied, he manages to smile warmly at you.

He then gasps in astonishment: "By the Gods! 'Tis be you, the Heroes of Wailsrond!" Shouting his announcement, the other soldiers gather around you, cheering loudly.  Clasping your hands with renewed hope, the lieutenant continues:
"Ye don't know how much yer arrival means to us! Things are getting more desperate by the day. I may be no seer, but I'm certain that Lord Pyre will be mighty happy to see ye!"

The gates of the city are then opened to let the soldiers and wounded back in. "Please, enter and go speak with our Lord as soon as ye can!" The lieutenant adds, before helping his men clearing the battlefield of the wounded and the dead.

You help your warband captain to take care of your own wounded, then bid him to make camp again just outside of the city's North gates. With a tired -but proud-  smile, he gets to organizing the warband for camp.
You then proceed to enter the city with haste.

As the gates close behind you, you see numerous soldiers and citizens scrambling about with buckets of water, trying to extinguish some of the houses and buildings which have been set on fire during the battle.
Only then do you notice that all too many houses and buildings have been burned or damaged already. Wailsrond is truly suffering a harsh and bloody siege.

The fires are extinguished soon enough, the soldiers and citizens showing great organization in dealing with such disasters. That Wailsrond still stands proud and defiant in the face of a siege is a telling testimony to Lord Pyre's leadership qualities.
Soldiers on watch at the battlements cry out in alarm: "Here they come again! Sharranth's attacking!!!" Immediately, Wailsrond's soldiery scramble to meet the attackers.
After the battle, soldiers, priests and citizens gather the wounded and the dead. Despite the victory, you sense that the spirits of all Wailsrondese are sliding into greater despair each day.
With relief and pride, you see that your warband has already left camp to meet the attackers as well!

"In the name of Wailsrond, I thank ye, noble strangers!" He exclaims, clasping your hands firmly. Gazing over the battlefield, he sighs with relief: "Ye don't know how much the arrival of adventurers like you means to us!" He shakes his head at that.

"I tell ye: things are getting more desperate every day, and we need all the help we can get. I'm no seer, but I'd wager our good Lord Pyre will want to speak with ye. By the Abyss, I know we could sure use noble folks like ye against Sharranth!"

You then realize that the lieutenant has no inkling that you are in fact the Heroes of Wailsrond: it would appear that your disguises are very effective indeed. You are thinking that perhaps you should shed them, if you want Lord Pyre to recognize you.

Realizing that you can't indeed take your warband with you anywhere you please, you tell your warband captain to make camp outside the Northwest gates, until you come back to pick them up. With a firm nod, your captain orders the warband to march out.
Soldiers are ever watchful for any signs of the enemy. Upon your approach, the gates are opened to let you through.
The gates are closed behind you, and the soldiers resume their alert watch.
The city's gates are locked shut here.

These gates have a sign above them which reads: "First Port". Some harbor workers, merchants, sailors and carts carrying goods pass through the gates in both directions. However, this activity pales to the usual business that would normally occur here.
You also notice numerous soldiers about the battlements, ever watchful for any signs of enemy attack.

However, this camp and the forces it shelters are too large in numbers for you to face, even with the help of your warband. Not wishing to take any foolish risks, you manage to walk away from the camp's perimeter, unseen.
However, this camp and the forces it shelters are far too large in numbers for you to face. Not wishing to take foolish risks, you manage to walk away from the camp's perimeter, unseen.
This secret door opens to a tunnel which appears to lead far upside, perhaps even to the surface. Do you go into this tunnel?
After nearly a week of a long and arduous journey, you begin to feel a breeze of fresh air from the surface world.
This tunnel appears to lead quite deep underground, perhaps even as deep as the underearth. Do you go on in this tunnel?
After an arduous weeklong journey, you enter into the dampness and darkness of the underearth.
This sign points to the North for Lantharond, and to the South for Creek Dale, Arvoranaan, and Tanirith.
Warriors and adventurers are training hard to master the skills that Swordmaster Jothun has taught them.
You hear the loud sounds of weapons clashing about, along with the audible grunts and groans of people fighting with intensity.
The sounds of trainees fighting hard to learn their skills echo loudly still as you leave the gymnasium.
You go back upstairs.
You go downstairs.
A finely wrought bronze plaque hangs above the door of this building. The plaque reads: "Adventurers Inc. -Home Office-".
You enter a large lobby where numerous adventurers are seated, waiting. In the center, you see a lady sitting behind a kiosk, smiling warmly at you.
A guard stops you: "Only authorized folks are allowed in there!" Embarassed, you leave.
You go upstairs.
The sign on this door reads: "Jobs and tasks department". Do you go in?
The sign on this door reads: "Information and lore department". Do you go in?
The sign on this door reads: "Administration". Do you enter?
"Greetings and welcome to Adventurers Inc.!" The lady exclaims. "Our motto is 'If you are not successful, we are not successful'! So, good gents, what services do you require from us?"
"Here's what we are currently offering."
"As you wish." Replies the lady, still smiling warmly. "Come back any time you need our services; remember: we are open every day of every sevenday, all day and all night!"

"You will not be disapointed!" Replies the lady in earnest. "Our new resident sage is among the most knowledgeable of the region! Here's a voucher: take this to our Informations department, on the second floor. Thank you for using our services!"
A sign above this door reads: "Stairs to second floor". Do you open the door?
A guard stops you: "Only those with a valid voucher are allowed to pass!" Embarrassed, you leave.
A sign above this door reads: "To Gymnasium". Do you enter?

As you show your voucher to this old, grumbling dwarf, he goes into a fit: "Ye durn fools! This ain't the right voucher! This is fer the Information section! Whot do me look like: a durn librarian?" You make haste to get out of here.
"I'm sorry." This venerable elf tells you, as you show him your voucher. "This is a voucher for the Tasks section, right door next to here." As he goes back to his books, you leave.

This aging, but still towering and fit, warrior scowls at the voucher you present to him: "This is the gymnasium, not a bloody library or job-office!" Without further due, he goes back to supervising his trainees.
"I'm sorry, but we can dispense only one voucher at a time. I suggest you use the voucher that you already have, before coming back for another one?" Embarrassed, you leave the kiosk.
"You will not be disapointed!" The lady replies. "We have a good choice of tasks to offer. Here's a voucher; go to the second floor and present it at our Tasks department."
"Ah! Yes indeed!" Replies the lady. "Skills training is a brand new service that we offer. Take this voucher to the gymnasium in the basement; our resident Swordmaster will take care of the rest!"

Upon your approach to this kiosk, a venerable elf  looks up to you from behind old and dusty tomes: "Ah! Seekers of lore!" He exclaims, smiling. "I offer knowledge of many  things; each topic costs 100 gold pieces in coins."
"Here is the knowledge I offer."
"Not enough money, eh?" Without any further due, your voucher is taken. "Come back another time."
"No voucher?" This person exclaims, aghast. "Ye need to get one!" Embarrassed, you leave.

"Where to begin? To know about Astaroth, one must journey back in time some fifteen millennia, during the age of the empires of Telluria and Macremia. Although both emerged on the continent of Anarym, explorers of the two empires sailed far and wide."

"Some of these explorers eventually arrived on the eastern shores of our Realmz continent, and colonies bethroded to Telluria or Macremia were settled. But as the two great empires began their Great War on Anarym, so did their respective colonies here."

"You must understand that these two empires were incredibly advanced both in arcane arts and technology; hence, terrible weapons which blended the two arts were created and used during the Great War of the Empires; with devastating results as well."

"Such terrifying weapons were of course used by the two major colonies of the empires over here, namely Asturia -bethroded to Macremia- and Algaroth -bethroded to Telluria-. Algaroth used to be on the shores just north of Lantharond."

"Whereas Asturia in turn lied further north of Algaroth, occupying the fertile plains there. In any event, their use of the terrible weapons of destruction caused the birth of the Volcanic Rockies, at the same time levelling both colonies."

"Algaroth was completely buried by the lava from the newly born volcano, and to this day lies deep under dirt, rocks and hardened lava southeast of the volcano. Most of Asturia was likewise destroyed, its once fertile plains turned into sand and dust."

"As the Tellurian and Macremian empires destroyed each other on Anarym, so had their colonies here. Over time, the two empires were forgotten and their advanced knowledge was lost; over here, the names of Asturia and Algaroth became as one into legends."

"And the name which came to unite them in the ashes of history was Astaroth, the same name given to the hot, rocky, and dusty desert that lies north of the Volcanic Rockies, which comprises Asturia's territory but now closed off by lava-made mountains."

"Now, numerous stories about Astaroth exist, most of them being pure fables. But one thing is certain: it is a forbidding place, where great sandworms and other monstrous creatures roam, most likely mutated long ago in the wake of the devastation."

"However, three fables appear to be grounded in historical possibilities, although they remain to be proven fully. One, some descendants of Asturia and Algaroth may live to this day in Astaroth, albeit in a degenerated form as near-mindless beastmen."

"Two: it is said that huge stone towers guard to this day a secret passage which would lead to where the city of Asturia used to be, buried under sand; these silent guardians are rumored to shoot strange beams of light that disintegrate any trespasser."

"And three: those who founded Lantharond centuries ago may have been descendants of a tribe of Tellurians that survived the devastation; it is said that the blood of the Dragonheart dynasty which rules the city today is strong in Tellurian ancestry."
The sage pauses to catch his breath. "Well, would you like information on another topic?" He asks, eager to dispense more of his knowledge.

"As you wish." Replies the venerable elven sage, as he takes your voucher to file it among his mass of paperwork. "Come back again." He adds, before sitting down to read another one of his old, dusty tomes.

This aging but towering and fit Swordmaster is overseeing trainees which are practicing hard. "Welcome!" He booms in a deep voice, while eyeing you critically. "I take it ye wish to learn new skills?" You nod, showing your voucher.

"Very well. I am SwordMaster Jothun, and this be my domain." He adds with a sweeping gesture over the gymnasium. "The fees for skills vary depending on which skill ye wish to learn; training for each skill takes two sevendays."
"These are the skills that I offer to teach ye."
Swordmaster Jothun scowls at you: "Ye were already trained for that! Choose a skill that ye haven't trained for, eh?"

Swordmaster Jothun nods. "Survival, yes. I'll train ye to better withstand the damaging effects of heat and cold; this won't make ye immune, but at least allow ye to be a little bit more protected against them."

You come upon a vast desert of sand and rocks, enclosed by towering rugged mountains. A hot, scorching wind blows, the only sound heard amidst the dreary silence of this desolate landscape, except for the faint rumblings of the volcano to the south.

You wonder what horrific creatures could live in such a desolate and forbidding place; checking on your food and water supplies, you pray that a few welcoming oasises are to be found as you begin your journey in this harsh and unforgiving landscape.
With much relief, you leave the desert wastes behind you, only to be welcomed by the rumblings of the Volcanic Rockies.

You come upon a vast mountain range of blasted peaks, scorched rocks, and suffocating air of dust and sulfur. You hear with dread the rumblings and lava spasms of the volcano further to the north, as you feel the earth trembling beneath your feet.
With much relief, you leave the Volcanic Rockies behind you. As if in parting, the volcano rumbles a few more times, its spasms becoming fainter as you journey further onward.
You hope that you won't lose you footing as you travel this arctic wasteland. You also wonder what horrific creatures would live here.
With much relief, you leave the Snowy Rockies behind you.
After nearly a full sevenday of travel, you begin to hear the faint rumblings of the earth to the north.
After nearly a full sevenday of travel, you finally smell fresher and cooler air; you must be nearing Lantharond indeed!
After nearly a full sevenday of travel, you begin to feel cold air blowing in your direction. As you gaze northwards, you glimpse at towering mountain peaks that are covered with ice and snow.
After nearly a full sevenday of travel, you begin to feel warmer air again.
A group of Fire giants are guarding this cave!
This cave leads to a tunnel carved within the mountains. Do you go in?
A group of Frost giants are guarding this cave!

For two, long and arduous sevendays, you train your bodies to better withstand hot and cold weather, under the strict but expert tutelage of the Swordmaster. Once your training is done, you all gain bonuses to resist heat and cold!
"So, do ye wish to be trained for another skill?" The Swordmaster asks.
"Very well; I bid ye safe journeys and safer returns!" The Swordmaster replies, as he takes your voucher and returns to supervise his other trainees.
The Swordmaster nods. "Ah, advanced fighting! With this skill, ye will gain an attack bonus as well as a defense bonus, using my advanced thrust, parry and dodge techniques that I'll be teaching ye."

During the next two arduous, strenuous and exhausting sevendays, Swordmaster Jothun drills into you his experienced fighting techniques through direct training and exercises. After that time, you all gain an attack and defense bonus!

Jothun nods. "Ah, yes. Discipline. A most essential tool! Through the meditation techniques that I have developed and which I'll be teaching ye, your minds will gain greater focus and strength, making them harder to be influenced or distracted."
After two sevendays of intense meditation and practicing complex mental exercises under the wise mentoring of Jothun, each of you gains a better resistance to mental attacks!

A grumbling old dwarf sits behind this kiosk, shuffling through a hopeless mess of paperwork. He is visibly frustrated by his disorganization: "Durn it! Cain't ye see I'm busy?" He snarls. "I'm always being bothered! Ah well, I s'pose ye want a job?"
You then recognize the dwarf as being the same one that used to provide tasks in the branch office of Adventurers Inc. in Aranys. His left eyebrow raised, he seems to recognize you as well.

"Hah! Well, I'll be an orc's behind!" He exclaims. "Ye're the lads that used to bother me back in Aranys, ain't ye? Surprised to see me here, eh? Well, after Sharranth's armies came into town, I had to close off the branch office fer the time being."

Going back to his mumbling while shuffling more through his chaotic filing system, he finally retrieves a couple of parchment sheets. After looking them over with annoyance, he shows them to you: "Ye want small jobs or big ones?"
"Here's what's available."
Small
Big
"You already have accepted to perform a task. You must complete the task assigned to you before you can take on another one."
The lady smiles warmly: "Congratulations for a job well done! Our contacts informed us of your success; here is your justly deserved reward."
The old dwarf scowls: "Durn it! This one's been done already, and the company won't pay fer something already done! Me sorry, lads, but ye have to choose another job."
This rusted trap door is hopelessly locked. You notice a surprisingly well-preserved lock, which appears impervious to any tampering. You wish you had the key to open this trap door.
With the sewer key in hand, you easily unlock the trap door, revealing stairs going down to a dark and damp place.
You find yourselves within a very old sewer system, probably one that was used by a previous incarnation of Tanirith. You wonder what forgotten ruins, or terrible creatures, you will find here.
You are suddenly attacked by a band of pillagers, intent on hoarding whatever they can find in the ruined city!
You spot a band of pillagers, busy at hoarding anything valuable they can find in the ruined city. Do you stop them?
Yelling your most fearsome war cry, you attack!

You try to run for your lives, only to be overwhelmed. As you lay fallen and unconscious, the pillagers strip you all of your equipment and valuables, leaving you for dead as they run away to find another place to pillage or new victims to terrorize.
The shore here falls steepily, preventing you from going on further.
You decide to leave things well enough alone. As you walk away from the unruly bullies, you can't help but feel responsible for this catastrophic fall of Wailsrond.

This tragedy is making you wonder if you had ever been truly deserving of the tile of "Heroes" bestowed upon you months ago by the people of Wailsrond. Has it been only months? In truth, you feel like it happened years ago ...

The castle gates lay wide open, their once sturdy iron doors laying about, battered beyond recognition. The bodies of numerous soldiers of Wailsrond lay fallen here and there, having lost a heroic -but doomed- final stand.

And so it is. You hoped against all hope that this could not happen, and yet you knew it had to be the moment you entered the city. As you stand still, struggling to accept the terrible reality of it all,

the smoking rubbles of Lord Pyre's castle lay in front of you, their silence accusingly revealing your failure. Was this then, the preordained fate of the city? To be sacked, and then condemned by history to disappear under earth and dust, forgotten?

Wary that Sharranth soldiers may still be in the area, and not wishing to alarm survivors, you tell your warband captain to camp outside the city's North gates, until you come pick them up. With a firm nod, your captain orders the warband to march out.

To your horror, you find the iron doors of the city gates wide open, twisted and battered beyond recognition. Numerous bodies lay about, both of Wailsrond's and Sharranth's armies. As you gaze with dread beyond the open gates, you see houses burned down,

buildings reduced to rubble, and even more dead bodies, too many of which are civilians. As you hear the terrified cries of people being victimized, the crying of the despaired, and the crackling of dying fires, you finally grasp the grim truth:
You have arrived too late, and Wailsrond has fallen.

In a daze, you realize that the city has been mercilessly ransacked and burned, raped of all of its wealth and left to crumble in a state of anarchy and chaos. After long, stunned silence, you finally gain back your composure and enter the fallen city.
From beyond the crumbling city gates, you still hear the faint cries of the few remaining survivors being victimized, and the crazed shouts of unruly bands of pillagers.
You tell your warband captain to camp outside the city's North gates, until you come pick them up. With a firm nod, your captain orders the warband to march out.
As hard as you try, you just can't open this secret door. It appears to be hopelessly stuck for some unfathomable reason.
