"Make sure to never lose this!" Anthraxus Storm warns you. "Now, I must go back to Sharranth; you go meet my Herzog, then come to my castle, for we have much to discuss and plan!" Shaking your hand one last time, the Warlord and his knights leave.

"Oh, and I'd advise strongly against going back to Tanirith," the Warlord calls out from the entrance of the cave, "since I am certain my old friend Essain Helmfire will have news rather quickly of our bargain!"
A patrolling warband from Sharranth comes your way. Upon seeing you, the captain of the warband gives you a respectful salute and orders his warband to march on.

You spot a supply caravan flying the colors of Sharranth being under attack. The cargo it is transporting is likely to resupply the invading forces. Losing the caravan could cause a set back for Sharranth. Do you help the caravan?

After the battle, the caravan captain gives you a respectful salute as his men pick up any useful item from the attackers, to add them to the caravan. Immediately after, the caravan goes on to its destination.

You find yourselves near a large camp of soldiers and warriors, their tents flying the colors of Tanirith. Numerous patrols come and go within the perimeter of the camp.  It would seem that you have not been spotted yet.

As you get on your way, one of the soldiers on guard at the camp shouts: "It's them! It's those traitors!" At that, the camp's captain rushes out of his tent: "Get these enemies of Tanirith!" He orders. Immediately, numerous warriors scramble to attack!
With your best war cry, you rush ahead to overtake the camp! Initially taken aback, the Tanirith warriors manage to mount up a semblance of defense.
"It's them!" One of the soldiers shouts, pointing at you. "The traitors!" Immediately, the patrol moves in to apprehend you!

Panting and tired after this clash, you wonder if it would no be best to make a run for it and get out of this place! In any case, to quickly move to side-streets to avoid the eyes of onlookers, and perhaps another patrol.
Knights of the Flame and more militia soldiers rush to join the fray!
"It's them!" One of the knights shouts, pointing at you upon your approach. "The traitors!" Immediately, the knights move in to apprehend you!
You begin to feel tremors in the ground.

You then hear a large explosion coming from far away, to the northeast. Looking over there, you see a huge plume of smoke. Something must have happened with the collapsed volcano in the Khanark Rockies. Your gut instincts tell you it must not be good.
With a grim smile, you dart swiftly into a side-street, hoping not to have been seen. As the sounds of battle become fainter, you can't help but be impressed by Anthraxus Storm's boldness.
"Bah!" Someone else replies. "Don't count on them! I heard that they got a better offer from the Warlord of Sharranth, and took it!" A woman shakes her head, sadly: "Then we may be doomed ..."

You overhear a conversation: "Me heard that the Heroes of the Sword Lands accepted to join the Warlord of Sharranth!" Muses a sailor. "Lies!" Replies a woman, vehemently, "They would never do that!" The sailor becomes flustered: "I tell ye they have!"

You overhear a conversation: "Me heard that the Lord Paladine's adventurers accepted to join the Warlord of Sharranth!" Muses a mariner. "Lies!" Replies a woman, vehemently. "They'd never do that!" The mariner becomes flustered: "I tell ye they have!"

You overhear a conversation: "Adventurers! Bah! They go where the money is! I hear some of them accepted to join the Warlord of Sharranth!" Muses a fisherman. A woman shakes her head, sadly: "Then we may all be doomed ..."

"Welcome, noble gents!" Jarad Noll greets you, smiling. Immediately, goblets of wine are served. "Now," continues the councilor, as he sits down, "we have much to discuss. As you've seen, the High Council is in disarray, bogged down by indecision."

"Although the High Council has never been exemplary in ordered and proper conduct of political affairs and legislation," he drolls, "things have degenerated to such a state that nothing is decided, nothing is done, nothing happens."

The councilor sighs heavily. "We might as well get rid of the High Council: the way things stand, Tanirith would not even notice! The unsettling aspect of it is that no councilor is overtly or consciously derailing the Council." He shakes his head.

"No. It's more subversive, like an invisible shroud muddling the wits of the councilors, making them debate, discuss, question, object, and whatever, whenever a decision must be made or when a consensus must be reached. Hence, all is debate nowadays."

"And without ending." Jarad adds, before taking a sip of his wine. "Well, you understand now why I strongly suspect a spy or traitor among the High Council. After all, only a councilor -and a shrewd one at that- would be capable of such manipulations."

"Only another councilor has the opportunity for this. Indeed, he must know other councilors to influence them with a glib tongue and whatnot behind the scenes, so that all proceedings of the Council end up being derailed." He then chuckles.

"Since I was the first to have such suspicions, and since I was the one who correctly suspected Golam Thrall of treason last year, the Lord Paladine entrusted me with the task of exposing this new menace to Tanirith's peace." He winks at that.

You then remember hearing that councilor Noll was indeed involved in exposing the treasonous high councilor Golam Thrall, with the help of the adventurers who eventually defeated the three Overlords that threatened the Sword Lands.

Jarad continues: "I've already narrowed down my list of 'suspects' to two councilors. Mind you, I have to admit that I came down to these two simply because the problems within the Council began around the time of their return to council affairs."

"The first would be councilor Nomune Ngallan. He returned to Tanirith and reclaimed his council seat two months ago, after a year-long absence. He had gone to far away Westmore City, not long after the demon problems or whatnot had been resolved there."

"Daughter of the unlamented Golam Thrall and his only rightful heir, she returned to Tanirith four months ago to claim her father's estates and, in doing so, taking his place on the Council." Jarad sighs anew.

"She had left years ago, unable to see eye-to-eye with her father about something or another. In any case, she eventually settled in far away Specularn, where she became a merchant lord in her own right. She apparently had her father's gift for trade."

"He spent a whole year there establishing new trade deals, all of which have been very lucrative and profitable for him and his mercantile company." Jarad pauses to take yet another sip of wine. "My second suspect is, not surprisingly, Shalla Thrall."

"To her credit," Jarad goes on, "she not only survived the war with the giants there a few years ago, but even managed to increase her holdings. That's why I find it strange that she took her father's death rather badly, even if he was a proven traitor."

"And to come back here, after selling all of her holdings in Specularn?" Jarad shakes his head. "I don't know. Maybe I'm seeing shadows where there are none, but ..." He leaves his sentence in suspense, then shrugs. "Well, that's it: Shalla and Nomune."

"So, I'm asking for your help in this. I need solid proof. In the case of Shalla, it could be easily construed that I'm seeking to victimize her for her father's sins, like a political vendetta. Nomune is quite popular, so the same applies for him."
"Mind you, this does seem like I have acquired a habit of asking for your help to unravel conspiracies that threaten our city." He adds ruefully.

"In any event, we must be extremely careful in this matter. That is why I ask you to come speak with me and show any proof that you may find, against either one ... or both!" Jarad winks at that. With a nod and firm clasp of hands, you take your leave.
Councilor Jarad Noll is busy conferring whith his advisors and business associates. You decide it best not to disturb him for nothing.
Mercenary guards are on watch at these gates: "This be the private property of High Councilor Jarad Noll!" Intones one of them. "If ye have no business here, then leave!" With a shrug, you walk away.

Mercenary guards are on watch at these gates: "This be the private property of High Councilor Shalla Thrall!" Intones one of them. "If ye have no business here, then leave!" With a shrug, you walk away.

Mercenary guards are on watch at these gates: "This be the private property of High Councilor Nomune Ngallan!" Intones one of them. "If ye have no business here, then leave!" With a shrug, you walk away.
As you approach the gates to Nomune Ngallan's estate, his guards open the doors: "Come quickly!" One of them whispers. "Lord Ngallan has been expecting you!"
The door of this house is not only unlocked, but not even closed. You notice that the immediate surroundings of this house are rather unkept, as if it had been abandoned for quite a while.
Upon remembering of having heard, at one time or another, that an assassin's guild may have been hiding here, you find all of this rather strange.
Do you enter ?
You find here a pile of burned documents and letters. Sifting through the ashes and useless bits and pieces of unburned parchment, you find a badly fire-damaged and barely legible letter.
You attempt to make sense of the badly damaged text on the burned and torn sheet of parchment.
You read the restored letter.
Looks like the contents are hardly incriminating. You wonder why it was among the burned documents of the abandoned house of the assassin's guild.
A sign hanging above the door of this house reads: "Maps of All Trades".
"Welcome!" Chimes a burly furfoot, smiling gingerly. "I am Maps Longroads, and yes: I sell maps, maps that I've made myself during my travels! Welcome to my humble map shop!"
"Now, which map of mine would interest you?"

"Hello, cousin Maps!" Exclaims Ellai. "Cousin Ellai! So good to see you!" Intones Maps, as both rush to each other's arms. Immediately, both begin sharing news and stories, with much laughter and zest. You then cough impatiently. "Oh my!" Exclaims Maps.

"I'm so sorry! It's just that I don't have much chance at seeing my valorous cousin Ellai, what with his Quest for the Real Law of War and all." Ellai groans: "That's Quest for the Code of the True Warrior, Maps!" He then shakes his head, chuckling.

"Oh, my, yes! Of course!" Replies Maps, embarrassed. "Anyhoo, you won't regret having Ellai at your side, good gents!" He adds with a confident wink. "He's a fighter that one! Well, then ... where were we? Oh, yes! My beautiful maps!"
"No problem!" Replies Maps. "Come back any time!"
"Ah yes! This one was quite dangerous for me to make, when I went there! That'll be 5000 gold pieces in gems, so 50 gems, please."
"Ah, yes! I discovered this entrance quite by accident! That'll be 200 golds in gems, so 2 gems, please."
"Here you go! That'll be 500 gold pieces in gems, so 5 gems please."
"Ah! This one is very rare. I am quite proud of it! That'll be 10000 golds in gems, so 100 gems please."
"Well, that one is my pride and joy! I nearly died to make it! It also gives the location to a frost giant stronghold. So, this one will cost you 500 gems, please."
"Not enough money, eh? Ah, well, come back another time."

On a hunch, you ask him if he could restore the badly burned letter you found in the abandoned assassins' guild house. "Sure!" Maps muses. "I am a master papermaker and map restorer! That'll cost ya 100 gold pieces."

After two long hours, Maps come back with a brand new parchment. "I could not really restore it, but through treatments and stuff too complicated to explain, I could reproduce it by hand. Here's the 'restored' letter!"
Putting the restored letter back in your travel sack, you take your leave. "Come back any time!" Maps exclaims in parting.
Wererats are camped here, and they are not happy with your intrusion!
Having dispatched the occupants of this place, you realize that you could safely camp here without fear of being attacked.
This trap door is locked. What do you want to do?
Opening the trap door, you find a rope ladder going down to a lower level of the sewers.
Wererats are standing guard here. Upon seeing you, they attack, along with their pets!
More join the fray!
You've stepped on a critter.
Your search reveals a loose brick in the wall here. Do you pull on the brick?
You hear something huge moving, somewhere distant from here.
Do you push the loose brick back in place?
You find the accumulated wealth of the wererats!

In this well furnished room, you see a huge wererat standing tall, staring at you angrily with his beedy, fiery eyes. You see him surrounded by other wererats, as well as some humans. Looks like you have disturbed an important meeting here!
"I'm Rhodin." The huge wererat announces. "Why are ye invading my home? My peoples have no quarrel with ye! Leave, and thisss matter will be forgotten." Do you back off and leave?

Just as you lower your weapons and begin to back away, one of the humans walks over to Rhodin and whispers angrily into the Ratlord's ear. "I've jussst been informed of new developmentsss." Continues Rhodin. "I'm afraid we can't let ye leave here."
"Ssso have the Fatesss decided!" Adds Rhodin, before his wererats launch their attack along with the Ratlord's human guests!
You stumble upon numerous wererats standing guard in this rather well furnished room. They immediately attack!
The room appears like a salon and dining room combined. You deduce that the leader of these wererats must be living here.
This large room is some sort of communal eating area. Numerous wererats are here. One of them sees you and sounds the call to arms!
Searching the place, you find a few useful items on tables and in cupboards.
This is a dormitory were numerous wererats are sleeping or taking a rest, some with their rodent "pets". One of the wererats shouts the alarm upon your intrusion!
After the clash, you search the beds and cots. You manage to scrounge up a few interesting items for your use.
You stumble into a trap! A flurry of poisonous darts rain on you!!!
This room is empty. You are quite certain that you could rest within without being disturbed or attacked.
The trap consists of a loose tile on the floor: stepping on it depresses it and activates the mechanism of the trap.
You manage to bypass the trap's trigger!

You find yourselves in an ancient room filled with grime, fungus, garbage and filth. The stench of the place is making you nauseous. In the center stands an old, worn out column-like marble statue filled with bas-reliefs of rats in various poses.
The place is eerily quiet, aside from the muted shuffling and scurrying noises you hear from within the walls.
Suddenly, the room gets filled with hordes of hungry rats swarming to their fresh dinner: you!
More rats swarm in!!!
At the base of the column, you find that the eye of one of the rat bas-reliefs is in fact a button that could be pushed. Do you press this button?
A small compartment within the column is revealed! Within, you find a set of pipes that radiate a strong magical dweomer.
The water here begins to run deeper; from the sound and smell of it, you know this tunnel opens to the sea.
These stairs lead down to a tunnel under the sewers. Do you take these stairs?
This rusted trap door has been nailed-shut. You also notice a surprisingly well-preserved lock, which appears impervious to any tampering.
You wonder who did this, and why.
Although you have a strong suspicion that the authorities of Tanirith are likely responsible, not wishing to re-live another tragedy like the unlamented Cult of Lankharh.
You find yourselves standing in front of a large portal made of solid bronze. Gold-etched symbols and bas-reliefs adorn this ancient work of art. Strong magic radiates from it as well.
As you pass through the door, the magic prevents the passage of your party members of netherwordly origin.
You notice two huge rings attached to the portal. Do you pull on the rings?
Just as you are about to grab the rings, nine phantomatic beings appear in a rush of cold winds. Each appears as a beautiful maiden, although their haunting eyes betray their outerwordly origins.
"We are the guardians of Dianchuur's temple." One of them intones in a cavernous, but musical voice. "Begone from here, and ye shall live." Do you back off?
As you back away from the portal, the guardians disapear in gusts of winds, as quickly as they appeared.
"Then ye leave us no choice but to perform our sworn duty!" Replies the guardian. At that she, along with her "sisters", attack!
With these guardians defeated, you grab the rings and pull on them. Opening the portal, old worn-out stairs are revealed, leading further down.

As you lay down, bloody and on the verge of losing consciousness, one of the guardians stands next to you: "We shall not end yer life today." She intones menacingly. "Ye may count yerselves lucky ..."
At that, the guardians disapear in gusts of winds, as quickly as they appeared.
The portal stands open still. Do you go back downstairs?
This door is protected by a powerful magical shield, preventing entry.
The shield responds with a magical backlash!!!
The shield is dissipated!

The door opens to a small chapel. The place is dusty and damp, soiled with centuries of accumulated grime and fungus. Facing you at the other end of the chapel, you see an old, worn out altar of solid marble.
Guardians appear to destroy the intruders that you are!
The altar is covered with centuries of dust, codwebs, grime and fungus. You find nothing interesting, or particular, about it.
However, your attentiveness reveals a small button on the side of the altar. Do you push the button?
After the clash, you finally get the chance to push the small button on the altar's side.
Sliding to the right, the altar reveals a cache of treasure in the floor! This was probably forgotten by Dianchuur's priests when the temple was abandoned by them.
To your dismay, you do not find the icon of Dianchuur among the items left here. You wonder where it could be, if it is somewhere at all in this abandoned temple.
You hear Riel Moonsong sighing heavily. "You know," he mumbles, "it is becoming quite evident that things are never easy with you." He then chuckles at that.
The putrid guts of the creature spill onto the ground.  Thousands of vile, buzzing insects had been feeding on the horrid creature's innards.
The construct reverts to inanimate stone, trapping your weapon.
Your search reveals a loose brick on the east wall. Do you pull on it?
The wall to the west moves upwards!

You enter an old chapel. Although quite dusty, time nor dampness appear to have exercised any effect on its decor. You notice numerous marble statues of Dianchuur standing next to the walls, and an altar of platinum at the other end facing you.
Suddenly, some of the statues come to life and move to attack the intruders that you are!
You find the secret treasure of the temple!

The altar is covered with centuries of dust. Aside from the fact that it is made of solid platinum and etched with numerous esoteric symbols which you cannot fathom, you find nothing interesting, or special, about it.
As the altar begins to sink to the ground, the wall behind it moves upwards, revealing a secret chamber!

The walls around these stairs are covered with watery leaks and dripples. A faint rumble of moving water is heard beyond the walls. You deduce that these stairs lead to an underground passage beneath the Tarterys river, which runs through Tanirith.
This ladder leads to a lower level of the sewers. Do you go down?
You find a few interesting items.
This iron gate is locked with a state of the art locking mechanism. You doubt you could manage to force it or pick it. Looks like you'll need the right key to open this gate.
With the sewer key, you are able to unlock and open this gate.
This grime- and fungus-covered statue bears the likeliness of Orcas, the God of Horrors and Undeath.
Do you open this sarcophagus?
Its occupant rises to attack you!
You find numerous potions and concoctions.
You are overwhelmed by the almost palpable aura of evil that permeates this place. You wonder with dread what awaits you beyond ...
This is a dormitory where some necrowizards are resting. Of course, those that are here are not happy to see you!
Searching the cots and beds, you find a few items of interest.
You find a secret stash of treasure!

This room is lavishly furnished, acting as both study and bedroom. Dimly lit, you see wall-to-wall shelves of books and parchments. Whoever lives here must be quite a scholar; however, no one seems about.
Suddenly, the shadows of the room begin to stir. Before you realize what is going on, you find yourselves under attack!
Alerted by the sounds of the fracas, necrowizards come to investigate!

You have entered a small chapel. Or rather, a veritable nightmare. At the other end facing you, you see a man who has just driven a ceremonial dagger into the heart of some poor wretch, which was lying in chains on an altar made of solid obsidian.

Behind the altar, you see a towering statue of Orcas. Next to the man who has just made the horrible sacrifice, numerous necrowizards are chanting, while numerous undead creatures watch silently the unholy ceremony.

One of the undead creatures screams, having seen you. "Who are you?" Demands the man at the altar, angrily. "As my name is Zeghor Deathmaster, I swear that your blood will flow to honor the Dark One!" At his silent gesture, the undead move to attack!
"Very well!" Intones Zeghor Deathmaster. "Now, you shall face the wrath of Orcus!" At that, he and his retinue attack!
Zeghor Deathmaster calls upon more undead to his help!

The obsidian altar is drenched with the blood of the poor wretch that Zeghor Deathmaster just sacrificed. You feel a strong aura of evil emanating from the altar; so strong is the aura that it almost chokes you with its almost palpable darkness.
Defacing or destroying the altar would be a prudent thing to do. Do you destroy the altar?
Under your repeated bashing, the altar easily breaks up in pieces, consuming at the same time the body of the poor wretch that was sacrificed upon it. It would appear that the altar was hollow.
This room is filled with caskets and sarcophagi. As if sensing your presence, some of the occupants rise to meet you!
Opening this trap door, you find stairs leading further below in the sewers. Do you go down?
Men dressed in dark garments and masks are standing guard here. At your approach, they attack!

On this work desk, you find numerous paperwork, ledgers, etc. One of the letters catches you attention: "Dear Rhodin; I am pleased that you are receiving my alliance proposal favorably. Indeed, continued war between our oganizations would be pointless."

"I thank you for receiving this new delegation of the Red Claw, in order to further define the details of our soon-to-be alliance. Furthermore, as a token of my sincere intentions, they will be giving you a map, showing the entrance to our Guild."

"In hoping that these negociations prove useful and successful; Sincerely, (signed by) the Shadowsilk, Grand Dagger of the Red Claw, Cabale of Tanirith."  Appended to this letter, you find an interesting map.
Underneath this bed, you find a small coffer. Opening it reveals a small stash of loot, probably Rhodin's personal possessions.
You disturb some denizens of the sewers living here!

On this work desk, you find numerous notes, formulas, inventories, and the like. However, one letter catches your attention: "Dear Lord Zeghor; I am quite pleased by the progress you have made, although I never had any doubts of your capacity to do so."

"However, I would caution you not to proceed with haste in this; the people of Tanirith must succomb to horror and terror, thus weakening their resolve, but not be conquered by your creations. I hope that my additional monies will convince you of that."

"I look forward to your next progress report, as well as further word from our agents in Tanirith to this effect. Sincerely, (signed by): Ertham Zoh, Supreme Warlock of Sharranth, for his Dread and Sublime Majesty, the King and Warlord of Sharranth."
It would appear that Sharranth has a long arm indeed. Shuffling through the rest of the paperwork, you find sheets of parchment that could be of use to you.
Furfoot defenders on watch nod politely and let you pass.

There is a lot of coming and going through the gates of Upper Umaldyr. Indeed, merchants, travelers, sailors and all sort of people pass through the gates. You also notice numerous soldiers on watch at the battlements.
As usual, there is a lot of coming and going through the gates of Coral Towers.
Assassins are on guard here. "Why are you here?" One of them ask you. "We were not told to expect you ..." Shrugging, he lets you pass nonetheless.

Wererats are on guard here. As they raise their weapons to attack, you tell them that you have been sent by the Shadowsilk to meet with their leader. After a few nervous sniffs and grunts, they let you pass.
This is a dormitory, were numerous wererats are sleeping or taking a rest, some with their rodent "pets".
This large room is some sort of communal eating area. Numerous wererats are here.

You stumble upon numerous wererats standing guard in this rather well furnished room. As they raise their weapons to attack, you tell them that you have been sent by the Shadowsilk to meet with their leader. At that, they let you pass.

In this well furnished room, you see a huge wererat standing proud, staring at you angrily with his beedy, fiery eyes. You see him surrounded by other wererats. Looks like you have disturbed an important meeting here!
"Foolsss! Only the weak turnsss hisss back on hisss bettersss!" Adds Rhodin, before his wererats launch their attack!

A battered and bloody Rhodin chuckles as you stand prone in front of him. "Yessss. Ye are ssstrong after all. I know why ye've come here: go tell the Shadowsssilk that an alliance with sstrong peoples like hisss isss welcome."
With a firm nod, you leave.
Wererats on watch here block your way: "Our Lord Rhodin isss not expecting ye!" One of them stammers. "Ye be gone now!" With a shrug, you back away.

The Ratlord Rhodin chuckles as you stand tall before him. "Yessss. Ye are ssstrong after all. I know why ye've come here: go tell the Shadowsssilk that an alliance with sstrong peoples like hisss isss welcome."
A wererat on guard here nods to you, as he pulls a loose brick on the wall next to him.
The wererat then directs you to go to the west.
Assassins are on watch here. After scrutinizing you suspiciously, they let you pass.
Assassins on watch here attack the intruders that you are!
Assassins come to investigate what is all the fracas about!
This is a large dormitory. Numerous assassins are resting here.
One of them sounds the alarm upon your intrusion!
Upon your approach, one of the assassins pulls on a loose brick in the wall, revealing a secret passage. He then motions you to go into the passage.
This is a supply room. You manage to scrounge up interesting items for your own use.
Your less-than-conspicuous activities have attracted attention!
This is a small cell. Aside from the fact that it is damp and filthy, it is otherwise empty and its door is unlocked.

The door to this cell is locked. Looking through the door's barred window slit, you see a wretch of a man chained to the walls. From his tatered, stained clothes, and his dishiveled hair and beard, he must have been here for months.

As if having sensed you presence, the man looks up to see who is at the door. You then recognize him as being the councilor Nomune Ngallan. However, he doesn't recognize you one bit. "Please." He begs, his voice weak and strained.

"Let me go ... I will pay anything. I promise." He then breaks down in tears, utterly despaired. Leaving him to his fate, you then wonder who exactly is the Nomune Ngallan you met and spoke with in Tanirith ...

"Let me go ... I will pay anything. I promise." He then breaks down in tears, utterly despaired.  You are now wondering who exactly is the Nomune Ngallan you met and spoke with in Tanirith. Do you free this man?
Not wishing to be burdened, or bothered, you leave him to his fate.

"Thank you, good gents." Mumbles weakly Nomune as you unchain him. "Please, help me get to the Lord Paladine or Jarad Noll. They must be informed of my abduction!" Arming him with a dagger, you set yourselves to escort him safely to Jarad Noll.
Nomune Ngallan has joined your party; check out the Allies menu.
Lieutenants of the Guild are shacking up in this room. "What are ye doing here?" Demands one of them, angrily. Embarassed, you back away.
Lieutenants of the Guild are shacking up in this room. "What are ye doing here?" Demands one of them, angrily.  At that, he and his collegues advance to teach you a lesson in the respect of privacy!
Searching the place, you find a few interesting items.
This is the guild's armory. You find items of interest from its inventory.

This meeting room is lavishly furnished. Red Claw assassins are standing watch, as lieutenants sit at a large table of oak. All present are intent upon a non-descript man, who'se piercing eyes and commanding voice identify him as their Grand Dagger.

"Who dares disturb me?" The man asks of you, his voice calm yet cold. A shifty man sitting next to him whispers in his ears. "Well, well, well" The Grand Dagger muses, smiling menacingly. "The thorns in Storm's behind in the flesh and blood!"

"I am the Shadowsilk," he continues, "Grand Dagger of the Tanirith Cabale of the Red Claw. Tell me, so-called heroes: are you insane or simply fools?" He asks, obviously in derision. "Fools, no doubt." Answers the man sitting next to Shadowsilk.

"I be the Raven." The second man continues, smirking while bowing mockingly. "My Lord and Liege Anthraxus Storm shall be most pleased to hear news of your death!" At that, the Shadowsilk snaps his fingers, as his assassins make their move!
"Remember," you hear the Shadowsilk add to the Raven, "they will be killed by us, hence double the promised reward for their death!" The Raven nods silently in response.

"I suppose we'll have to do this ourselves, then!" Exclaims the Shadowsilk. Only then you notice his advisors standing next to him: a beautiful but obviously evil witch, and a priest of Kharalkuur, God of Death and Murder.

As the Raven joins the others while more master assassins and assassins join the fray, you wonder if Hurme, the God of Luck and Happenstance, has gone away on vacation ... or simply decided to leave you to your fate!
You notice a piece of paper protruding from the Raven's shirt.
You find the Red Claw's treasury!

"Who dares disturb me?" The man asks of you, his voice calm yet cold. A shifty man sitting next to him whispers in his ears. "Well, well, well." The Grand Dagger muses, smiling menacingly. "Storm's infamous new recruits, in the flesh and blood!"

"I am the Shadowsilk," he continues, "Grand Dagger of the Tanirith Cabale of the Red Claw. Tell me, so-called heroes: are you that good and powerful?" He asks, obviously in derision. "There is no doubt." Answers the man sitting next to Shadowsilk.

"I be the Raven." The second man continues, smirking while bowing mockingly. "My Lord and Liege Anthraxus Storm told me of your coming." At that, the Shadowsilk snaps his fingers: "Enough of platitudes! I have business to discuss with these recruits."

"I need you," the Shadowsilk goes on, looking at you, "to deliver an offer of alliance to a band of wererats. We have been at odds with them ever since we've moved to these new headquarters. Being quite territorial, they've perceived us as a threat."

"Although not very bright, these wererats have abilities which could be quite useful to the Red Claw. So, I charge you with this simple task. Do not return until you have succeeded." With another snap of his fingers, a lieutenant gives you a map.

"I be the Raven." The second man continues, smirking while bowing mockingly. "My Lord and Liege Anthraxus Storm told me of your coming." At that, the Shadowsilk snaps his fingers: "Enough of platitudes! I have business to discuss, so you begone!"

Just as you are about to leave, the Raven walks up to you: "I need you to bring this message to His Dread Majesty. Do so with haste." He hands you a letter, then goes back to sit at the table. Seeing the Shadowsilk begining to fume, you leave.
Not wishing to disturb the Shadowsilk and incur his ire, you back away.

The Shadowsilk is eating a sumptuous feast. "So? Did Rhodin accept?" He asks, annoyed. You nod. "Good!" He mumbles between sips of wine.  At a snap of his fingers, an assassin brings you a small chest. "Here's a little something for your troubles."
"Now begone from here, and we best never see your faces around our headquarters again! And I advise you to do the same concerning Rhodin's lair!" Waving you away, the Shadowsilk returns to his feast.
This is a lavishly furnished study and bedroom. This must be the Shadowsilk's private quarters.

You come upon a marble altar dedicated to Kharalkuur, God of Death and Murder. From the spots of caked and dried blood, you deduce that the Red Claw must have already performed a few human sacrifices to honor their dark God.
Do you demolish this unholy altar?
Your hacking and bashing cause the hollow altar to crumble in numerous pieces.
Suddenly, a cold wind arises from the desecrated altar, dust and pieces swirling about where it stood. It would appear that the God of Death and Murder did not appreciate your gesture!
You disturb the occupants of this place!
This is a large chest. Unfortunately, it is locked.

This ancient, slimy wall is adorned with bas-reliefs of wizards fighting armies and conquering kingdoms, alongside a sorceress which seems to lead them. You have no idea what all of this is for, nor why such art was carved into this wall so long ago.
At the base of the wall, you find that the eye of one of the wizard bas-reliefs is in fact a button that could be pushed. Do you press this button?

This ancient door is made of solid bronze and appears locked shut. You sense a strong magical aura about it. Numerous arcane symbols are etched in platinum and silver upon the door.  You can also make out copper-etched runes which you manage to decipher:
"HEREIN LIES DEATH AND DESTRUCTION. FINALLY IMPRISONED, IT CAN NO LONGER RAIN TERROR UPON US MORTALS. WOE TO YOU WHO WOULD BREAK IT FREE FROM THIS PRISON".
The demon summons other demons to his help!
The portal then opens by itself!
You hear a malevolent laughter coming from deep within the chamber revealed. Without anything further, the chamber's prisoner decides to vent his centuries of imprisonment on you!
You come upon a part of the sewers made up from the ruins of an ancient, older incarnation of Tanirith. Not surprisingly, what little of these ruins left are moldy and crumbling.

"WHO DARES DISTURB THE SLEEP OF ARCHONYA?" A deep, cavernous, netherwordly voice booms upon your entrance. You then notice a vaporous woman shape floating above the sarcophagus, her eyes burning with the light of anger, hate and evil.

On cue, the seemingly crusty statues suddenly come to life, shaking off their dust and grime, to reveal undead skeletal guardians. "LEAVE MY CRYPT NOW, OF PAY THE PRICE FOR YOUR FOLLY!" The spectre of Archonya intones. Do you leave?
You enter a dark crypt. In its center, a large stone sarcophagus stands, covered by centuries of dust, grime and cobwebs. Numerous statues stand guard along the walls of the silent chamber.
"SO BE IT, TOMB ROBBERS! TIME TO FACE YOUR DEATH!!!"
After the battle, you search the place and manage to scrounge up interesting valuables.
"FOOLS! DO YOU THINK I WOULD ALLOW TOMB ROBBERS LIKE YOU TO FIND MY RESTING PLACE AND LET YOU LIVE?"
Archonya summons ghostly revenants of her former apprentices.

You enter an ancient antechamber which appears to have been carved within the stones which now make its walls. More bas-reliefs of wizards are etched on the old walls, although they appear more life-size like.

Suddenly, ghostly apparitions come out from some of the bas-reliefs, silently floating to the center of the antechamber, and approaching to block your path. "NO ONE IS ALLOWED TO DISTURB THE SUPREMAR ARCHONYA!" One of the apparitions intones.
"WE, HER LOYAL WIZARDS, HAVE PLEDGED TO PROTECT HER EVEN IN THE AFTERLIFE!" At that, the ghosts move to attack!
This ruined place looks to have been a market place, many centuries ago. Unfortunately for you, it is now occupied by fearsome monsters!
You find the accumulated wealth of Khraash and his gang!
The large orc stands tall, surrounded by numerous brigands. "Me be Khraash," he intones, "an' me don't care who ye are, cuz ye'll pay fer yer intrusion in our place!" At that, he and his men attack!
More brigands join the fray!

A large orc is sitting at a table, in a meeting with his lieutenants. Of course, you have no doubt that this is Khraash, the orc Bandit Lord. Upon your entrance, numerous brigands already within this room charge at you, while Khraash moves to the side.
Khraash and the rest of his gang are banding together just to your left, now ready to face you.
Numerous brigands are here, either eating, talking, or taking a rest. One of them sees you and sounds the alarm!
The trap consists of a web of invisible silk threads strewn from wall to wall: passing through breaks the threads and activates the mechanism of the trap.
The trap is triggered!
Brigands are camping in this cavern!
You find a secret door into the back wall of the cavern. Opening it, you see that it leads to stairs which appear to go deep underground. Do you take the stairs?
You find yourselves in an ancient part of Tanirith's sewers. In fact, you estimate that you are in some lower level of the sewers.
These stairs appear to lead all the way back to the surface. Do you take these stairs?

You notice that the wall to the west is not really a wall, but rather a pile of rocks and boulders that have smoothed out over the centuries. Upon closer examination of this "wall", you feel a small draft coming from the other side.
Hacking away at the wall, the smoothed out rocks and boulders finally collapse, opening the way!
Your spell causes the smoothed out rocks and boulders to collapse, thus opening the way!
Bashing away at the wall with your weapons didn't even dent the smoothed out rocks and boulders. Not wishing to break your precious weapons, you try to find another solution.
You find a forgotten treasure cache!
Amidst the rubble here, you find large pieces of what was once rows upon rows of bookshelves. Carefully clearing the rubble, you find interesting books that have been miraculously preserved!
You see numerous homeless men, women and children shacking here. You are certain that you could rest here without being attacked.
One of the homeless has stolen some of your valuables while you were sleeping. As you wake up from his meddling about, the homeless person runs out of the room, too fast for you to catch him.
From the looks of it, this must have been a granary or food storage area. After centuries of rot and scavenger pilfering, it is no surprise that nothing edible remains.
The old headquarters of the Cult of Lankharah are abandoned, as it should be thanks to you.
This old dormitory is empty. You are certain that you could rest safely here.
From the looks of it, this must have been a granary or food storage area, up until a year ago.  After months of rot and scavenger pilfering, it is no surprise that nothing edible remains.
A wererat opens this trap door, revealing stairs going to a lower level of the sewers. He silently motions you to take the stairs.
You find a few interesting items in this slimy bookshelf, items which have somehow survived the centuries of dampness, fungus and grime.
The sign above the doors reads: "The Sailor's Wharf". Judging from the look of the building, mostly sailors and mariners must be patrons there.
These stairs appear to lead down in Tanirith's sewers. Do you go down?
The place is dimly lit and reeks of pipe smoke and alcohol. It is surprising that so many people frequent this place.

"Yup, Khraash." Mumbles the dwarf. "Ye see, this Bandit Lord wuz roamin' the Heartlands. But at the begining of the war, that orc-pig migrated over to the Eastern Lands, an' causing trouble ever since, o'course!"

"We ain't sure where he hides, but we know that some of his gang shack in the cavern shown on the map I'll be givin' ye. So, yer mission is simple: find Khraash, an' deal with him ... permanently! Or, if yer in a nice mood, bring him back alive."
"Now git outa here, an' don't ye come back to bother me unless ye've done that job!" Snarls the dour dwarf, in parting.

"Well, one of our sponsors -probably a durn mage, if ye ask me- needs this book fer something or another. We've no idea where the durn thing is, except that it wuz in Tanirith's library centuries ago.  Heh!"

"Now here's the joke: that library -and the durn book- got burried by the big earthquake of four hundred years ago. So, if the book still exists, then it's somewhere down deep in them sewers. Find the book, an' bring it back."

"Ah! The durn wererats! Well, them foul things have begun to infest Tanirith's sewers. The authorities are concerned, since some of them foul things have begun roamin' the streets at night, and attackin' folks an' all."
"So, ye have to go into the sewers, as deep as need be, find their lair and rid us of them. Usually, that's done by killin' every one of them, especially their lair leader!"

"Ah, yes. Them foul zombies and all. Well, them things have begun wanderin' the streets at night! We know that they come from the old southeast cemetary, near the Scholar Halls, but we've no idea who or what's behind them apparitions!"
"So, go to the southeast cemetary, find the cause behind the rise of them foul undead things, and rid us of this problem!"

"The Assassins' Guild, yup. Well, rumors abound that this guild, called the Red Claw, has set up shop in Tanirith. Of course, the authorities won't have that! But we don't know where them assassins are hidin'!"

"Some say their headquarters is inna house just south of the eastern-central piers, while others say that the Red Claw hides in them sewers. Me suggest to ye to investigate the house first: if there's nothin', then go walkabout in them sewers!"

"Either way, bring them assassin sons-of-orcs down! Preferably, terminate or apprehend their leader while yer at it, who's title is somethin' like 'Grand Dagger', or whatnot. Good luck, and good huntin'!"

"The continent of Anarym is a large land mass situated far east of here, across Ukkor's ocean. Not much is known of these lands, except fables and fabulations, or exaggerations borne out of ignorance."

"Some speak of Mage-Kings ruling over large empires out of floating magical fortresses, others of terrifying monsters prowling the lands everywhere, or yet others who tell of godly avatars warring with each other for the dominance of the continent."

"Umaldyr is an island-nation located some one thousand leagues east of here and is part of the continent of Anarym.  Sea trading between Tanirith and Umaldyr is now in its second year in the going, and many have sailed there to see the place."

"One must first know of the Lankharhans. This people established an empire some twelve thousand years ago on the continent of Anarym. This was a 'psionic' empire, since all Lankharhans were born with innate powers of the mind, or psionic powers."

"Also, the empire was a peaceful one, growing only through willfull adherance of other countries or cities to the empire. There came a time when powerful psionic individuals rose to become Lords, Regents, Princes and Emperors of the Empire."

"Those were aptly named 'Mentarchs', or 'Mind Lords', and they brought about a golden age for all citizens of the Empire. Indeed, their mind powers almost equalled those of gods, and they could live for centuries if not even more."

"Thus the Nine began wars of conquest not only against peoples apart of the Empire, but as well against their own, seeking to control all of the Lankharhan Empire without opposition. Those dark times became known as the 'War of the Mind Lords'."

"Indeed, as these Wars resulted in much suffering and death for the Lankharhans and even more so for non-psionics, powerful magic and magical weapons were devised to combat the Nine Mentarchs and their armies of psi-warriors."
"As I said, three Mentarchs were also instrumental against the Nine; the name of one still lives on to this day: Kith Khanaan."

"However, most of the Mind Lords became increasingly mentally unstable with time, and they began to lust for the utter domination of all non-psionics (whom they considered mongrels fit only to be slaves), even of all ordinary Lankharhans."

"In effect, the Mind Lords had become nothing short of evil, ruthless god-like monsters bent on conquest, enslavement and destruction; they even began warring among themselves. Indeed, three of them stood against the other evil-mad nine."

"But in time, thanks to the three Mentarchs who managed to rally lankharhans and non-lankharhans alike, these devastating Wars brought about the fall of the Nine. Unfortunately, the Wars caused the fall of the Lankharhan civilization as well."

"During the nine or so centuries since its foundation, Tanirith has undergone many changes and survived many disasters, both natural and man-made. Each time the city was rebuilt or expanded, it was done so on top of the previous buildings or structures."

"Hence, the sewers are the remains of buried streets, canals, and buildings from previous incarnations of Tanirith. Many of the homeless are living there, also numerous outlaws and renegades. It is rumored that much treasures are to be found there."

"However, such hoards are rumored to be guarded by  terrible monsters and fell creatures from the Abyss. Many secret places are also said to abound, such as ancient temples and crypts, which are most likely protected by magic and powerful guardians."

"In any case, everyone agree that the sewers are the domain of foul creatures, such as giant rats and sewer beasts. Now, the most known entrance to the sewers is to be found underneath the Memorial Statue in Tanirith's city park."

"But I know for a fact that many entrances can be found around the battlements, outside of the city. One last thing: should you venture into the sewers, you best be good at mapping, for the sewers are a veritable labyrinth with more than one level."

"And thus ended the Lankharh Empire after two millennia of existence. Interestingly, the reclusive people of Anarym known as the Keryndorhyans are said to be direct descendants of the Lankharhans; but the existence of this people is itself debatable."

"We know that until six years ago, Umaldyr was a truly unified, two-island nation. But the northern island was ravaged by goblin hordes, and the chaos this caused encouraged ambitious Lords and Barons to become independent and seceed from the crown."

"Thus, although the crown-capital Umaldyr still stands, only petty baronies remain of the 'island-nation' along with bandit or goblin kingdoms. Most of our trading is with Umaldyr, although some trade agreements are being negociated with other baronies."

"I would however point out that what we know of Umaldyr so far still remains somewhat sketchy, while we have yet to learn more about Anarym itself. But I am confident that in a few years, our ignorance of this 'new' continent will have disappeared."

Snatching away your voucher, the old grumbling dwarf goes into a fit: "Ye durn fools! Then why did ye come here an' bother me fer? Whot do me look like: a durn librarian?" You make haste in getting out of here, as the dwarf goes on ranting.
The fight breaks into an all out brawl!!!

A bunch of somber, tough-looking, and cocky sailors are sitting here. One of them, a huge and brawny man, rises up to you: "Whot do ye want, ye bums?" He asks menacingly, his hand already on the pommel of his weapon.
The sign above this door reads: "Maroon's Eating Halls".
The place is filled with people.

The secret door that used to lead to the sewers has been replaced by a real wall. Perhaps Maroon didn't want to be threatened or blackmailed again into allowing unsavory characters to use this secret entrance to the sewers.
This is a kitchen. You see many cooks and wenches busy at making the meals and preparing the drinks. One of the wenches sees you, and ushers you out politely.

You come upon a large half-ogre dressed in a chef's outfit. From the food stains on the garment, this must be one of the cooks of the place. You notice that he keeps grinning with satisfaction while speaking with any patron he sees.
"Greetings!" The half-ogre exclaims at your approach. "Me Maroon, and welcome to me Eating Halls! Me have ta best food in all Tanirith! Ye want to see me menu?"
"What would ye like?"
"Good choice! Who'll pay?"
"One of me wenches will seat ye and yer meals with refreshments will be coming! Enjoy!"
Once seated, you do not wait long for your food and beverages. And what a feast you have: the meal is plenty and delicious, and the drinks are more than enough!
"This serving costs 90 golds total per party!"
"This serving costs 150 golds total per party!"
"This serving costs 180 golds total per party!"
"Well, ye don't have enough gold ... another time, mayhaps?"   At that, you leave to make way for other patrons that are waiting in line behind you.
"Now, that IS proper cuisine for royalty!" Exclaims Jorale, between bites of her meal and a sip of her drink.
"Thish ish shucculent!" Exclaims Riel, his mouth full. "I knew I wash doing the rightsh thshing when I dshoined yon merry bandsh!" He adds with a wink, before taking a sip of his drink.
"Moradin be praised!" Exclaims Braggan, clapping his hands while eyeing his dish with greedy eyes. "This truly be a feast fit fer me weary bones!" Without further ado, he digs in with gusto.
"Truly a dish perfect for the cultured and delicate palate." Muses Leira between bites of her meal and sips of her drink.
As usual, Maroon the half-ogre is at his post, grinning with satisfaction while speaking with any patron he sees, oblivious of the food stains all over his apron.
"Welcome back, good Heroes!" Maroon booms upon seeing you, opening is huge arms wide. "Welcome back to me Eating Halls! Me still have ta best food in all Tanirith, ye know! Ye want to see me menu?"
"Welcome back to me Eating Halls!" Maroon booms upon seeing you, all smiles. "Ye want to see me menu? Only looking at it will make yer mouths water, me tell ye!"
"I feel quite fortunate," muses Denard between bites and sips of his drink, "for it is not often that one has the means to sample Maroon's highly acclaimed cuisine!"
"Bah!" Exclaims Braggan in disgust, as he is wiping his axe clean of blood.  He then winks at you: "Foul creatures, me tell ye! They don't even taste good! Make me belly hurt!"
"Praise be Thask!" Exclaims Ellai, while wiping his weapon clean. "Now, that was a testing battle!" He adds with satisfaction.
"Clanggedin Silverbeard must be smiling today!" Exclaims Braggan, grinning while wiping his axe clean. "This be a durn good brawl we've just had!" He adds with a wink.
"Justice is served." Denard intones with finality, as he wipes his weapon clean.
Under the repeated bashing, the altar easily breaks up in pieces, consuming at the same time the body of the poor wretch that was sacrificed upon it. It would appear that the altar was hollow.
"Are you insane?" Denard exclaims, outraged by your choice of action. "This evil thing must be destroyed!" With out another word, Denard grabs his weapon to have it at the altar!

"This is wrong, my comrades!" Exclaims Athos, who is usually serene and calm. "This altar must be destroyed; otherwise, its evil influences will persist and expand!" At that, he begins to bash at the altar.

"This is wrong, my comrades!" Exclaims Leira, who is usually calm and aloof. "This altar must be destroyed; otherwise, its evil influences will persist and expand!" At that, she begins to bash at the altar.

"By Moradin! Have ye become as dumb as an orc's behind?" Exclaims Braggan, quite agitated by your decision. "This foul thing must be destoryed, me tell ye!"  At that, the dwarven kingson begins to bash at the altar.

"Something's not right with this here wall." Mumbles Braggan, who is scrutinizing the wall next to you while stroking his long beard. "Me tell ye that this wall can move, or me is a sonofanorc!" Intrigued, you take a closer look at this wall.
"What is wrong with you?" Asks Denard, obviously disturbed by your choice. Without a word, he frees the man from his chains.

"It is obvious that this man must be helped, for I suspect he holds the key to some of the mysterious problems besieging Tanirith!"  Exclaims Athos, obviously disturbed by your choice. Without a word, he frees the man from his chains.
"What is wrong with you?" Asks Belrion, obviously disturbed by your choice. Without a word, he frees the man from his chains.
"What is wrong with you?" Asks Jorale, obviously disturbed by your choice. Without a word, she frees the man from his chains.
"That'll teach those miscreants!" Belrion mutters grimly. "Good riddance to foul company!"
The catapult finally gives under the hacking and bashing, crashing to numerous pieces in a cloud of splinters, nails and dust!
The body of a woman is lying here. It looks as if it was being prepared to be revived as a zombie.

A middle-aged man is chained to this table. Although bruised and cut, he doesn't seem the worse for wear. "Ah! Rescuers, mayhaps?" He asks, with a mischevious gleam in his eyes. "I am Athos, humble monk of Astrane, Goddess of the Moons and the Stars."

"I had taken it upon myself to discover what was responsible for the awakening of the dead, but, as you can see, I have not been entirely successful. Umm, would you mind?" He adds, raising his chained wrists. You immediately free him.

"Thank you, good gents!" Athos replies, while massaging his bruised wrists. "Well, how about we join forces? I could tell you what I have learned so far." He intones, with a wink. Do you accept Athos in your party?

"Very well, then." Athos replies with a sigh. "I guess I better fetch some healing services, which I sorely need, before coming back here to take care of this undead business." He adds to himself, while picking up his gear.
"Well, then, I bid you safe journeys and safer returns!" Athos exclaims, before limping back out of the place.

"Praise the Moonsister!" Athos exclaims as he picks up his gear to join you. "Well, I have found out that those responsible are a group of necrowizards under the leadership of a very powerful one, named Zeghor. Their main quarters are in a lower level."

"There is a secret door at the south wall of this lab that opens to a secret passage that in turn will lead us to stairs to the west: these stairs will take us to the den of these worshipers of Orcas!"
Athos has joined your party; check out the Allies menu.

You find Athos sitting at this table, engaged in discussion with a beautiful woman. "Why, you are back!" He exclaims with surprise, glad to see you. He then truns back to the woman: "Well, my dear, as much as I enjoyed this talk with you, I must now go."
Gathering his gear, Athos rejoins you.
This is the Hall of Justice. You see many militia patrols going in and out of the huge building; occasionally, a patrol brings in some captured misfits or criminals.
This is the Hall of Justice. It is closed at this time.
Guards block you way. "This area's restricted: no unauthorized folks may come here!"
The sign on this building reads: "Harbor Master-East Port". It appears to be closed at this time.
The sign on this building reads: "Harbor Master-East Port". Many sailors, ship captains, travelers and merchants go in and out of the place. Do you enter?
"Thank you. Go to the East Port, the very last pier to the south. Your boat is anchored at the end of this pier. Have a good sail."
After waiting for about an hour (many merchants and mariners were waiting for their turn before you arrived), a lady makes you fill out forms.
"Boat rental is 30000 golds payable with 300 gems, time unlimited, along with Captain and crew." She intones. "Who will pay?"
You walk up to a kiosk with the sign: "Ship Rentals". Do you want to wait in line to rent your own boat?

Looking over your filled forms, the lady frowns: "I'm sorry, but according to our files, you have already rented a boat from Tanirith's Port Authorities. We do not rent a second time if the boat has not been returned to us first." Embarassed, you leave.

"Greetings!" A stout man chimes, as he walks up to you. "I'm Suhl Teros, Captain of ta Tsunami, ta ship ye have rented. We're ready to set sail and waitin' for ye!"  He then turns and boards his ship, shouting orders to prepare for setting sail.
The Captain then boards his ship, shouting orders to leave anchor and prepare to sail out.  You figure you should board the ship as well, lest it leaves without you!
The lady smiles behind the kiosk smiles warmly: "Greetings. Which is the destination of your choice?"
You walk to a kiosk with a sign bearing the words "Boat Fares and Tickets". Do you wish to buy a ticket to sail to another city?
"Fare to Wailsrond? That will be 150 gold pieces payable in coins. Who will pay?"
"Thank you. Go to the westside of South Port, the very last pier to the south. Your boat is anchored at the end of this pier. Have a good sail."

As you walk up to the boat, a sailor stops you: "Have you a ticket? This caravelle leaves soon."  After handing your tickets to him, you are escorted to your cabin: "The ship leaves in about five minutes and the trip will last eight hours."
Indeed, the ship leaves soon after you are settled in your cabin.  After an uneventful trip, you finally disembark at your destination.
While it took more time before leaving, the ship finally sails out.  After an uneventful trip (aside from high waves which were unsettling), you finally disembark at your destination.

As the ship leaves, you notice dark clouds looming.  Sure enough, a thunder storm rages throughout the trip, with high winds and rocky waters!  Nonetheless, you arrive safely at your destination, thanks to an expert captain!
"Fare to Lantharond? That will be 150 gold pieces payable in coins. Who will pay?"

As you walk up to the boat, a sailor stops you: "Have you a ticket? This caravelle leaves soon."  After handing your tickets to him, you are escorted to your cabin: "The ship leaves in about five minutes and the trip will last about a day."
"Fare to Coral Towers? That will be 1500 gold pieces payable in gems, so 15 gems. Who will pay?"

As you walk up to the boat, a sailor stops you: "Have you a ticket? This caravelle leaves soon."  After handing your tickets to him, you are escorted to your cabin: "The ship leaves in about five minutes and the trip will last about a sevenday."
"Fare to Umaldyr? That will be 3000 gold pieces payable in gems, so 30 gems. Who will pay?"

As you walk up to the boat, a sailor stops you: "Have you a ticket? This caravelle leaves soon."  After handing your tickets to him, you are escorted to your cabin: "The ship leaves in about five minutes and the trip will last about two sevendays."

A sign hanging above this kiosk reads: "Port Working, Shipping, and Custom Permits". Numerous sailors, captains and merchants are standing in line here. Since you are not into sea trading nor looking for a job at the Port or on a boat, you leave.
The sign on this building reads: "Harbor Master-South (Eastside and Westside) Port". It appears to be closed at this time.
The sign on this building reads: "Harbor Master-South (Eastside and Westside) Port". Many sailors, ship captains, travelers and merchants go in and out of the place. Do you enter?
A sign above the door of this building reads: "Harbor Master -Lantharond Port".  It appears to be closed at this time.
A sign above the door of this building reads: "Harbor Master -Lantharond Port".  Do you enter?

After waiting for about an hour (many merchants and mariners were waiting for their turn before you arrived), a lady answers you: "Sorry, but we have no boats to rent at this time." Somewhat frustrated, you walk away.
"Thank you. Go to the Port, at the very last pier to the south. Your boat is anchored at the end of this pier. Have a good sail."
"Fare to Tanirith? That will be 150 gold pieces payable in coins. Who will pay?"
The sign on this building reads: "Harbor Master".  Many sailors, ship captains, travelers, and merchants go in and out of the building.  Do you enter?
The sign on this building reads: "Harbor Master".  The building appears closed at this time.
"Thank you. Go to the Port, at the very last pier to your left. Your boat is anchored there. Have a good sail."
This is the Harbor Master building of Coral Towers. The place is filled with people. Do you go in?
This is the Harbor Master building of Coral Towers. The place is closed.
"Fare to Wailsrond? That will be 1500 gold pieces payable in gems, so 15 gems total. Who will pay?"
"Thank you. Go to the Port, at the very last pier to your right. Your boat is anchored there. Have a good sail."
"Fare to Tanirith? That will be 1500 gold pieces payable in gems, so 15 gems total. Who will pay?"
"Fare to Sharranth? That will be 3000 gold pieces payable in gems, so 30 gems total. Who will pay?"
"Fare to Umaldyr? That will be 5000 gold pieces payable in gems, so 50 gems total. Who will pay?"

As you walk up to the boat, a sailor stops you: "Have you a ticket? This caravelle leaves soon."  After handing your tickets to him, you are escorted to your cabin: "The ship leaves in about five minutes and the trip will last about three sevendays."
This is the Harbor Master building of Sharranth. The place is closed.
This is the Harbor Master building of Sharranth. The place is filled with people. Do you go in?
"Fare to Coral Towers? That will be 3000 gold pieces payable in gems, so 30 gems total. Who will pay?"
"Thank you. Go to the port outside of the city, to the south of here. Your boat is on the first pier to your right. Have a good sail."
"Fare to Tanirith? That will be 500 gold pieces payable in gems, so 5 gems total. Who will pay?"
This worn out sign reads: "Koralya". It also points to the north for Ashkor.
This worn out sign points to the north for Ashkor and to the west for Koralya.
This worn out sign points to the north for Ashkor and Koralya.
The city gates of Aurelyan are heavily guarded, with numerous soldiers standing watch on the battlements. Aside from fishermen and pier workers, not many people pass through the gates.
This is the Harbor Master building of Upper Umaldyr. The place is filled with people. Do you go in?
This is the Harbor Master building of Upper Umaldyr. The place is closed at this time.
"Thank you. Go to the West Harbor, the third pier from your left. Your boat is anchored at the end of this pier. Have a good sail."

There is a lot of coming and going through the gates of Umaldyr. Indeed, merchants, travelers, sailors and all sort of people pass through the gates. You also notice numerous soldiers on watch at the battlements.

Panting and tired after this clash, you dash through the door before more reinforcements come in.

Mercenary guards nod politely and let you enter the mansion. From within, you hear music and numerous people talking and laughing. Looks like a nice soiree is happening there!
Servants open the door for you.

As minstrels are playing beautiful music, numerous people are attending this soiree. Many lords and ladies, among which you recognize councilors and councilwomen, are eating, drinking, dancing and enjoying themselves.
Among them, you spot lady Shalla Thrall, dressed in a flowing satin red dress and wearing sparkling jewelry, socializing with her guests and apparently enjoying herself as well.

One of the mansion's servants is standing next to you: "Would ye like me to take care of your cloaks for ye, lords and ladies?" Shaking your head in response, you go back to the ball room to mingle.
As you are about to open this door, a servant of the mansion stops you: "Me apologies, lords and ladies, but these be private quarters." Embarassed, you walk away.
Mansion servants stand behind this table covered with enough food to feed a large village or more. You see roasted phesants, grilled boars, various seafoods, vegetables, fruits and desserts.

By the aroma and the stylish, if not exquisite, presentations of the plates, you wonder if lady Thrall's cook is not in fact a grand chef! As one servant is handing out plates containing samples of everything to other guests, another is serving you.
"Wine and other drinks are served at the other table, lords and ladies." He tells you, after giving you your plates and bowing politely.

Mansion servants stand behind this table covered with enough wine and beverages to sate a large village or more. You see Tanirith wine, rare wines (like from Waterford), as well as rhums and ales from various parts of the Realmz.

Lady Thrall sure knows how to entertain, indeed! As one servant is handing out goblets to guests, another one asks what you would like. After giving him your choices, he hands you large goblets filled to the rim of what you asked him.
"Food and desserts are served at the other table, lords and ladies." He tells you, after giving you your goblets and bowing politely.

The minstrels are playing lively music at the guests' delight. From their garments, you guess that they are actually part of lady Thrall's retinue. The lady must be rich indeed to be able to retain such services on a permanent basis.
Do you want to try to pick the lock, even if the odds are you'll be caught in the act while doing so?
Your fiddling about attracts the attention of one of the mansion's servants. "Sorry, lords and ladies, but this be private quarters." He intones. Embarrased, you leave.

A militia patrol finally arrives. "What has happened here?" The captain asks.  As lady Thrall and her guests explain what you have done, he nods: "No worries, me lady." He then turns to you: "All right! You are under arrest! Off to the magistrate!"

The guests are appalled by what you just did! Immediately, mercenary guards rush in to surround you.  "How dare you?" Lady Thrall demands angrily. "I invite you to my home, and you try to vandalize it? The Lord Paladine will hear of this, I assure you!"

"Call the militia!" She then orders to one of her servants, before turning her angry stare back at you: "I knew you were nothing but uncivilized, opportunistic criminals! Well, you are going to jail for this, and I hope you rot there!" She snarls.

A servant has seen what you did and sounds the alarm! Immediately, mercenary guards rush in to surround you.  "How dare you?" Lady Thrall demands angrily. "I invite you to my home, and you try to steal from me? The Lord Paladine will hear of this!"

You approach Lady Shalla Thrall as she is conversing with some of her guests. Upon seeing you, she nods politely: "Welcome." She greets you amicably. "I am glad that you could come. I hope you are enjoying yourselves?" You nod, smiling. What do you say?
"You are no bother at all." Lady Shalla replies, smiling. "We'll speak again later then." With a respectful nod, you move on.
After giving your polite regards to Lady Shalla Thrall and thanking her for a delightful soiree, you take your leave.

Lady Shalla nods, a bit of sadness in her eyes: "Yes. I was always rebellious and hard-headed in my youth, often disagreeing with my late father's visions concerning trade, life in Tanirith, and his way of going about his affairs."

"So, upon reaching the age of maturity, I left home to seek my own fortunes." She then chuckles. "Of course, I had to go as far away as I could from home, so I ended up in Specularn, on the northwestern frontiers of the Realmz continent!"

"I worked for about five years as an apprentice trader sponsored by a baron there ... 'Vlad' was his name, I believe. A horrible, harsh and narrow-minded fellow." Shalla shrugs at that. "In any case, I left his sponsorship to establish my own company."

"Of course, a few years after that came the giant wars. But thanks to adventurers like you, Specularn was spared from catastrophe. However, numerous merchants had left the city as the giants had begun their troubles. But I stayed ... and profited!"

She then laughs: "Of course I did, since I was the only trader brave enough -or foolish enough- to stay as Specularn faced grave dangers!" She then sighs. "Well, after that, my fortune only grew as the years passed."

"I had kept in touch with my late father all along. So when I heard of what happened almost a year ago, as well as of his treason, I felt compelled to sell everything and come back here, to manage what he had left behind ... and restore our good name."

Lady Shalla frowns: "Well, from what I have come to know about the Warlord of Sharranth, I must say that I am not surprised by this push of conquest on his part. Of course, I do not approve of war one bit, especially to build an empire by force."

"Although I don't always agree with the foreign policies of our esteemed Lord Paladine and that of my colleague Lord Noll, I do agree with the fact that we should honor our alliance treaty with Wailsrond and help the besieged city."

She chuckles. "After all, it doesn't sit well with anyone when a partner renegs on his deals or promises, no? Of course, if we didn't have an alliance with Wailsrond, then I would be siding with those who feel that others' problems are not our concerns."
You overhear a piece of conversation between guests:

"I am telling you," a woman says, "councilor Nomune Ngallan is such a charming and intelligent man!"  Another woman nods: "Yes! He's so persuasive, I do believe he could convince anyone of doing anything! What a dream!" Both giggle at that.

"I hear that Lady Shalla is still in mourning of her late father." A man muses.  "Well," another man adds, "daugthers are often quicker to forgive their fathers' sins, no?" A third man whispers: "Or maybe because she approved of those 'sins'?"

"Have ye heard this one?" A woman asks of two others. "Gossip has it that Queen Aramina of Lantharond has taken a lover over King Vallar, ever since he was stricken by that strange sickness of his!" She shakes her head in disaproval.

"Have ye heard?" A man asks of two others. "The Warlord of Sharranth has appointed a Herzog to the Heartlands, who rules by his writ from Aranys, of all places!" One of the other men nods: "Aye. From Aranys now, from Tanirith later?"

"I heard that Umaldyr is not an island-nation at all, at least not anymore!" A man intones. "Aye" a second one replies. "They were swarmed by raging goblin hordes, and the battered nation has split up into numerous baronies and all, as a result."

Lady Shalla shakes her head slowly: "No. But this situation worries me much. When things are such that even treaty obligations have become a matter of prolonged debates and arguments, any fool would see that there is trouble underlying all of it."

She then sighs: "Any fool would see, except those that are arguing for no reason. I wish I knew why this is so; perhaps I could try to correct the situation. But I feel I am alone in seeing this state of affairs, and powerless to do anything about it."

Showing her the burned letter you found in the abandoned house, you ask her if she would have any idea why it ended up in this place. Frowning, Lady Shalla shakes her head slowly: "I recognize my writting, and I think I know what this letter was."

"I wrote it for Lord Hardin, a merchant of Tanirith. He and my late father had been in negociations prior to his demise; when I came back and took over my late father's business, I wrote to Lord Hardin weeks ago in order to complete the negociations."

"However, I never got a response from him, nor did I get any news from the courier whom I had charged with the letter. But last week, I met Lord Hardin at another soiree and found out he had never received my letter -this letter- in the first place."

"We both concluded that my courier had been mugged or something dreadful like that. In any event, we did continue the negociations and successfully at that. But now, your showing of this letter confirms to me that it was somehow 'intercepted', sadly."

"How dare you?!?" Shalla shouts, angered by your accusation. Smiling grimly, you show her the burned letter you found in the abandoned assassins' house. "I don't care about your fabricated proof!" She shouts back. "I know what you're trying to do here!"

"You are trying to discredit me in front of my guests and my collegues! Did Jarad Noll put you up to that? I am certain of it! He just wants to acquire my late father's -and now my- holdings! My father may have been a traitor, but I am NOT!"

"Now get out of here, you louses!" She spits, pointing to the door, as guests look on to you with scowls of disaproval. You are then seized by servants and mercenary guards, and promptly escorted out.
You wonder if you did not make a monumental mistake.
"Noll and the Lord Paladine will hear of this, I swear!" Shalla adds angrily, as you are taken out. "There will be Abyss to be paid!" The mumblings of the guests show approval of her words.

As a servant opens this door for you, you see Councilor Ngallan sitting at a dinner table, enjoying a bottle of wine or two with a few of his friends and associates. Upon seeing you, he smiles and motions you to the table.

What do you reply?
"You are no bother at all." Lord Ngallan replies, smiling. "We'll speak again later then." With a respectful nod, you rise from your seats and leave.

"Welcome, back!" Nomune greets you, as goblets of wine are served. "I am glad that you could honor me again with your visit!" You nod, smiling, as servants show you to comfortable seats at the table. "So, how may I be of service?" The councilor asks.

Lord Ngallan frowns: "From what I have come to know about the Warlord of Sharranth, I must say that I am not surprised by this push of conquest on his part. Of course, I do not approve of war one bit, especially when used to build an empire by force."

He chuckles. "After all, it doesn't sit well with anyone when a partner renegs on his deals or promises, no? Of course, if we didn't have an alliance with Wailsrond, then I would be siding with those who feel that we should help our neighbors anyway."

Lord Ngallan chuckles: "All of this situation does not worry me much. Politics are a matter of prolonged debates and arguments, and any fool would see that such things do not mean that there is any underlying trouble."

He then sighs: "Any fool would see, except those that disapprove open debating.  As much as I respect the Lord Paladine and Jarad Noll, and as much as I agree often with them, I am afraid that I count them among those who seem to resent open debates."

Lord Ngallan nods: "Yes. I'm always seeking to expand my business ties, and looking for new markets as well. After the demon problems in the Westmore City area, I felt the region was ripe for a new company to go in and seize the vacant opportunities."

He then winks. "You see, numerous merchants and traders had fled from Westmore City and the region, during the demon troubles. So, a whole new market was open for me -practically- to make my own!" He laughs ruefully at that.
"But I wanted to be sure that it all worked out in my favor, so I decided to forego my usual dealers and journeyed to Westmore City to make the deals myself. And it paid off, big!"

"After a one-year stay there, I felt confident that this branching organization of my trading company was settled enough to be run by a merchant of my choosing, and so I finally returned to my home here in Tanirith."

"So! Storm has an agenda of his own after all!" Snarls Nomune. At the same time, his features begin to haze and distort, settling to that of a middle-aged man dressed in white robes, his eyes alit with an eery green glow.

There is no doubt now that you are facing an Overlord. "I am Taroth Sark, Seventh Speaker of the Inner Council." He intones menacingly. "Well done, fools. However, the end-game is not upon me quite yet!"

With a snap of his fingers, Taroth's 'friends'  change shape to that of strange knights, as numerous warriors appear to surround you. "Deal with them!" Taroth Sark snarls, as he dashes away through the door to the northeast.

After the battle, a short-lived chaos erupts as servants and drudges rush outside of the mansion in a fit of panic. Trying not to pay attention to any of this, you set yourselves to find Taroth Sark, wherever he may be hiding within the mansion.

Nomune nods with a wink: "Yes, so I have heard. Well, as you may now know, I am the secret 'liaison' to Anthraxus Storm's Royal spy, a shifty man called 'The Raven'. He is a guest of the Assassins' Guild, which is headquartered in the sewers."

"In any event, you'll understand I hope if I ask you not to reveal my -ah- true role in this war, especially to officials in Tanirith?" You nod in response to reassure him. "Splendid! I am looking forward to work closely with you then!" He adds, smiling.

A bit surprised, 'Nomune' then regains his composure: "Well, this is interesting. I take it, then, that you saw the real councilor back in the Assassins' Guild?" You nod, looking at him square in his eyes. "Quite interesting indeed." He answers back.

"Well, it doesn't really matter who I am really, no? After all, I do act as secret 'liaison' to Anthraxus Storm's Royal spy, a shifty man called 'The Raven'. And have I not been quite useful so far? Of course I have." He then takes a sip of his wine.

"Let's just say that I am a very interested party in Anthraxus Storm's plans, that I have no wishes other than his successful conquest of the Sword Lands, and that I work for the Overlords, and leave it at that." You nod, somewhat satisfied by this.

"So! You have managed to stumble upon the truth!" Snarls Nomune. At the same time, his features begin to haze and distort, settling to that of a middle-aged man dressed in white robes, his eyes alit with an eerie green glow.

"Really? Can I see it?" Nomune replies. After handing him the burned letter, he studies it long and hard. "My word!" He then whispers, both shocked and dismayed. "I would have never thought it possible, although I did have my suspicions." He sighs.

"Well, this letter proves it. It would appear that councilor Thrall has followed her father's footsteps and has allied herself with the enemy. Why else write a letter which, although hardly legible, hints at renewing alliances and such?"

He pauses. "And it's all about her late father's work with 'them' and her wish to continue this relationship. With the fact that this letter was found in a house formerly owned by assassins, well ..." He shakes his head in sadness.
