As you enter this study, you see numerous psi-warriors standing watch for your arrival. Behind them, Taroth Sark is standing in front one of those communications globes you have come to know well, apparently speaking with another Overlord.
"They are here!" Taroth Sark snarls to the globe, upon your entrance. Turning to face you with a look of pure hatred, he then motions silently to his psi-warriors to go forth and attack!

You hear Taroth Sark moan, as he lays on the ground, nearing death: "You have won this round." He whispers through clenched teeth, coughing blood all the while. "But you won't stop us!" Turning a strange ring on his left middle finger, he then vanishes!

As you enter this study, you see numerous psi-warriors standing watch for your arrival. Behind them, Taroth Sark is standing in front strange glowing globe, apparently speaking to someone else through this device.
You notice a fake book in one of the shelves of this library. It appears to be tied to a string mechanism of some sort. Do you pull on this fake book?
The library slides to the right, revealing a hole in the floor! Looking in the hole, you retrieve a small coffer: looks like you have found Taroth Sark's secret treasure stash!

However, his features remind you nonetheless of the Overlord you spoke to after defeating the three Overlords in the temple of Graaz'z, nearly a year ago. "So, we meet again." The man intones, his voice as cold as steel, confirming your guess.

As you stand in front of this communication globe, you see the face of someone within, attempting to "see" what is about in the room. You have difficulty making out the details of this man, as the image within the globe is all blurry and distorted.

"Let me introduce myself formally." He continues, bowing his head in mocked respect. "I am Primus, High Praetor and First Speaker of the Inner Council, which I have founded. I salute you for your valiant efforts; Taroth Sark is not an easy man to best."

Primus then chuckles. "Sadly for you, Master Sark will recover from his critical wounds, having just teleported back to our sanctum sanctorum; I can assure you now that he will wish fervently for a rematch with you all, if only to regain his dignity."

Primus then sighs. "It is unfortunate that we did not have enough teleportation rings to give to our late General Qui, as well as to Commanders Enol and Vezzir. Perhaps they'd be with us still if they had such rings, after you defeated them last year."

"Well, no matter: let's return to the actual business at hand. I chose to grace you with my presence in order to give you a final warning: stay out of our affairs. In any case, no matter what you manage to achieve against us, you will lose in the end."

"Of that, I can assure you. It is simply a matter of inevitability, especially since you can't even fathom the depths of our many-faceted goals.  Thus, I enjoin you to abandon your foolish and futile quest to defeat us. And to encourage you to do so ..."
The communication globe suddenly explodes into thousands of flying, deadly shards!

"Even as allies to Anthraxus Storm, whom evidently has an agenda of his own which goes against ours. But we are not surprised by Storm's treason; in fact, we expected it. What we did not expect was for people like you to actually side with him."

Primus chuckles again. "It would seem that desperation calls for desperate measures, eh? Well, all of this matters none. As I said, whatever you contrive, by your own or alongside the Warlord of Sharranth, will fail miserably to prevent us from winning."

As you stand in front of this floating globe, you see the face of someone within, attempting to "see" what is about in the room. You have difficulty making out the details of this man, as the image within the globe is all blurry and distorted.

"Who are you?" The man demands, his voice as cold as steel. "No matter." He intones, before you can answer. "It would appear that dispatching those Heroes of the Sword Lands months ago, in retaliation for their meddling in our affairs, was not enough."

The man chuckles at your shocked reaction upon hearing that the remaining Overlords managed to kill the Heroes that saved the Sword Lands last year. "Yes, we did." The man muses. "But that did not discourage other fools to follow in their footsteps."

Primus then sighs. "It is unfortunate that we did not have enough teleportation rings to give to our late General Qui, as well as to Commanders Enol and Vezzir. Perhaps they'd be with us still if they had such rings, after they were defeated last year."

Among various empty sheets of parchment, you find on this desk a draft version of a letter. Although scribbled with haste, you manage to read most of its contents: "To the Raven; All is well as planned in the High Council, with dissention ever growing."

"Thanks to my skills and glib tongue, more and more councilors are being confused and unwittingly maneuvered to do our bidding by debating incessantly every decision put to the floor of the High Council. I can now declare this body neutralized."

"I am however worried still concerning those adventurers enlisted by the Lord Paladine. Is your Warlord doing anything about this? And if so, what? I would appreciate being kept in the loop about that." The letter ends and this point.

"How is your progress?" The Lord Paladine asks, being obviously worried. He then gapes in surprised at seeing Nomune Ngallan besides you, his clothes dirty and in tatters. "What is the meaning of this?" The Lord demands, eyeing each of you sternly.

"Lord Paladine." Nomune intones, stepping forward. "Do not blame these noble gents for my current state. Quite the contrary in fact, for they have delivered me from bondage at the hands of an illicit guild of assassins underneath our fair city!"

You then proceed to tell the Lord Paladine under what circumstances you found councilor Ngallan."By Tyr!" The Lord exclaims. "For how long have you been prisoner of these criminals, Lord Ngallan?" Nomune shrugs and shakes his head, at a loss.

"Then I suggest," the Lord Paladine continues, "that you all go speak with Lord Noll. I've given him carte blanche to rid us of traitors in our city: he'll tell you what to do next, and take good care of Lord Ngallan." With a nod, you get on your way.

You even show him the letter you found on the sharranthine spy master: "A plot to assassinate me?" The Lord Paladine exclaims, after reading the letter. "Assassins in my castle already?" He adds, shocked by this revelation.

At the Lord Paladine's words, some of the servants of the castle shed their disguises and draw their weapons, seeking to kill the Lord! Shoving Nomune Ngallan to the Lord Paladine's side, you position yourselves to meet the assassins!
Castle guards rush in to give you a helping hand!

"I can't believe this!" Mutters the Lord Paladine, after the clash. "How could these murderers have infiltrated my castle so easily?" Nomune Ngallan steps forward: "I believe that each and everyone of these 'servants' came with false recommandations."
"Probably," Nomune adds, ashamed, "from the one who has been impersonating me all along." The Lord Paladine nods in agreement, putting a reassuring hand on the dejected councilor.
"How is your progress?" The Lord Paladine asks, being obviously worried. With much urgency, you proceed to tell him how you have uncovered a plot to assassinate him.

At the Lord Paladine's words, some of the servants of the castle shed their disguises and draw their weapons, seeking to kill the Lord! Without a thought, you position yourselves to meet the assassins!
"I can't believe this!" Mutters the Lord Paladine, after the clash. "How could these murderers have infiltrated my castle so easily? I'll get to the bottom of this!"

As soldiers, knights, advisors and servants run around with haste to root out more assassins, you start to make your way to the door. "Wait!" The Lord Paladine calls out.  Walking to you, he takes a deep breath: "I do not know how to thank you for this."

"You not only saved my life, but most likely prevented Tanirith from falling into chaos. Words can't convey my gratitude for what you have done. Please, accept these small tokens of my -and Tanirith's- appreciation for your noble services."
Shaking your hands, the Lord nods firmly and goes back to coordinate the search for more assassins within his castle.

"How's your progress?" The Lord Paladine asks.  You then announce proudly that Wailsrond stands independent and free. "Praise be Tyr!" The Lord exclaims, raising his fists in victory, as his advisors and guards shout their approval at such news.

"Surely those councilors who opposed help to Lord Pyre will fall for this!" Another one exclaims. "Why didn't King Dragonheart sign this himself?" Someone else asks. Through it all, the Lord Paladine remains slumped on his throne, pensive.

"By Tyr!" He then exclaims, a bit frustrated. "Well, Lantharond's actions change things somewhat." He begins to pace around his throne, deep in thoughts. He then stops, turning to you: "The High Council be damned, then!" He snarls.

"Go take a deserved rest." He adds, with renewed determination. "I'll order High Commander Fireblade to send a detachment of knights near Sparklestone; tomorrow, you go see Lord Pyre to tell him that Tanirith stands ready to help to retake Sparklestone."
Without further due, you take your leave with even greater determination to bring down Sharranth.
"Tell him that the knights will ride in the moment his army launches its assault. With you alongside, I am certain that the enemy will fall!"

You then offer that, having dispatched Taroth Sark, the councilors should be free of the nefarious mental influences of the Overlord. The Lord Paladine nods: "Yes. But it will take quite a while before they all come back to their senses." He counters.

"By the way," the Lord adds, "the embarassment that you caused at Lady Shalla Thrall's mansion has been very costly to us politically, since Jarad and I have fought hard to sponsor you to the High Council." At this reminder, you blush with shame.

"Never mind that." The Lord Paladine continues, dismissively. "You are, after all, adventurers, and not folks versed in diplomacy or politics ..." He then shrugs, although you perceive him to be somewhat disapointed by what you have done.

"How is your progress?" The Lord Paladine asks you, being obviously worried. You tell him all you have done so far. He nods thoughtfully in response: "Well done, but remember that time is of essence: you must concentrate on our current objective!"

The Lord Paladine is busy coordinating the defense preparations for the city. The old knight looks weary and tired, looking as if he's one hundred years old and near death. You wonder how he manages to stand, let alone think.
Not wishing to disturb him for naught, you turn away to leave.

"Welcome back, Heroes!" Lord Pyre greets you warmly. "So? What news to you bring from Tanirith?" Grinning, you tell the Lord that knights of the Flame stand poised to help Wailsrond to liberate Sparklestone. "Ah-Ha!" Pyre exclaims, with satisfaction.
You notice that more and more people are going in and out of Wailsrond, now that it is not under siege anymore.

One of the guards on the battlement shouts in alarm: "It's them! The traitors!!!" He yells, pointing to you. As numerous soldiers rush to the gates, you decide it best to avoid a confrontation for now and simply run away.

Looks like news travel fast ... or was it Anthraxus Storm himself who decided to let the news out of your defection to his side, knowing this would spread like wildfire? It would appear that he is intent on keeping you on your toes!

"By Tyr!" He then exclaims, a bit frustrated. "Well, Lantharond's actions change things somewhat." He begins to pace around his throne, deep in thoughts. He then stops, turning to you: "The High Council be damned!" He snarls.

"Great!" She exclaims. "I know that this invasion of Sharranth must be dealt with first, so I'll help you! But at the first occasion, we must go to that monster's lair and rid the seas of it once and for all! I found out where its lair is,
from a map I managed to acquire!" Giving you the map, Jorale gathers her gear to join your party.
Jorale Ramoor has joined your party; check out the allies menu.
"Very well, then!" Jorale scoffs, as she gathers her gear. "I'll do it alone!" At that, she storms out of the place.

You are surprised to find sitting here a teen-age girl that looks a lot like Jorale Ramoor, the princess of Coral Towers, having glimpsed at her a few months ago when she made an official visit to Tanirith. Seeing your surprise, she enjoins you to sit.

"Well met, noble adventurers." She greets you politely. "I take it you must have recognized me. I'm indeed Jorale Ramoor, princess of Coral Towers. I've heard of your enrollment by the Lord Paladine, and I was hoping to find you here."

Seeing your look of confusion, she chuckles: "Never thought a princess like me would be here, of all places, eh? Well, I am on a mission for Coral Towers. Unofficially, of course!" At your dubious looks, she sighs in frustration.

You overhear a conversation: "Me dunno how long we'll last." Mumbles a merchant. "Aye." Replies a woman. "Supplies are nearly gone and our morale is low." Shaking their heads slowly in dejection, they take a sip of their drinks.

You overhear a conversation: "More and more folks are trying their luck at fleeing from here." A lady intones. "Yup." Replies a man. "They'd rather be killed out there by the sharranthines, than left to die slowly within the walls of our city."

You overhear a conversation: "What is Tanirith waiting for?" A peasant asks, angry and desperate at the same time. "Aye!" Replies another. "Me thought they were our allies. They probably figured its too late ... and me think so too."
A small family has taken shelter in this burnt house. Upon your intrusion, they run away from openings in the walls, scared to death of you.
This body is that of a wailsrondese soldier. He probably died while defending Dagger Keep from the sharranthines.
The occupants of this cave attack upon your intrusion!
"Greetings, Heroes!" He exclaims, smiling. "As ye can see, not much has changed fer us here since the sharranthines have arrived. Me suppose our village is too small fer them to bother with."

He grunts: "Have ye heard? Me brother Maleck in Coral Towers sent news the other day, and told me that the princess Jorale has fled from Coral Towers! The Queen is all distraught." After exchanging more pleasantries, you take your leave.
Daleck is still sitting on his porch, smoking his pipe while rocking in his chair.  He waves in greeting as you pass by, then goes back to enjoying a peaceful sunny day.
The sign above the door of this shop reads: "Lantharond's Forgeworks".
A sign above the door of this establishment reads: "Inn of the Singing Mermaid".
A sign above the door of this place reads: "The Dragon's Lair".
The sign-post here reads: "Crescent Lake".

The gates of the amazon village lie open, the doors twisted and off their hinges.  From where you stand, you see that all the huts have been razed to the ground, as numerous amazon bodies lay everywhere.
You can't help but wonder who, or what, caused such systematic destruction of this amazon nation.

This amazon is lying here, battered, bloodied, and on her last breath.  She looks at you, pleading with her eyes to lean closer: "Last night ..." She rasps. "Shadow elves ... most of us fell ... others were taken ..." At that, she expires.
The sign above the door of this store reads: "The Sailor's Deck".
The sign above the door of this shop reads: "Imported Arcane Wonders".
A sign above the door of this place reads: "Inn of the Coral Reefs".
The sign above the door of this shop reads: "Leatherwork Masters".
This shop looks like a general store.
These are the Magistrate Halls of Coral Towers. Having no business here, you get on your way.
A sign above the door of this place reads: "The Laughing Tempest".
Just as you are about to open this door, one of the wenches stops you: "Me apologies, sirs and ladies, but patrons are not allowed in there." Embarassed, you walk away.
"Food will cost 12 golds total. Which one of ye will pay?"
Soon enough, you are brought large, steaming bowls of seafood stew made with shrimps, clams, cod and vegetables. Not only is it very tasty, but it hits the spot very nicely indeed!

"Aah, yes!" Exclaims Jorale before digging into her food. "I had missed the shrimp and cod of Coral Towers! They are the best of the Realmz continent, you know!" At that, she starts to eat with gusto.
"Drinks will cost 12 golds total. Who'll pay?"
"Food and drinks will cost 30 golds. Which one of ye will pay?"

Soon enough, you are brought your servings. The meal consists of steaming bowls of shrimp, cod, clam and vegetable stew, along with mugs of local mead. The stew is tasty and hits the spot nicely, while the mead is bitter but quite refreshing and strong.

Looking inside this larger hut, you make out the body of a slain amazon amidst the rubble and ashes. Upon closer look, you see that this amazon is dressed in an embroidered leather robe and adorned with feathers.

Although the robe and apparels are now soiled, bloodied and tatered, you guess that this amazon must have been the queen. Before she died, she managed to write the words "shadow elf" into the ashes next to her, with her other hand pointing to the west.

Looking inside the burnt queen's hut, you make out the body of Scyrella Silverspear amidst the rubble and ashes. Before she died, she managed to write the words "shadow elf" into the ashes next to her, with her other hand pointing to the west.

Looking inside the queen's hut, you make out the body of Scyrella Silverspear amidst the rubble and ashes. Your heart stops with dread at seeing her laying there, battered and bloodied. A burning rage for her killers begins to well up inside of you.

To your astonishment, you then hear a faint moan coming from Scyrella. Rushing to her, you heal her as best as you can. As she regains conscience, she rises with a start in a sitting position, her fists raised: "Shadow elves!!!" She shouts in alarm.

"Stand fast my sisters!" She screams, now becoming hysterical. As you restrain her, she begins to register your presence: "What? Who?" She mumbles incoherently. "My friends! Quick! Help us against these savages!" She exclaims in earnest.

With great sadness, you calm her down with soothing words while explaining to her that her tribe is no more. As reality sets in, Scyrella begins to wail and sob: "Noooo! This can't be!" She cries, her devastation and pain breaking your heart.

Consoling her as best as you can, you vow to her that you will help to avenge her tribe. Hugging you fiercely, Scyrella regains some of her usual strength and determination: "Yes, my friends. I thank you with all my soul. We will seek out those killers,

and make them pay!" She says between clenched teeth. Gathering herself, she gives a long, sadened look at her destroyed village. "Let us go to the west of here." She whispers, as tears well up in her eyes anew. "There must be a passage leading to them,

for they came from the west to attack us." Looking one last time at the ruins of her village, as if to etch forever in her mind the destruction done by the shadow elves, Scyrella begins to walk resolutely to the west. With heavy hearts, you follow.
Scyrella Silverspear has joined your party; check out the Allies menu.

This amazon is lying here, battered, bloodied, and on her last breath.  She looks at Scyrella, pleading with her eyes to lean closer: "My Queen ..." She rasps. "You live! ... Like you, most of us fell ... but others were taken ..." At that, she expires.

Closing the eyes of her dead amazon sister, Scyrella rises with a look of grim determination: "Then there is hope. If some of my sisters have been taken away, probably as slaves, then we must free them!"  You nod in earnest.
"Then, and only then, will we make the shadow elves pay!" She adds with a snarl of pure hatred.

Catching up to Scyrella, you tell her what the other amazon told you before dying. With a look of grim determination, Scyrella turns to you: "Then there is hope. If some of my sisters have been taken away, then we must free them!"  You nod in earnest.
"This must be it!" Scyrella Silverspear exclaims, a twinge of triumph in her voice. "This must be the way to the shadow elves!"

You overhear a conversation: "Me tell ye me saw it with me own eyes!" A sailor exclaims. "Bigger than ten boats, me says!" Another sailor nods. "Aye. It does appear that Sseshinibonss, the great sea serpent, has awaken! We be doomed, me friend!"

You over hear a conversation: "Have ye heard?" A woman asks to another. "Apparently, princess Jorale has run away to the mainland! The Queen is all distraught!" The other nods: "Yes. I wonder why Jorale has done this."

You overhear a conversation: "More sea serpents are spotted each week!" Exclaims a fisherman. "Aye." Replies another. "Some say them beasties have been emboldened by the awakening of Sseshinibonss, the great sea serpent! I ain't returning to sea soon!"
You notice that Jorale is warily pulling up the head cover of her cloak, as to better conceal her identity.

You overhear a conversation: "That mess on the mainland's still going on." Mumbles a fisheman. "Aye." Replies a sailor. "Me just glad that we're not having any of these woes over here in Coral Towers. Last year's pirates and the regent were enough!"

You overhear a conversation: "Trading with Umaldyr is going in earnest!" Exclaims a sea merchant, quite smug. "Indeed!" Replies another, grinning. "Although, I am worried of the problems they are experiencing over there ... could be bad for business."

You overhear a conversation: "That Warlord of Sharranth sure is greedy!" Mumbles a sailor. "Yup!" Replies another. "But me don't think us in Coral Towers need fear of him: after all, he doesn't have a navy, eh?"
Soldiers on watch nod politely.
"No!" Exclaims Jorale, as you approach the gates of the castle. "We have not defeated the great sea serpent yet! I can't go home now!"
Guards are on watch at the castle gates. "Sorry gents!" One of them exclaims with authority. "Folks without proper business aren't allowed through."
Soldiers are coming out of the barracks to go on patrol.
Queen Aquillae Ramoor is conferring with her advisors. At your entrance, one of her servants motions you to walk up to her.

"And please don't take me back to Coral Towers just yet! I need to do this!" She implores you.  Smiling, you inform her that you have already taken care of Sseshinibonss. "You- ... you have?" Jorale replies, dismayed. "What will I do now?"

You offer her to join you, for a while, and then bring her back to Coral Towers. Sighing, Jorale rises from her chair: "I guess that's better than doing nothing. I know that this invasion of Sharranth must be dealt with first, so I'll help you!"
"Jorale!" The Queen exclaims with joy, as her daughter rushes to embrace her. Both lay in each other's embrace as soldiers and servants voice their happiness at the return of the princess.

"We did it, mother!" A tearful Jorale mumbles between sobs. "Sseshinibonss is dead for good. We are saved!"  The Queen hugs her daughter even tighter: "Oh, Jorale! Why did you risk yourself so? You did not need to!"  Jorale takes a step back at that.

"Yes I did, mother. I had to prove to our people that I am worthy of becoming Queen once you pass on the Coral Crown to me."  Aquillae Ramoor shakes her head, thorn between pride and irritation at her head-strong daughter: "My dear Jorale." She whispers.

"Haven't you realized by now that our people want not a strong ruler, but a wise and compassionate one? That is what your unlamented, late uncle the Regent refused to understand. The people's respect for their Liege comes from our caring for them,

not from our feats or from a fear of us! Beside, didn't you know you had already earned the respect of our people, by standing against your uncle Thorgal when he usurped the Coral Crown last year?" By Jorale's surprised reaction, she obviously had not.

The Queen sighs, smiling tenderly at her confused daughter: "If anything, your escapade only worried our people to death, and me as well!" At that, the Queen hugs her mollified daughter once more, before turning to you: "I thank you, noble ones,
for not only returning the princess to us, but destroying Sseshinibonss as well. Please, accept a token of our deepest gratitude." Immediately, a small chest is brought to you.

"We thank you again." The Queen adds, bowing her head. "It was awesome, guys!" Jorale adds, beaming with joy. "But now I have to stay ... if only to learn once and for all how to be a good ruler!" Her mother hugs her again at that.
With final goodbyes, you take your leave.
The Queen nods politely to you as she goes on discussing important matters with her advisors. With princess Jorale nowhere to be seen about, you bow in turn to the Queen and take your leave.

"Oh, mother!" A tearful Jorale mumbles between sobs. "Sseshinibonss is dead for good. We are saved!"  The Queen hugs her daughter even tighter: "Oh, Jorale! Why did you risk yourself so? You did not need to!" Jorale takes a step back at that.
for returning the princess to us. Please, accept a token of our deepest gratitude." Immediately, a small chest is brought to you.
"Welcome, noble adventurers." Queen Aquillae Ramoor greets you.
"It is good to see you again!" She adds, smiling.

"I am glad that you have come," she continues, a look of sadness on her face, "for my daughter, princess Jorale, has run away from Coral Towers. She has taken upon herself to rid us of Sseshinibonss, the great sea serpent, which awoke a few weeks ago."

You immediately tell the Queen that you have killed Sseshinibonss. "Oh! By Ukkor! This is great news for us, since the leviathan was a true menace for our ships! But what of my daughter? Could I impose on you to find her and bring her back?"
You nod in acceptance. "Oh, thank you, noble ones! As gratitude for ridding us of the great sea serpent, place accept this token from us." At that, a servant brings you a small chest.
Vowing to bring her daughter back, you take your leave from the Queen: "Safe journeys, and safer returns!" She bids you in farewell, full of hope that you'll succeed.

"Have you found her?" The Queen asks expectantly. With your silent shaking of the head, her hopes fade away. "Please, find Jorale. I am so worried for her!" She whispers, before returning to the affairs of her state.

She sighs heavily: "So, not only are we being threatened by this leviathan which is terrorizing our seas, but my daughter is missing and probably in danger! If there is anything you can do to help, we would be much grateful."
"I wish I could speak more with you, but with these two crises upon us, I must return to the affairs of our state." With a respectful bow, you take your leave.
This large cave opening leads deeper within the small island. A sickening aroma of fish and dead meat permeates the air. Do you go in?
Sea serpents!!!
Rising from the waters, a serpent at least thrice the size of any other sea serpent gazes at you, its baleful reptilian eyes glaring at you with pure evil.
The sight of this towering leviathan induces a primal fear of such intensity that you have great difficulty fighting the urge to flee!
Immediately, the great sea serpent attacks!
Lesser sea serpents come to help Sseshinibonss!
Cutting up the great serpent, you find precious items in its large stomach, probably belonging to previous victims it ate!
"We did it!" Exclaims a jubilant Jorale. "Now, I can go home!"
Tired but smiling with pride, you set yourselves to get on your way.

"Welcome back!" Jarad greets you. "What have you to report?" You show him the spy report that you found. "Hmmm ..." The councilor mumbles, as he reads it. "Well, this confirms it! We do have a traitor among us! You must find him of her!"
With a firm nod, you get on your way.

"Welcome back!" Jarad greets you. "What have you to report?" You show him the burned letter that you found. "Hmmm ..." The councilor mumbles, as he reads it. "Well, this does tend to implicate Lady Thrall, but clearly this is not enough."
"You must dig more!" He adds in earnest. "However, be careful as not to accuse anyone without proper proof; otherwise, it will be costly to the Lord Paladine and me!"

"Welcome back!" Jarad greets you. "What have you to report?"  He then gasps in surprise at seeing Nomune Ngallan with you, all dishiveled and tired. "What is the meaning of this?" Jarad demands, glaring at you.

"Lord Jarad." Nomune intones, stepping forward. "Do not blame these noble gents for my current state. Quite the contrary in fact, for they have delivered me from bondage at the hands of an illicit guild of assassins underneath our fair city!"

You then proceed to tell Jarad Noll under what circumstances you found councilor Ngallan."By Tyr!" Jarad exclaims. "For how long have you been prisoner of these criminals, Lord Ngallan?" Nomune shrugs and shakes his head, at a loss.

"Well, then!" Jarad continues. "It is now obvious 'who' is the traitor, or rather under who's guise he operated under! Time is now of the essence: you good heroes must go to Lord Ngallan's mansion and apprehend this impostor!"

"In the meantime, I'll take good care of Lord Ngallan until your return." Nomune sighs with relief: "I deeply appreciate this, Lord Noll." He then turns to you: "I wish you good luck, noble ones." With a determined nod, you get on your way.

Both Jarad Noll and Nomune Ngallan are smiling, quite happy to see you: "Congratulations!" Jarad beams. "And my deepest gratitude" adds Nomune. You then proceed to tell them what you uncovered in Nomune's mansion. "By Tyr!" Jarad exclaims.

"An Overlord? Within our midst?" He adds, incredulous and shocked. "Well, it all makes sense then: who else but someone with mental powers could subtly alter the minds of our councilors and make them do his bidding?" You nod in agreement.

"Well, he is gone now!" Jarad continues, "Although the damage he has wrought will take some time to heal." Nomune then intervenes: "Yes, sadly. But now, we must go on, especially in my case. So, I'll return to my estates and put things back together."

He then nods to Jarad: "I thank you again from the bottom of my heart for your hospitality. Now, before I take my leave, I would like to reward those noble adventurers for saving me and my estates."  He presents you with a small chest.

"It's not much," Nomune adds, "but it's what I had stashed in a deposit box of mine at the bank." He winks at that, before taking his leave. "Well, then!" Beams Jarad, "It is now my turn to reward you for your valorous services to Tanirith!"

"On behalf of Tanirith, the Lord Paladine, and the High Council, I thank you again." Jarad adds, bowing in gratitude. "I wish you safe journeys and safer returns, noble gents!" With these final partings, you take your leave.
At that, you show him the burned letter that you found. "Hmmm ..." The councilor mumbles, as he reads it. "Well, this does tend to implicate Lady Thrall, but clearly this is not enough."
He then gasps in complete surprise upon seeing Nomune Ngallan standing among you, all dishiveled and tired. "What is the meaning of this?" Jarad demands, glaring at you.

"By the way," Jarad adds, "the embarassment that you caused at Lady Thrall's mansion has been very costly to us politically, since the Lord Paladine and I have fought hard to sponsor you to the High Council." At this reminder, you blush with shame.

"Never mind that." He continues dismissively. "You are, after all, adventurers, and not folks versed in diplomacy or politics ..." He then shrugs, although you perceive him to be somewhat disapointed by what you have done.

"Sharranth was founded some five centuries ago. Until about one hundred winters past, the growing city had always suffered the rule of petty lords and despots. Even when the Halgard royal dynasty arose, things did not change much for the sharranthines."

"Although it was under this ruling dynasty that Sharranth sort of opened to the rest of the Sword Lands, establishing numerous peace and trade treaties with other city-states of the region. But six years ago, Anthraxus Storm arrived at the gates ..."

"Baerun Halgard, the last king of Sharranth, did all he could to repel Storm's invasion. But the infamous Warlord had the size of his army on his side, and it was rumored at the time that he had managed to buy off some 'inside' help."

"Thus, he conquered the city and seized the crown for himself. Of the Halgard dynasty, only Baerun's son, Naerun, managed to escape with his life. Since then, Sharranth has been again closed off from the rest of the Sword Lands,

leaving everyone guessing as to the Warlord's intentions. One thing that quickly became known, however, is that adventurers are forbidden to enter the city. Apparently, Storm rightfully distrusts meddling adventurers."

"Heh, the Eye." Mumbles the dwarf. "Well, this magical trinket wuz created by Khan-Alghuul, the sorcerer-king that ruled Sharranth centuries ago. Some say that the Eye allows ye to spy on others from afar. "

"O'course, the durn Eye wuz rumored to have disappeared when old Khan wuz deposed an' killed by some usurper. But it eventually became known that the item is in fact transmitted from one sharranthine Royal Warlock to another."
"So, me guess is that the Eye is in possession of the current Royal Warlock, a shifty, evil man named Ertham Zoh. Yer job is to take it from him an' bring it back!"

"Hah!" Exclaims the dwarf. "Well, this one's simple: find the ruins of Asturia in the desert of Astaroth, an' bring back a couple o' baubles from there as proof that ye found the place! Good luck, cuz no one ever managed even reach the durn desert!"

"Hah!" Exclaims the dwarf. "Well, this one's simple: find the ruins of Algaroth in the Volcanic Rockies, an' bring back a couple o' baubles from there as proof that ye found the place! Good luck, cuz no one ever managed to survive such journey!"

"The wyrm, eh?" Intones the dubious dwarf. "Well, this big critter is rumored to be lairin' somewhere in the Western Lands. Some say she's been asleep fer decades now, while others are afraid that she may have mated and now in cluch."
"Either way, she's a terror an' must be killed before she strikes agin! So, ye find her lair an' rid the Sword Lands of this critter!"
"The wyrm, eh?" The dubious dwarf intones. "Well, this one's just moved in  the northeastern Lands, an' terrorizing folks all around. So, yer job is to find this critter and rid us of it!"
The mansion of Lord Cheron Ironseed lies in ruins. You fear that the lord must have died during the invasion of the sharranthines.
This rubble used to be a mansion, probably owned by Sparklestone's last lord. You fear that this lord must have died during the invasion of the sharranthines.
Dagger Keep's castle lies in rubble, thanks to the sharranthines.
Your intensive search reveals that part of the mountain wall is an illusion, covering the entrance of a cave!

As you pass here, Braggan Stoneheart stops, gazing pensively at the mountain wall. "Somethin' ain't right here!" He grumbles. "Me sure this mountain wall is wrong or me's a beardless goblin!" Intrigued, you walk up to him to look closer at this.
"Hah!" Exclaims Braggan, quite proud of himself. "Me told ye, eh?" He winks at that, tapping the side of his nose with his index finger.

You come into a small, windy valley. Facing you is a centuries-old temple, crumbling to ruins. From the few legible markings left on the temple's walls, you find that it was once dedicated to Bhalaal, God of Pain and Torture.
You arrive at the home of Daleck, the fisherman you helped six months ago. He is sitting on his porch, rocking slowly while enjoying a good smoking pipe.
The battle rages!!!
You must warn the Lord Paladine of Tanirith that there is now War in the Sword Lands!!!

From where you stand, it would seem that a rather quite sizeable contingent of sharranthine forces are stationed in the town.  Without additonal help on your side, you're not confident at all you could reclaim the town from the sharranthines.
You decide to keep a low profile and stay clear of the town.
You then hear a large explosion coming from far away, to the northeast. Something must has happened with the collapsed volcano in the Khanark Rockies. Your gut instincts tell you it must not be good.
"Durn it!" Exclaims the dour dwarf. "We've already gave this job to someone else, although we haven't heard from them fer a while. Well, ye'll have ta choose another job, folks!"

Out of nowhere, vials are thrown at you feet, breaking and releasing a powerful sleeping gas! As if in a dream, you see yourselves being tied up and your heads covered with black hoods, then dumped into a cart.
The old, crumbling temple of Bhalaal looms ominously. Instead of doors, the entrance to the temple consists of a high and wide opening flanked by old marble columns. Do you go inside?
This old, crumbling statue represents Bhalaal, the God of Pain, Suffering and Torture.
This is an old, moldy altar that was most likely used to sacrifice the living to Bhalaal. Brushing away the mold, dust and crust off the altar, you decipher old markings etched into the stone:
"Let him who hath understanding of the key of life known to Bhalaal speak it, and he shall receive our Dead Lord's blessings".
Outerwordly beings are sent to punish you for your manhandling of the altar!
A dark light emanates from the altar, rapidly enveloping you and providing healing energies!
Bhalaal rewards your ineptitude the only way he knows best!
This large gaping hole goes deep into the ground. You cannot fathom its depth.
A large gaping hole high in the ceiling of this cave appears to lead back to the surface.
Success! You all end up on the other side!
Your fidgeting about has attracted attention!

This small, quiet lake prevents you from going on further. Although you can see the other end of the lake, the darkness beyond prevents you from seeing what is on the other side. If anything awaits you, that is ...
You attentiveness reveals that this section of this moldy carpet covers a large hole in the floor!

"Wait, my comrades!" Athos interjects, preventing you from going on further. Without a word, he kneels down to the moldy carpet and easily removes a section of it here, revealing a large hole in the floor!
"I sensed that something was amiss with this section of the carpet." Your comrade muses.

"Wait, my friends!" Riel interjects, preventing you from going on further. Without a word, he kneels down to the moldy carpet and easily removes a section of it here, revealing a large hole in the floor!
Just as you walk over this section of the carpet, the fabric gives way, revealing a large hole into the floor!
Thanks to your spell, none of you fell to a certain death.
The party member positioned at the front of your formation falls to a certain death!

To your horror, a huge green dragon comes out of the darkness to face you. You barely have time to notice troll servants coming to his side, before being gripped by dragonfear at the site of this ancient wyrm. This must be indeed Sapphire Death!

To your horror, a huge green dragon comes out of the darkness to face you. You barely have time to notice troll servants coming to his side, before being gripped by dragonfear at the site of this ancient wyrm. This must be indeed Sapphire Death!

"Intruders .... and dinner!" The huge wyrm snarls, gusts of gas flaring out of his nostrils. "It has been a while since I've enjoyed a good meal such as you, fools that you are!"  At that, Sapphire Death and his servants attack!

But thanks to your alertness, you are not surprised at ending up face to face with the wyrm. Sapphire Death also senses this. "So, intruders." He snarls, gusts of gas flaring out of his nostrils. "What should I do with you?" He asks, chuckling.

"Well, I am not that hungry right now, and I am impressed by your temerity. Hence, I give you a choice: give me all your belongings, and I give you my word as a dragon that I will let you go." Do you give all your items to Sapphire Death?
"Good!" Muses Sapphire Death as you start taking off all your equipment and droping it at his feet. Once you are done, the wyrm grabs all of you and flies you back to the surface!
"And don't come back!" The wyrm snarls, as he drops you off. "Or next time, I shall not be as merciful!" Casting at you a final glare of anger, Sapphire Death returns to his lair.

Once again, the huge green dragon comes out of the darkness to face you. You barely have time to notice troll servants coming to his side, before being gripped once more by dragonfear at the site of this ancient wyrm.
"I warned you, fools!" Snarls Sapphire Death, before he and his troll servants attack!
"Very well, you have made your choice!" Sapphire Death snarls, before attacking along with his troll servants!
You find the hoard of Sapphire Death!
Catching your breath, you decide you might as well explore this compound further.

From where you stand, it would seem that a rather quite sizeable contingent of sharranthine forces are stationed in the town.  Without additonal help on your side, you're not confident at all you could reclaim Sparklestone from the sharranthines.

"Welcome back!" Jarad greets you. "What have you to report?" You then proceed to tell Jarad Noll that you found councilor Nomune Ngallan and liberated him from the Assassins' Guild, but that he was killed before you could bring him back to safety.

"By Tyr!" Jarad exclaims, aghast at your revelation. "It is now obvious 'who' is the traitor, or rather under who's guise he operated under! Time is now of the essence: you good heroes must go to Lord Ngallan's mansion and apprehend this impostor!"
"In the meantime, I'll take care of Lord Ngallan's body until your return. I wish you good luck, noble ones." With a determined nod, you get on your way.

You are surprised to see Nomune Ngallan standing beside Jarad Noll. "Congratulations!" Jarad beams. "And my deepest gratitude." Adds Nomune, bowing his head. You then proceed to tell them what you uncovered in Nomune's mansion.

"By Tyr!" Jarad exclaims, surprised and shocked. "An Overlord? Within our midst? Well, it all makes sense then: who else but someone with mental powers could subtly alter the minds of our councilors and make them do his bidding?" You nod in agreement.

He then nods to Jarad: "I thank you again from the bottom of my heart for paying to raise me from the dead. Now, before I take my leave, I would like to reward those noble adventurers for saving me and my estates."  He presents you with a small chest.

More psi-warriors join the fray! However, real soldiers of the Royal guard of the Dragon Throne rush in the throne room to protect the crown, fighting on your side!
