"I believe you, cousin." Red answers, his angry gaze upon a repentent Eregion. "But your ambition blinded you, and thus endangered our people and our kingdom. I order you to retire to your estates, and remain there until you are called to stand trial."

Erion sighs in resignation. "I will do as you say, my King." He whispers. "I know in my heart that your judgment will be fair and equitable. I thank you for that." In response, Red puts his hand on Eregion's shoulder to confirm the man's faith in him.

As more soldiers of the Royal guard scour the castle to root out any remaining psi-warriors, the deposed Regent turns to leave. "She probably was responsible for King Vallar's death as well." He mumbles, dejected. Red Dragonsbane nods in agreement.

Red Dragonsbane turns to you: "My thanks and gratitude, noble ones." He says, shaking your hand. "Please, go take a well deserved rest and come back to see me tomorrow. In the meantime, I must properly affirm my proclamation, and stabilize our kingdom."
Tired, you nod with a smile. As the new King Red Dragonsbane walks up to stand before his throne, you take your leave.
King Red Dragonsbane is engaged in discussions with his advisors. You decide it would be best not to disturb him for naught.

"Welcome back, noble ones!" Red exclaims, smiling. He is visibly relieved by your arrival. "I have been King but for a single day, and already I am tired of dealing with advisors and aristocrats!" He whispers with a wink, chuckling at the same time.

"In any event," he continues, "I have managed to stabilize the crown, but a few loose ends remain." He nods pensively: "For example, our diplomatic status with Tanirith. Misguided, Erion managed to convince the court that our alliance was worthless."

The King sighs. "Unfortunately, too many remain convinced that breaking the alliance with Tanirith is the right thing to do. I am all too aware that the Lord Paladine needs some stability concerning Lantharond, given all that's been happening."
"However, I do wish to be of friendship with the Lord Paladine and resolve any diplomatic uncertainty. So, I have come up with a plan which will help to this end, as well as my people!"

"As you may have heard, we have been plagued with savage raids by fire giants, of late. These raids are most disruptive to my people and our economy. So, I ask for your help in ending this threat ..."

"All I know," the King continues, "is that the fire giants live somewhere northwest in the Volcanic Rockies. I don't expect you to destroy them by yourselves, and I'm quite aware that Tanirith's army is currently rather 'occupied', and thus unavailable."

"Therefore, my plan is simple: you end the fire giant threat to us and, because you are seen as representatives of Tanirith, this will certainly sway the Dragon Court back in favor of a renewed alliance with the Lord Paladine. So, everyone wins!"

"Of course," King Dragonsbane adds with a wink, "I will reward you for doing such a service for Lantharond!" Smiling in turn and shaking the hand of the King to seal the bargain, you take your leave. "I wish you success!" The King says in parting.

"Welcome back!" King Dragonsbane greets you. You annouce proudly that the fire giants have been defeated and routed. "Praise be Tyr and Codan!" The King exclaims, as the Dragon court erupts in cheers.

After the cheering winds down, King Dragonsbane presents to you a small chest: "For your heroic deeds which have not only preserved the Dragon Thone but, most importantly, ensured the security of our people!" He announces solemnly.

"I thank you again, noble ones." The King continues. "I'll soon send envoys to the Lord Paladine to secure our alliance. Maybe not tomorrow, for we still have much to do to restore our kingdom, but very soon." You bow respectfully before leaving.

You notice that some in the court are not convinced yet about a renewed alliance with Tanirith. However, these remain in the minority and thus you know that King Dragonsbane will be successful. "Safe journeys, and safer returns!" He tells you in parting.
Emboldened, you take your leave.
Guards on watch nod politely and let you pass.
Numerous people cross the gates of Lantharond. You notice soldiers on the battlements, ever watchful and alert.
The compound of the false Lantharond troopers you defeated months ago now lies in rubble.
Mariners and harbor workers are busy loading and unloading goods and foodstuffs from merchant vessels.
A sign above the door of this establishment reads: "The Great Wyrm".
You notice that Red Dragonsbane is warily pulling up the head cover of his cloak, as to better conceal his identity.

The barkeep leans closer to whisper: "Trade with the island-nation of Umaldyr has really increased, and we're receiving goods from there and other places from Anarym. But some say that Umaldyr has plenty of grave problems of its own ..."

The barkeep leans closer: "Our King is on his death-bed, fallen by some strange disease. Our priests can't do a durn thing about it. Some say that mayhaps the King is dead already, 'cuz Queen Aramina has appointed a Regent to rule in his place ..."

The barkeep leans closer: "Queen Aramina's apparently having an affair with Eregion Dragonshield, whom she named as Regent of the Dragon Throne to replace our ailing King Vallar Dragonheart. Many speak of dark intrigues within the Dragon Court as well."

The barkeep leans closer: "The Captain of the Royal Guard, Red Dragonsbane, has disapeared from sight. Some say he wuz done with by Queen Aramina and Regent Eregion, 'cuz he supported our ailing King Vallar. Others say he's on a quest to save the King!"

The barkeep leans closer to whisper: "Me heard that the amazons of Artemisia Forest have been completely wiped out! Some say that's the price they paid for invoking dark and evil gods; others say the fire giants did it. Who knows?" He shrugs at that.

The barkeep leans closer to whisper: "Fire giants have begun raiding us again. Some of them hide in caves north of here. Me heard that they found a way to control the collapsed volcano, and are aiming to use it as a weapon to destroy us fer good!"

The barkeep leans closer to whisper: "Me heard talk about some temple in ruins lying southwest of here in the mountains. So far, no one has managed to find a way to get to it. Some say that an old green dragon lives there!"
"Hear ye, hear ye!" Booms a paige upon your entrance into the Hall, flanked by numerous militia soldiers. "His excellency, the Magistrate Dragonstone, is now ready to hear and arbiter this case!"
"Hear ye, hear ye!" Booms a paige upon your entrance into the Hall, flanked by numerous militia soldiers. "His excellency, the Magistrate Naros, is now ready to hear and arbiter this case!"
"Hear ye, hear ye!" Booms a paige upon your entrance into the Hall, flanked by numerous militia soldiers. "His excellency, the Magistrate Issus, is now ready to hear and arbiter this case!"
"No money to pay or that ye want to spend, eh?" Replies the Magistrate. "Very well: I therefore sentence ye to a full sevenday in our city jail!"
At that, your equipment and your valuables are striped from you, as you are put in chains and escorted to jail.
The jail door is locked shut.
"Here's some food and water, ye bums!" As militia soldier snarls, tossing the stuff at your feet before closing the jail door.
Guards open the door of your cell, calling your names: "Yer sentence is over!" He tells you. "We're sending ye back outside!"
You are given back your gear, and brought swiftly out of the Justice Halls. With much relief, you shed no tears at leaving your cell behind.

Red Dragonsbane sits down on the floor, dejected: "How humiliating!" He complains. "Me, the Captain of the Royal guard, thrown in prison! I suppose I should thank Tyr that no one recognized me!" He shakes his head in resignation.
You notice that Scyrella Silverspear is glaring at you, her reproachful silence stinging even more than if she were actually shouting angry words at you.
Denard Fireshield shakes his head in disgust. "So," he muses, his cold and sarcastic tone of voice visibly directed at you, "this is what a prison cell looks like. How quaint!" You shrug in response.
"Anyone for a little game of cards? We have plenty of time, now." Riel Moonsong asks with levity, just as he settles himself comfortably on one of the beds.

Jorale Ramoor goes into a fit: "I can't believe this! This is so humiliating! What was I thinking when I chose to tag along with you guys? By Ukkor! I just hope my mother won't forsake me as her successor because of this!"
"THIS IS ALL YOUR FAULT!!!" She adds with a scream, pointing an accusing finger at you. At that, she turns her back on you to sulk.
Without a word, Master Athos sits in a corner, adopting a meditative pose.
"I suppose," muses a dejected Belrion, "that being thrown in prison is simply a continuation of my miserable existence." Shaking his head in disgust, he sits in a corner to brood.
"Durn good building!" Muses Braggan Stoneheart, his tone appreciative as he strokes and pats the bricks of the walls. "I've always known human prisons were almost as good as ours."

"Very well." He exclaims, with exasperation. "There has been reports that an assassins' Guild has established itself somewhere in the Sword Lands, and that it goes by the name of the Red Claw. I'll inform my commanders of what happened here."

"Me heard that trade with the island-nation of Umaldyr has really increased, and we're receiving goods from there and other places from Anarym. But some say that Umaldyr has plenty of grave problems of its own ..."

"Remember the famous Heroes of the Sword Lands, who saved us from them three Overlords?" You nod, trying hard not to smirk. "Well, me heard talk that the other six Overlords finally did them in! This goes to show that good deeds never go unpunished, eh?"

"Me heard that the amazons of Artemisia Forest have been completely wiped out! Some say that's the price they paid for invoking dark and evil gods; others say the fire giants did it. Who really knows?"

"Me heard some explorers talk about a desert wasteland north of the Volcanic Rockies. They wuz mentioning that monstrous beastmen and sandworms roam about this forsaken land of death! They also mentioned evil Stone Guardians, but I ain't sure."
"Me heard talk about some temple in ruins lying southwest of here in the mountains. So far, no one has managed to find a way to get to it. Some say that an old green dragon lives there!"

"Me heard talk of some lost ruins in the Volcanic Rockies, near to the sea. They say that the ruins are thousands of years old, and haunted still by the powerful spirits of those who used to live there. Demons are also said to live in them ruins!"

You overhear a conversation: "I can't belive this of our Queen!" A woman exclaims. "I'm telling you!" Replies the other. "She's having an affair with the Regent while our King is dying from this strange illness! Why else would she name him Regent?"

You overhear a conversation: "It's really a shame for our good king." Muses a sailor. "Aye!" Replies another. "And no one knows what is this disease that's killing him. Even the priests are baffled!" Both men shake their head in sadness.

You overhear a conversation: "Who'll take the throne when our poor king passes away?" Asks a farmer. "Probably the Regent, who is a cousin." Muses a sailor. "How about Red Dragonsbane, the captain of the guard? He's a cousin too!" Replies the farmer.

You overhear a conversation: "I heard the captain of the Guard is missing!" Exclaims a merchant. "I've heard this as well." Replies another. "Apparently, he's gone on a quest to find a remedy that would cure our good King Vallar!"

You overhear a conversation: "Me tell ye," muses a merchant,"if them raids by fire giant are not stopped, the economy'll be hit hard!" Another merchant nods. "Aye. And I've heard talk that them raids are but a prelude to an all out invasion!"

You overhear a conversation: "Me tell ye!" Exclaims a sailor. "One of the barkeeps confirmed it to me. The fire giants are trying to find a way to use the volcano as a weapon against us!" Another sailor shakes his head: "Then, we are doomed!"

You overhear a conversation: "What are the authorities doing about them fire giants?" Asks an incensed woman. Her friend shrugs: "I've heard that cavalry troopers are patrolling the north and west of our city, but many of them get killed by the giants."
The sign above the door of this store reads: "The Sailor's Deck".
A sign above the door of this shop reads: "Nyressyl's Wondrous Wonders".
A sign above the door of this shop reads:  "Jereph's Shop of Conveniances".
A sign above the door of this place reads: "Crescent Lake Store and Inn".

To your surprise and horror, you stumble upon the princess Jorale Ramoor as she is fighting for her life against shantiles! Wondering how in the Abyss she managed to get this far on her own, you rush to her help!

"What are you looking at?" A panting and bloodied Jorale asks with scorn, obviously resentful at your previous refusal to help her. "Did you think I'd wait for you louses to change your minds? Me, I've got a big snake to kill: what about you?"

At that, she turns and starts to walk further into the cavern. Feeling a mixture of disbelief, respect and frustration for the princess, you follow her lead. You figure you might as well help her, then return her home at the first chance you get!
Carpenters and masons are busy erecting a new building here. Curious, you spot a wooden sign planted into the ground, which reads: "Site of the future Lantharond branch-offices of Adventurers Inc.".
You are ambushed by a raiding band of fire giants!!!
You spot in the distance a raiding band of fire giants. Do you attack them?

A detatchment of cavalry troopers from Lantharond are valiantly fighting a raiding band of fire giants. From the looks of it, the troopers are badly outnumbered and loosing, despite their bravery. Do you help the troopers?

Battered and bloodied, the cavalry leader rides up to you: "Well fought, strangers! Your help came in the nick of time! If these damn fire giants keep raiding like this, they'll overwhelm us eventually." He shakes his head in dejection.

Battered and bloodied, the cavalry leader rides up to you: "Well fought, strangers! Your timely help is much appreciated! To tell you the truth, we are begining to lose morale, for them giants have been increasing their attacks." He sighs in resignation.

Battered, the cavalry leader rides up to you: "Well fought, strangers! Your help is much appreciated! We are getting weary of these raids, and look for the day when the fire giants will be defeated for good." He shakes his head in resignation.
"Ah well," he adds, "at least we're still here to fight at least one more day." With a nod in parting, he rides up to his troops to lead them back to Lantharond.
Leaving them to their fate, you walk away. However, the fading sounds of battle and the cries of the dying compound your guilt at having chosen this cowardly path.
You cross paths with a trade caravan. As the caravan passes you, the caravan master nods to you politely while mercenaries acting as caravan escorts eye you with suspicion.
You can't help but smile wistfully at the memory of your past stints as caravan escorts, during those early days of last year when you had just arrived in the Sword Lands.
You see in the distance a trade caravan under attack. Do you help the caravan?

After the battle, a bloodied and tired caravan master rides up to you: "Well fought, strangers!" He exclaims, smiling warmly. "I don't know how we would have fared without your timely help. Please, accept a token of our gratitude!"

After the battle, a bloodied and tired caravan master rides up to you: "Well fought, strangers!" She exclaims, smiling warmly. "I don't know how we would have fared without your timely help. Please, accept a token of our gratitude!"
After handing you a small chest, the caravan master bids you farewell as the trade caravan resumes its journey.
The entrance to this cave is hopelessly blocked by tons of rubble. The collapse of the mountain wall here must have occured during one of the numerous earthquakes that occur in the Volcanic Rockies.

The entrance to Kith Khanaan's ancient tomb is hopelessly blocked by tons of rubble. The collapse of the mountain wall here must have occured during one of the numerous earthquakes that occur in the Volcanic Rockies.

Being here, you wonder what has happened to Kith Khanaan's 'essence'. You are also thinking about Naryl Thezzat, the Kheryndorian psi-knight who helped you last year, and wondering where she could be now.
With the Overlords active again, you sort of expected to run into her once again. Shrugging off those questions, you get on your way.

The way here is blocked by the collapsed volcano. With the searing heat and the blinding, choking clouds of sulfur, you can't even see the other side of this infernal lava lake. Resigned, you back away.

You are rather dismayed at seeing how much the collapsed volcano has expanded, compared to the last time you had seen it. You wonder with dread what such expansion could herald for the rest of the Sword Lands, especially Lantharond.

As you enter this small vale, your are dismayed upon seeing a small group of red dragons resting and enjoying the 'weather'. While your are taken a back by this, they appear rather aloof upon your intrusion. Nonetheless, you are gripped by dragonfear.

One of the red wyrms moves toward you, glaring at you with a mixture of amusement and excitement. "Well, well, well. What have we here?" He asks with a cruel and frightening draconic grin. "Food?" One of the other asks, likewise amused.

"Fresh slaves?" Another one intones, playing along as well. "Tell you what." The first dragon intones, turning his baleful gaze back to you. "Because you have provided us such amusement by blundering into our domain like you did, I feel magnaminous."

"Agreed! Things are too often boring around here!" Exclaims one of the other red dragons. The first dragon nods: "Hence, I offer you the chance to leave here peacefully and alive, provided you turn over all your gear and riches to us!" Do you accept?

"Wise choice, little ones!" The red dragon intones with glee, as you divest yourselves of all your gear. "Now, run along and don't come back!" Not wishing for the dragons to change their minds, you run for your life as they laugh aloud.
"You made your choice, fools!" The red dragon snarls. "Ha! Food it is, then!" One of the other dragon intones, as he and his kin attack!

As you enter this small vale, your are dismayed upon seeing a small group of red dragons resting and enjoying the 'weather'. By chance, they appear to be oblivious to your presence. Nonetheless, you are gripped by dragonfear at the site of them.
Do you seize on this chance and attack these red dragons?

To your dismay, the red dragons were waiting for you. "You again? Food it is, then!" One of the dragons snarls. You can't help but be gripped by dragonfear anew upon seeing them advance with their wings spread and baring their terrible fangs and claws!
The red dragons are still in this small vale, resting and enjoying the 'weather'. As luck would have it, they appear oblivious to your presence. Do you seize this chance and attack them?
You find the hoard of the red dragons!

Not saying a word, you contend yourselves at smiling smuggly. Just as Lord Jarad is about to inquire why your are in such a mood, Nomune Ngallan finally removes the hood of his cloak, revealing his presence. You then look to Jarad, grinning even more.

Sighing, you then finally proceed to tell Jarad Noll that you have in fact found apparently 'a' councilor Nomune Ngallan and liberated him from the Assassins' Guild, but that he was killed before you could bring him back to safety.

You come into a small, windy valley. Facing you are what appear to be millennia-old ruins, judging from the thick and deforming layers of baked dust and soot covering them. The ruins protrude from the hardened lava rock which paves all of the area.

From the way they appear to have been buried long ago by lava, you guess that a whole city must be lying under the hardened lava. Intrigued, you venture forth in order to find an entrance which, hopefully, would allow you to explore this buried city.

It then dawns on you that you never saw such ruins in the Volcanic Rockies the last time you ventured here. You assume that the recent expansion of the volcano, and the turmoil it must have caused, resulted in the 'uncovering' of these protruding ruins.
A strong breeze is blowing through this undermountain natural tunnel.
Distracted by the searing heat and choking fumes, you did not see a band of fire giants keeping watch here!
Thanks to your awareness, you spot a band of fire giants standing watch here. They have not seen you. Do you attack them?
As you approach these gates, Nomune Ngallan stops, a worried look on his face. "I think perhaps we should go see someone like Lord Jarad Noll first." Agreeing to this, you get on your way.
As you approach the gates of Nomune Ngallan's estate, you decide it would be best to go see Jarad Noll first to tell him under which circumstances you found -and lost- the late councilor.
Your search reveals that the hardened lava covering the ruin where you are standing appear to be of much lesser thickness, possibility covering a hole or entrance wide enough to allow entry.
Bashing away at the rock-hard lava crust with your weapons didn't even dent it. Not wishing to break your precious weapons, you try to find another solution.
The rock-hard crust of lava gives in, revealing an entrance!
Curiosity overriding your reason, you immediately step inside.
You enter the ruins again through the entrance you made earlier.
You feel a small breeze coming from your left. Upon closer inspection, you notice small fissures in the wall of hardened lava here.
You disturb the occupants of this place!
You find something shiny covered with sooth and dust, under this crumbling table.
Your rumaging unvovers something of interest!

You are entering what appears to be a very ancient vault, or bunker. The smooth walls and columns are made from a kind of granite that you have never seen before. Numerous dust- and soot-covered plaques are nailed to the walls.

Made of some unknown alloy, the plaques bear inscriptions upon them; try as you might, you just cannot decipher the language. From the crumbling cots and beds lying about the place, you suppose that this place was used as a dormitory, or shelter.
Panting and tired from this ordeal, you then spot at the center of the dust- and soot-covered floor some sort of small objects reflecting light.
Cautiously, you brush away the dust and soot from the small objects and pick them up.
Your search reveals something interesting lying under one of the cots here.

Only too late do you see strange, floating spherical creatures silently coming out of the darkness toward you. These horrors sport numerous baleful eyes darting in every direction, their gaping, fanged maws drooling some sort of acid saliva.
"Duurax oth'naroos!" One of the creatures snarls, in a language you do not understand, just as they attack!
Upon closer inspection, you notice strange impressions in the layers of dust and sooth covering the floor here, as if something large, heavy and cubical had slid over where you are standing.
To your amazement, nothing happens!
"I'll bet ye a large mug of mead that this here wall can move!" Braggan Stoneheart exclaims, as he is stroking the wall to your right.
With every member of your party lending a hand, you all push at the wall. Not bulging at first, your sustained efforts bear fruit as the wall finally slides away from you!
"Me'll bet ye a large mug of mead that this here wall can move!" Braggan Stoneheart exclaims, as he is stroking the wall to your left.
You have stepped on a loose stone on the floor! Immediately, the wall moves once again!
Thanks to your vigilance, you notice that you were about to step on a loose tile on the floor here. Carefully, you jump over it and avoid any potential dire consequences.

You enter a strange room filled with debris from what appear to have been devices and machines, with metal wires laying all about the floor. This room is filled with columns adorned with square glass ornaments of many colors, some of them illuminated.
As you come to the conclusion that you have no idea what this room used to be for, more of those horrific floating creatures swarm in to attack, apparently waiting for your entrance!
Amidst the scraps of metal and weird wires, you find something of interest.

"Me don't know much about the people who built this place," muses Braggan Stoneheart while pensively stroking his beard, "but me can tell ye that they sure knew how to build! Even us dwarves can't build as solid and as long-lasting like these folks did!"
"By the Muses!" Riel Monsongs exclaims in awe. "Never could I imagine that such a place could exist! I must put this down in writing!"
"This place is awe-inspiring indeed!" Muses Athos. "Praise be Astrane for allowing me to see such ancient wonder, and perhaps even unravel its mysteries!"

To your dismay, more beyonders are in this room. "Zinax! Zinax! Zinax!" One of them exclaims in alarm, upon your intrusion. The largest of them turns to you: "This find is ours!" It snarls. You are surprised at being able to understand what it is saying.

Panting and tired, your attention is drawn to those strange, recurring sounds. Looking in the direction from where they seem to be coming, you see a strange circular platform of glass lying on the floor to the northeast.
A strange beam of white light rises and dissipates from the platform, the cycle coinciding with the sounds you hear.
This strange, glowing globe floats above the floor in a stationary position. The light emanating from it appears coordinated with both the sounds and the wide beam of light rising from the platform.
This floating device must be the control mechanism of the platform; however, you can't fathom how to make it work.

The largest of the beyonders is still alive, albeit near death. As its criticaly wounded body begins its death throes, the beyonder spews something from its maw, just before releasing its last breath. With disdain, you carefully pick the items up.
"It may not work properly," the large beyonder goes on, "and we may not know yet how it works, but it is ours!" At that, he and his kin attack!

As you clean the items, you realize that swallowing must be the way these foul creatures keep their prized possessions, storing them in their stomach instead of a chest. A shiver of disgust runs through you at the thought.
More beyonders join the fray!

Your spellcaster then realizes that the glass platform may be some kind of teleporting device, the workings of which remain unfathomable. Consequently, there is no way to know in advance, or figure out, where the platform would teleport someone.
Are you sure you want to step onto the glass platform?

You land in the middle of a vast desert of sand and rocks, enclosed by towering rugged mountains. A hot, scorching wind blows, the only sound heard amidst the dreary silence of this desolate landscape.
The beam of light of the platform engulfs you, as you feel your whole body tingle and your stomach turn.
Searching the cave after this clash, you find some useful items accumulated by the pyrohydras!
Sreaming with rage and fury, fire giants charge out to repel the invaders that you are!
More giants rush in!

The pass ends here, blocked by the roilling and searing lake of lava of the collapsed volcano. Despite the chocking and blinding smoke and fumes, you spot another 'shore' relatively near you, to the north of where you are standing.
But with the lake of lava between you and the other shore, how will you get there?
The climbing of your party member begins well, but soon enough loses footing on the slippery rocks, taking a hard fall down.
But thanks to your spell, your party member floats down harmlessly.
After securely fastening your rope, you all start to climb along the mountain wall to reach the other shore.
However, the activity of the volcano renders the rocks and mountain walls unstable! It doesn't take long for your fastened rope to loose its fastenings, making you fall!
But thanks to your spell, everyone floats down harmlessly.
Success! You all get to the other side safely and effortlessly.

You stumble upon a battle between a band of fire giants and a band of frost giants. Surprised at seeing frost giants around here, you see that they don't have the numbers on their side, and are hard pressed against their opponents.
Do you intervene?
Who's side to you join?
Frost giants
Fire giants

After the battle, the battered and bloodied leader of the frost giant band comes up to you: "Thank you, little ones." She says, visibly surprised that you helped them. "Our blood-enemies, the fiery ones, murdered our Highlord's son."

"He had come to meet with their Khan to discuss peace between us. Their callous murder of him increased the hatred we have for our blood-enemies. We were sent as a punitive party, but I lost many of my kin coming here, and we were thus greatly weakened."

"I will return to my Highlord to tell him that if we are to finally rid ourselves of our blood-enemies, we'll have no choice but to send huge armies to do so." With a final nod in parting, the battered and demoralized frost giants leave.

After the battle, the fire giants stay away from you, snarling and gazing upon you with much hatred and suspicion: "Begone from here!" Their leader warns. "We don't need your help, or your kind of rabble around here!"
Do you walk away?
"And we better not meet again, if you value your pitiful lives!" Snarls the fire giant leader, as you start to walk away.
"You've made your choice then, fools!" Snarls the fire giant leader, as he and his kin attack!
It would appear that today is a bad day to make choices for you ...

You realize that you are nearing a large fire giant community. Considering the hostile temper of the fire giants, you doubt you could pass through without being overwhelmed by their numbers. You would need additional help for such a feat.

Just as you approach the gates of the fire giant stronghold, a shimering disk of light appears behind you. As promised, Highlord Sesserak and his best warriors have arrived to help you. "Let us end this once and for all!" Sesserak booms.
In response, the fire giants rush out of the gates, screaming with hatred and fury at their blood-enemies!

You are shocked at the destruction the frost giants have wrought. Fire giant bodies lay all about, while their houses and compounds lay crumbling or burnt to the ground. All is silent, except for the wind and the continuous rumbling of the volcano.

You wonder if any fire giant survived this utter destruction. In any event, Highlord Sesserak and his kin are nowhere to be seen, having probably gone back to their homes, the Highlord's son murder avenged. But at what price?

"By the Gods!" Riel exclaims, shocked as much as you are. "Have we become nothing but harbingers of destruction? Is this all necessary, in order to do what's good, what's right?" He asks, shaking his head in resignation for lack of answers.
A bloodied Sesserak comes up to you after the battle: "You little ones go take care of the vermin hiding in the Khan's castle; me and my warriors will take care of the rest of them in their town!"
With a firm nod, you rush to the castle. Behind you, Sesserak and his warriors begin battling their blood-enemies anew.
These gates lie open, the doors battered and twisted.
You return in the Khan's castle.
Do you pull on this lever?
You feel slight tremors under your feet.
Lava is blocking your way!

Before you stands numerous fire giants. One among them, most likely their leader, steps forward: "We may be doomed because our blood-enemies are at our doors," he snarls, "but all of the Sword Lands will taste the power of Ssuurtuur, God of Fire!"

At that, his followers erupt in a defiant cheer. "I've unleashed the volcano and now nothing will stop it from spreading fast and far!" The leader continues, a look of madness in his red, beady eyes. "So if we pass on, let it be in the Blaze of Glory!"
At that, the fire giants make their final stand!
Bloodied and tired, you now wonder exactly by what the fire giant Khan meant by 'unleashing the volcano' ...
This is a storage room for foodstuffs. You manage to replenish your supplies.
This statue represents Ssuurtuur, God of Fire.
You find treasure!

You come into a half-finished room. Indeed, most of the wall on one side is still rock and dirt. You hear a repetitive sound coming from the southeast. From this direction, you notice strange machines connected with wires that go into a pool of lava.
Coursing the wires are flashes of electricity which run all the way into the lava pool, each flash causing the lava to belch and bubble.
The machines keep humming, sending electrical flashes into the pool of lava.
Some of the machines shut down.
Numerous tremors are coursing through the ground.
Not wishing to turn the machines on again, you leave the lever alone.

With all the machines turned off, the tremors cease and the pool of lava is no more fueled with electrical charges. You are now certain that this complex contraption was responsible for the expansion of the volcano.
This lever has been stuck in this position, most likely by the fire giant Khan. However, by pooling the strenght of all your party members, you could force it back. Do you attempt this?
Together, you manage to pull the lever up!
Suddenly, sparks come out of the lever, causing a chain reaction all the way to the machines! Before you can blink, everything blows!!!
Frost giants are standing watch here. They do not move to attack but simply nod and let you pass.
Frost giants are standing watch here. Upon seeing you, they attack!
As even more frost giants rush in to defend the gates of their stronghold, you decide that you've had enough and make a run for it.
Frost giant warriors are coming out of this compound, most likely going on patrol.

This looks like a communal compound for all frost giants. Many are eating here, or conversing with others, or bartering. Not wishing to bother them (especially since they are allowing you to walk around unharmed), you leave.
Stumbling into this cave, you see to your horror that it is the home of a small group of ice dragons! Before you can blink, you are gripped with a tremendous dragonfear!
Not happy by your intrusion, the ice dragons decide to teach you a lesson!
Panting and tired, you gleam shiny objects at the back of the cave: you have found the hoard of these ice dragons!
Thanks to your awareness, you realize that this cave is occupied by a small group of ice dragons. They have not sensed you yet. Do you seize this chance and attack?
Caught up with excitement at exploring these ancient ruins of Algaroth, you wonder if you'' find anyone -or anything- alive in here.

"Welcome, little ones." The frost giant king intones, his deep voice echoing throughout the hall. "I am Sesserak, Highlord of the frost giants of the Snow Rockies. I wish to thank you for helping my warriors, back in the accursed Volcanic Rockies."

He chuckles: "It is rare indeed that we frost giants ever see eye to eye with little ones such as you! However, considering your valiant intervention in favor of my warriors, I have decreed that you be left unbothered by anyone of my clan!"
Bowing your head politely for the Highlord's consideration, you take your leave.
What do you reply?

The Highlord chuckles: "An alliance, with little ones? Please, let's not be ridiculous! While I do appreciate what you have done for my warriors, this hardly makes you worthy of being allies with us!" At that, he dismisses you with a wave of his hand.

"Bold words indeed!" The Highlord muses, an eyebrow raised in surprise. "However, while I do appreciate what you've done for my warriors, I have yet to be proven that proper mettle match such words!" At that, he dismisses you with a wave of his hand.

The Highlord nods pensively: "No one but I desire more the extermination of those fire giants, especially after they murdered my only son!" He snarls. "However, while I appreciate what you did for my warriors, why should we help you?"

"Indeed." He continues. "I have yet to be convinced that you are trustworthy, and that you have no ulterior motives other than simply needing our help to defeat our blood-enemies once and for all!" He then chuckles: "But doubts can be remedied."

"Here is my proposition: ages long past, the evil Ice Titan Tauruseus stole a gemstone from our very first Highlord, Viborg. This stone, 'Viborg's Stone', has mystical powers which work only in the hands of a frost giant Highlord such as myself."

"With this stone, I could easily bring my whole army to the doorsteps of our blood-enemies, in an instant and without losses or fatigue! However, at the end of the fabled War of Light and Darkness, Tauruseus was imprisoned for eternity for his crimes."
"His prison lies a few leagues west and south of here. Before being imprisoned, Tauruseus was allowed to keep his most precious belongings, and unfortunately, Viborg's Stone was one of these items."

"Therefore, bring back to me Viborg's Stone, and we will indeed help you against our blood-enemies!" Appreciating your stoic reaction to this proposition, Sesserak smiles: "Here is a map to a cave which will lead you to Tauruseus' prison."
"Bring back the Stone," the Highlord says in dismissal, "and we will fight together a glorious battle that will toll the death of the fire giants!" Bowing your head respectfully, you take your leave.
"Welcome back, little ones!" Highlord Sesserak intones in greetings. "I hope you have something important to discuss, for I am quite busy right now."
The Highlord is busy discussing war plans and such with his priests and lieutenants. Not wishing to disturb him for naught, you leave.

"Have you retrieved the Stone?" The Highlord asks upon your approach. Smiling, you hand over Viborg's Stone to him. "By the Gods! You have done it! Not even our most fabled heroes managed such a feat! Truly, it is we who are not worthy to help you!"

"But help you we will." He adds in earnest. "That is, if you still need our help?" You nod in affirmative. "Then so be it!" He booms, smiling. "Let me organize my attack force. In the meantime, you should trek back to the fire giants' stronghold."

"The moment you get to the gates, I will transport my army in an instant to your side, thanks to the Stone's powers! The battle will be glorious!" As the Highlord begins his preparations for war, you take your leave with confidence.

As you enter this hall, you see a large frost giant engaged in discussions with his priests, warlocks and lieutenants. This large giant is most likely the king here. One of the forst giant guards then notices you.
"If you wish to speak with our Highlord, walk forward." He tells you, not without some harshness in his voice. "Just remember to stay on the water stones to speak before him: that is our custom!"
Not wishing to insult the frost giants and, especially, the Highlord, you decide to remain on the 'water stones' to speak before the Highlord.

You stand before a citadel made of solid crystal, as blue as the purest of ice. Despite being covered with snow and ice from countless storms and blizzards, the citadel appears as pristine as you imagine it appeared after being newly constructed.

A large archway is set at the base of this citadel. Without doors, the gap it creates allows for the wind to flow and whistle inside the stucture. Above the archway, you spot a plaque of platinum etched with symbols which you cannot decipher.

Thanks to the magic of the stone of tongues, the symbols suddenly become legible: "Herein lies Tauruseus the Cruel and Darkhearted. Woe to those who should free him; Woe to the World should he be freed".
Do you enter?
This ominous portal blocks your way. A stramge shimering field of energy covers it, probably to prevent any tampering with it.

Just as you enter this hall, two of the millennia-old statues animate, breaking the feet-thick ice covering them with a loud cracking noise. Their lifeless eyes glowing with an eery, pulsating yellow light, they advance silently toward you!
It would appear that 'someone', or 'something', wishes for this place to remain free of unwanted visitors ...
A glowing disk is lying on the floor here. Do you step on it?
You are teleported to somewhere else!
Some kind of force field is blocking your way!
A fireball is lauched from the end of this corridor, coming right your way!
At the base of this column, you find a small button. Do you push it?
The shimering force field lets you pass!
As you enter this hall, some of the columns change shape and attack you!
This glowing globe of muti-colored lights floats a few inches above the floor. Do you touch it?

"Welcome to your prison." A disembodied feminine voice intones. "You who have chosen to walk the path of darkness, whether knowingly or by mistake, are now condemned to wander these halls until you die." The globe becomes silent at that.
As you enter this hall, smoke rises from the floor. This eery smoke gradually takes shape and solidifies into horrific creatures!
A small fountain filled with water is here. Do you take some to quench your thirst?
Your search reveals a loose tile on the floor. Picking it up, you notice a small button underneath. Do you push on the button?
This ancient door of platinum-steel is hopelessly locked. You are certain would would need the proper set of keys to open it.
Hoping against hope, you try to use the brass keys you found.

As you enter this room, a huge titan stands ready to attack you: "Tauruseus the Immortal, am I! Imprisoned here have I been, for thousands of years! Finally free will I be, on this day! Stop me, no one can!" At that, he moves in for the kill!
With the force field weakened, Tauruseus can summon help ... and does!

"Me not fer liking an alliance with giants!" Mumbles Braggan, as you are leaving. "Not one bit! Me tell ye, friends: they cain't be trusted! Methinks we best keep our eyes open ... in case me's right." Finding wisdom in his words, you nod in agreement.

Thanks to the Stone of tongues, you now see that some of the swirls of light within the globe are in fact some kind of moving and swirling text, which you now can read! One line of text keeps coming over and over within the globe:

"ERROR. ERROR. TRANSPORTER UNIT CRITICAL MALFUNCTION; CPCU DISABLED; SELF-REPAIR SYSTEMS DAMAGED; VECTORING SYSTEMS OFF-LINE. ERROR. ERROR." Although most of the terms have no meaning to you, this is obviously a teleporting device ... and broken at that.

Thanks to the Stone of tongues, you can read the inscriptions of some of the plaques hanging on the walls and columns. Although most of the inscriptions remain hard to read because of wear and time, here is what some of those plaques read:

"FOOD DEPOT - SUBLEVEL 2, WING 1". "SHOWERS AND LAVATORIES - SUBLEVEL 1, WING 3". "YOU ARE HERE: CENTRAL AGORA, SUBLEVEL 1, WING 1". "TRANSPORTER ROOM - SUBLEVEL 1, WING 5". "CCPU - SUBLEVEL 1, WING 4". "ARMORY AND BARRACKS -SUBLEVEL 2, WINGS 2-8".
Although many of those terms and words have no meaning for you, you guess that this place must have been indeed some kind of large bunker complex, with most of it now buried under hardened lava.
"CENTRAL CONTROL PROCESSING UNIT". "AIR AND TEMPERATURE CONDITIONING". "ARCANIC COMMUNICATIONS". "ARCANIC SELF-REPAIR SYSTEMS". "TRANSPORTER CONTROL". "TECHNOMAGE CONSOLE". "ARCANIC WARNING SYSTEMS".

Thanks to the Stone of tongues, you can now read the inscriptions on some of the plaques hanging on the walls and columns in this junk-filled room. While most of them remain hard to read because of wear and time, here is what some of the plaques read:

Although many of those terms and words have no meaning for you, you guess that this room must have been the very heart of this strange complex, and all that junk must have been the arcane machines that controlled it all.

Seing that many lights are still blinking and flashing about these ancient, but decrepit machines, you are amazed by those Tellurians. You wonder how they could power up such machines so that power would remain in some of them after numerous millennia.

The Ocean of Ukkor extends before you, with water extending everywhere without land in sight. To the far east is Umaldyr, at the end of Ukkor's Ocean. Knowing this represents quite a long voyage, do you set sail for Umaldyr?
After an uneventful trip, you finally have sight of a shoreline to your east.
After an uneventful trip (aside from high waves which were unsettling), you finally have sight of a shoreline to your east.

As your trip begins, you notice dark clouds looming on the horizon.  Sure enough, your voyage is punctuated by raging thunder storms, with wailing winds and rocky waters! But you all remain safe and sound, as you finally spot a shoreline to your east.

The Ocean of Ukkor extends before you, with water extending everywhere without land in sight. To the far west is Lantharond, at the other end of Ukkor's Ocean. Knowing this represents quite a long voyage, do you set sail for Lantharond?

After an uneventful trip, you finally have sight of a shoreline to your west.
