Which is you final destination?
After an uneventful trip, you finally have sight of Coral Towers' shoreline to the southwest.
After an uneventful trip (aside from high waves which were unsettling), you finally have sight of Coral Towers' shoreline to the southwest.

As your trip begins, you notice dark clouds looming on the horizon.  Sure enough, your voyage is punctuated by raging thunder storms and rocky waters! But you remain safe and sound, as you finally spot your destination to the southwest.
This is an ancient lighthouse, standing a good nine or ten stories high! Do you climb the stairs to the top?

Standing at the top of the lighthouse, you can see for leagues to the north, being able to spy features on the northern island of Umaldyr. You wish you had thought of bringing parchment sheets, so you could have made a quick map ...

Standing at the top of the lighthouse, you can see for leagues to the north, being able to spy features on the northern island of Umaldyr. Grabbing one of your parchment sheets, you quickly draw yourself a map!
Standing at the top of the lighthouse, you enjoy the great view and the rich aromas of the sea.

Standing at the top of the lighthouse, you can see for leagues to the southwest, being able to spy features on the southern island of Umaldyr. You wish you had thought of bringing parchment sheets, so you could have made a quick map ...

Standing at the top of the lighthouse, you can see for leagues to the southwest, being able to spy features on the southern island of Umaldyr. Grabbing one of your parchment sheets, you quickly draw yourself a map!

You come into a large, windy valley. Facing you are what appear to be millennia-old ruins, judging from the thick and enveloping layers of sand and dust covering them. The ruins protrude from the desolate ground of sand and rocks covering the area.

From the way the ruins appear to have been buried long ago, you guess that a whole city must be lying under this desolate valley. Intrigued, you venture forth in order to find an entrance which, hopefully, would allow you to explore this buried city.
Creatures have taken refuge inside these ruins!
Searching inside these ruins, you cannot find any opening of passage leading further into the buried city.

As you walk along this small river, you see numerous beastmen and women busy at farming crops, picking fruit, or carrying water. You spot further to the north the wooden gates of their village, with a good number of warriors on watch.

You are intrigued by these beast-looking folks: indeed, they wear simple robes or tunics, without any adornments. Children play and laugh alongside their busy parents. All in all, these communal folks appear to live simple, peaceful lives.

A few of the warriors standing on watch for the security of their kin have seen you. Many of them rush to you, their weapons at the ready, while the alarmed families rush back to their village. Obviously, these folks feel threatened by your presence.
What do you do?
Stay
Run
Not particulalrly inclined to fight these peaceful folks, you run away from their excited warriors and leave them be.

Shouting angrily, the warriors run toward you with their weapons raised, only to stop at about a dozen yards from you. They are obviously confused by the fact that they did not scare you into running away, and yet you did not draw your weapons.
As the warriors keep rushing in your direction, what posture do you decide to adopt?

"Oorgh'ak sanake?" One of the warriors asks you, obviously a leader of some sort. Not understanding a word of what he is saying, you look confused and unsure. "Azar'ak san isha?!?" He asks more firmly. You shrug to show him that you do not understand.
"DENAR BAL ISHA!" The leader yells with anger, raising his spear in an obvious gesture of ushing you away. His warriors repeat his words angrily, making the same gesture.
Knowing that you are not wanted, you decide to walk away and leave them be, promising yourself to find a way to communicate with these folks.
More beastmen attack!
Seeing even more beastmen rushing your way, you decide that you have had enough of this, and choose the better part of valor.
On high alert, the beastmen warriors have seen you coming back. Immediately, numerous warriors rush to attack you!
Seeing you draw your weapons, the warriors shout louder and step up their charge to meet you head on!
"Me said: who are ye and why are ye here! Answer or we'll attack ye!" The leader snarls. Thanks to the magic of the Stone of tongues finally kicking in, you can now understand their language!

You try to reassure them by stating that you are explorers, intrigued by this strange land and its people. "Explorers, eh?" The leader replies, somewhat doubtful. "Very well, then. Ye come with us to see our Shaman-King!"
Nodding in acceptance, you walk forward, with the warriors surrounding you as a guarding escort.
As you continue your march inside the village, folks gather around to see you, looking upon you with a mixture of curiosity and fear.

You are finally brought to the largest hut of the village, its dried mud walls adorned with flowers and vines. Out of it comes a middle-aged beast man. Grey-haired yet built like a warrior despite his age, his dark eyes betray a sparkling intelligence.

"Visitors!" He exclaims upon seeing you, smiling. His voice is deep, yet smooth and gentle. "Thank you for bringing them to me, valiant warriors. You may leave us now, for we have much to speak about." Seeing his folks' hesitation, he ushers them away.

"Now go, me said!" He chides them gently. "Nothing to fear from them strangers." Finally placated and convinced, the folks and warriors leave. Seeing your own look of confusion, he chuckles. "How amusing, that ye be as confused as me own simple people!"

Inviting you to sit down, he serves you goblets of succulent fruit juices. "Me name's Ogarond." He begins. "Shaman-King of the Astur Tribe, We of the True Faith. Our name is just, for we have never forgotten our history, never forsaken our birthright."

"Ages long on," he continues, "our ancestors looked like ye, fair of body and of mind. This vast desert was once lush with green and water, its weather fair and warm. And our ancestors lived in fabled Asturia, now the ruins lying east of our village."

"Then there was a Great War, and our ancestors fought with the people of Algaroth, which is also in ruins far southwest of here. But the Gods disapproved of this war, and so they brought upon both peoples the Invoqued Devastation!"

Ogarond sighs, shaking his head. "Rains of fire and exploding rocks fell upon both peoples, destoying the two fabled cities. The waters became poison, and the green withered away. But the curse of the Gods spread to the following generations."

"For those few that survived the Invoqued Devastation bore this terrible curse, slowly transforming their children, and their children's children, into beastly, difformed shells. And so it remains today, as we all still bear the mark of this curse."

"As the ages went by," Ogarond continues, "the knowledge held by our ancestors was lost to the Void of Forgetfullness. But the first ones of our Tribe never forgot history, passing it on so that we never again anger the Gods with our arrogance."

"As Shaman-King, it is me sacred duty to tell the history to our children, as me have done so with you today. But now, me will speak to you of recent history." He replenishes your drinks before continuing:

"The survivors of the Invoqued Devastation grew in numbers again, and these separated into different tribes, the peoples becoming more and more savage with each generation. All, except for our tribe. The others grew jealous of us, of our knowledge."

"And so our Tribe has ever suffered the harassment and wrath of these other savage tribes. We often weep for them, because they will never remember history, farming, or peace. They are lost to the curse of the Gods, and be so forever."

"Maybe because we chose not to forget, or maybe because the Gods took pity on the ancestors of our Tribe, we were chosen as Keepers of the Pearl of Asturia. This sacred relic is the key which allows entrance to the sacred grounds of fabled Asturia."

"Ye see, the way to its ruins is guarded by ancient guardians, the Stone Towers. Any trespasser will be destroyed by them. But those who have the Pearl of Asturia are allowed to go through, so that they may gaze upon the truth of history, of Asturia."

Ogarond sighs. "Two full moons past, the Pearl of Asturia was taken from us, when the savage Tribe of Murdor raided us. This tribe is strong, and rules many weaker tribes. Their Shaman-King, Ulh'Garath, is feared throughout the desert lands."

Ogarond smiles. "Auguries foretold me of yer coming. Me know that ye are searching for something with power, although ye may not be aware yet that ye are searching for it. But me know that ye'll want to explore Asturia, where ye'll find that power."

Intrigued by his words, you listen with increased interest: "But for ye to explore fabled Asturia, ye'll need the Pearl. So, me make a nice deal with ye: get the Pearl back from the Tribe of Murdor, use it to explore the ruins, then bring it back to us!"

You nod in acceptance of his fair offer. "Good!" Replies Ogarond, happy at your decision. "Me now will give you a map that shows where the Tribe of Murdor lives." Scrounging through piles of parchment sheets, he whips up a map which he hands to you.
"In the meantime," Ogarond continues, "ye can of course wander freely in our village. Now me must ask ye to leave, for me is tiring and needs me sleep." With a polite nod, you leave Ogarond's hut.
Ogarond is nowhere to be seen about his hut. Figuring he must be with his people in the fields or somewhere else, you get on your way.

"Ye are back!" Ogarond exclaims. "Does this means?" Smiling, you produce the Pearl and hand it to him. "Thank ye!" He mumbles, tears of joy falling on his sun-caked cheeks. "Now," he goes on, "we can continue our duty as Keepers of the Sacred Pearl!"
As his people gather around him to shout their joy at the Pearl's return, you walk away with the satisfaction of another great deed accomplished.
Warriors on watch eye you with a mixture of curiousity and suspicion, but you are otherwise left alone and allowed to pass through the village's gates.

You enter a large, desolate valley. You spot in the distance huge towers of weathered obsidian stone. Aligned in two rows of four to leave a wide berth between the two rows, you judge from where you stand that each tower stands about 900 feet high!
You come upon a huge dune of sand and rock, sprawling at the foot of the mountains. You estimate that this dune stands about three stories high.

After blowing on the horn as hard and as long as you can, you feel the wind slowly picks up speed and strenght, until it becomes a veritable tornado centered on the large dune! At the same time, the horn blows up into shards!

Although short-lived, the tempest of sand throws you from where you stand. The debris settles, uncovering cyclopean ruins from their sandy resting place. The desert then becomes quiet once more, only to be punctuated by the prevailing breeze.
The cyclopean ruins loom silently over you. Do you enter?
This looks like some ancient temple dedicated to a God unknown to you. Although eerily quiet, something stirs in the darkness the moment you walk further inside!
Something has taken up residence here!
You find a few items left over in this secret cache.
Your search reveal a small button at the base of this ancient altar. Do you push this button?

As you enter this chapel, you see strange, floating spherical creatures silently coming out of the darkness toward you. These horrors sport numerous baleful eyes darting in every direction, their gaping, fanged maws drooling some sort of acid saliva.
"Intruders!" One of the creatures snarls, understanding their language because of the Stone of tongues, just as they attack!
Amidst the rubble here, you find something of interest.
More beyonders have taken up residence here!
You are certain that you could rest in this secret room: you might as well take a breather!
You leave the safe room.

You come into a corridor made of solid steel. Neither the walls or the floor show any signs of rusting or weathering by time. The ceiling, also of this 'stainless' steel, is adorned by circular plaques of glass that, amazingly, glow with light!
Tons of rubble and rocks have blocked off the corridor at this point.

Seeing that many lights are blinking and flashing about these ancient, but decrepit machines, you are amazed by the Macremians. You wonder how they could empower such machines so that power would still remain in some of them after numerous millennia.

You enter another large room, also filled with junk and wires. To your horror, numerous beyonders are here, apparently attending court to a larger beyonder who is resting on something made of metal junk that looks like a throne.

"Oloor agh anak?" The large beyonder snarls at you. Unfortunately, you cannot understand a word of what he is saying. "Daruus erkon? Erkon?" He continues, as he rises from his 'throne'. "INAXYS!!!" He shouts finally, as his followers attack!

"Who dares violate our domain?" The large beyonder snarls at you. "Are you fools? Are you?" He continues, as he rises from his 'throne'. "DESTROY THESE INTRUDERS!!!" He shouts finally, as his followers attack!
You find a hiden cache under the beyonder's throne!
A tribe of beastmen has taken up residence here: they are not too happy with your intrusion!
Rumaging through the cave, you find a few interesting items.
You run into a patrol of beastmen!

"Oh, before I forget," he adds, "remember to bring back the icon of Dianchuur to the Lord Paladine." He chuckles at your surprise. "I sensed you possessed it." He replies cryptically, with a smile. At that, you take your leave.
"Oh, before I forget," he adds, "remember to bring back the icon of Dianchuur to the Lord Paladine." He chuckles at your surprise. "I sensed you possessed it." He replies cryptically, with a smile.
You nod in feigned acceptance, despite the fact that you already have the Pearl. Cautiously, you prefer to wait things out and weight your options before handing back the Pearl to him.

"Good!" Replies Ogarond, happy at your apparent acceptance of his offer. "Me now will give you a map that shows where the Tribe of Murdor lives." Scrounging through piles of parchment sheets, he whips up a map which he hands to you.
Numerous beastmen are standing watch at the entrance of this cave!
This cave leads to a deeper underground complex. Do you go deeper within?
This is a patch of mushrooms which look edible and very tasty. These would make excellent rations for your travels. Do you pick some?

Since this home of the Murdor is favored enough to allow the growth of such a rich source of food, you begin to understand how this tribe of beastmen was able to become so powerful. Indeed, they would have a much less need to fight for food.
And less need to scour the desert wastes outside to hunt or gather foodstuffs. With such superior nourishment, the tribe can raise healthier and stronger children.
This quiet pool of fresh mineral water is continually fed by a deeper underground source. Do you take some water for your travels?

Since this home of the Murdor is favored enough to host such a plentiful source of water, you begin to understand how this tribe of beastmen was able to become so powerful. Indeed, they would have no need to forage or fight for water.
As you enter this large cavern, you come face to face with the whole of the tribe living here. Having been alerted by the battle outside, they were waiting and ready for your intrusion!
Panicked by your superiority, the rest of the beastmen rush to the outside, fleeing for their lives!
Beastmen of sterner stuff make a stand at this cave entrance!
As you enter this smaller cavern, you see a large, brutish beastman standing menacingly, safely surrounded by other tough-looking beastmen. Obviously the king of this tribe.

As you enter this smaller cavern, you see a large, brutish beastman standing menacingly, safely surrounded by other tough-looking beastmen. Obviously, this must be the infamous shaman-king Ulh'Garath!
Standing behind the beastmen, you see to your shock and horror a psi-warrior! With alarm, you wonder why the Overlords would be involved with this tribe of beastmen.
Standing behind the beastmen, you see a strangely clad warrior! With alarm, you wonder what he is doing here, and who -or what- he is exactly.
"Me and me men kill ye, because ye be enemies of me friend here, so he says!" Snarls the king. At that, they attack you!
"Jeroos do'narak, haruush!" Snarls the king, as you are not able to understand his words. Nonetheless, they attack you!

Panting and tired, you spot a letter nestled within the armor of the psi-knight. Picking it up, you read it: "To: Sub-commander Hashok; I commend you on what you have accomplished so far. If, as you say, the Pearl is the key to Asturia,

it is therefore imperative that you manipulate these brutes you have befriended to accompany you in an expedition to those ruins. I suspect you would need them as canon fodder. Remember your main objective: you must find the power stone,

if it is buried there. If, after extensive search, you do not find it, then we can only assume that its location is in those macremian ruins near our base of operations. However, as you know, we have yet to find a way of entry there.
In any event, I wish you success! Signed: High Praetor Primus, First Speaker of the Inner Council". It would seem that you have yet more food for thought ...
Some of these items were obviously gifts brought by the psi-knight to befriend the tribe.
A sign hanging above the door of this little shop reads: "Sfirnillim's General Store". Do you enter?
A sign hanging above the door of this little shop reads: "Brivznafin's Little Shop of Curious Wonders". Do you enter?
You then hear someone nearby moan and groan with pain.

"What of the shadow elves?" Demands Scyrella. Storm raises his hands to plead innocence: "Something I am not involved with, I assure you! Apparently, these Overlords make alliances with whom they please, and without consulting their other 'allies'."

"I assure you," the Warlord continues with a mollified tone of voice, "that I have no more desire of associating myself with these foul shadow elves than being a vassal of these shifty Overlords." Scyrella nods firmly, seemingly satisfied by this.

You then turn to Naryl: "I sense no treachery from him." She states, as if having known the question you were about to ask her. "Although my principles make me ill at ease in such a bargain, my primary objective remains the defeat of the Inner Council."

"Well, me say this stinks!" Snarls Braggan Stoneheart. Gathering his belongings, he walks up to Storm: "Me warn ye: stay away from Stonegate and Gnomilar." He intones menacingly to the Warlord, before walking away.
Storm smiles cruelly: "Let him go." He muses. "As long as the dwarves remain out of our affairs, I will be content."
You negotiate the Western pass, which leads to the Western lands and Sharranth.

"Ah, welcome, welcome!" Exclaims Jhalor, while warmly clasping your hands. "Thank you for coming, for we have much to speak about." After showing you to comfortable chairs, Jhalor settles down on one of his own.

"Congratulations for what you have accomplished so far!" The High Commander exclaims. "I wanted to speak with you about the war and the woes of the High Council, but now many of those things have become moot ... so, less for us to worry about, eh?"

He chuckles at that. "Well, first and foremost I wished to offer you the help of the knighthood of the Flame ... the kind of help that I was fortunate enough to provide myself last year, when the first three Overlords were defeated!" He winks at that.

"How I wish I could join you!" Jhalor exclaims, wistfully. You take the chance to congratulate him for being confirmed as High Commander by the Conclave of the Knighthood of the Flame. Blushing, he shakes his head slowly.

Frost giant warriors prevent your passage. "Our Highlord is busy, little ones." One of them intones. "He shouldn't be bothered." With a shrug, you walk away. You wonder if you have overstayed your welcome with the Frost giants.
Frost giants are standing watch here. They simply nod and let you pass.

The pass ends here, blocked by the roilling and searing lake of lava of the collapsed volcano. Despite the chocking and blinding smoke and fumes, you spot another 'shore' relatively near you, to the south of where you are standing.
Numerous shadow elf warriors are standing watch here.
You are allowed to pass unbothered.
"Nashi al'aris, 'ro linas!" One of them tells you, as the others eye you suspiciously. Not understanding a word of their language, what do you do?
Back away
Use force
Wisely, you back away as the shadow elf warriors look upon you with scorn.
More shadow elves join the fray!
Drawing your weapons, you rush forward!
Seeing even more shadow elf warriors rushing to defend these battlements, you choose the better part of valor and leave things well enough alone.
"Passage will cost you 25 gold pieces for each one of you!" One of them tells you, as the others eye you suspiciously. What do you do?
Pay
Don't pay
Handing over the money, the gate are open and you are allowed to pass.
Without enough money to pay, you decide to back away.
Instead of paying, what do you do?
Shadow elves on watch eye you suspiciously, but you are allowed to pass unmolested.
"GNASH UT! GNASH UT!" One of the warriors yells in alarm, pointing to you, as you struggle to understand what he is saying. Immediately, they attack!
You decide that next time, you should shed your shadow dwarf disguises before approaching shadow elves ... and vice versa.
"Shadow dwarf raid! Shadow dwarf raid!" One of the warriors yells in alarm, pointing to you. Immediately, they attack!
These battlements are crumbling and in ruins.
You wonder what ever happened here.
A large web is covering this area. The strands are thick and appear quite adhesive. What do you want to do?
Run through
You get trapped by the web! Try as you might, your movement is slowed to a crawl. And to make things worse, the creators of this eerie web come to investigate!
With relief, you find that the clash has rendered the web to bits.

You find the body of a shadow dwarf here. From the state of decomposition, you guess that he died a few weeks ago. His body and limbs have been mangled and shredded, probably by some huge predatory creature.

This twisted statue of obsidian bears the likeness of a monstruous spider. Underneath the spider, a magical fire glows bright and hot. To your horror, crimson blood seems to be oozing out of this unholy statue.
Suddenly, the magical fire expands to engulf all near the unholy relic!
Thanks to your magical disguises, the fire mistakes you as shadow elves and attempts to heal you!
Protectors of the relic appear!!!
The magical fire lashes out at you!
The magical fire attempts to heal the shadow elves among your party.

You find the body of an earth gnome here. From the state of decomposition, you guess that he died a few weeks ago. His body and limbs have been mangled and shredded, probably by some huge predatory creature.

From all appearances, this millennia-old temple in ruins was once dedicated to Erond, God of Knowledge and Thought.  You can't even begin to guess how it ended being buried within this cave.  Do you go inside?
The millennia-old temple of Erond, God of Knowledge and Thought, still stands here. Do you go inside?
Rubble is hopelessly blocking the secret door you had found here, the last time you visited this old temple.

"I AM THE ORACLE OF EROND", the deep, baritone voice booms, enounciating each word slowly,  "I KNOW WHAT IS, WHAT WAS, AND WHAT WILL BE. AS WELL I KNOW THE PATH WHICH YOU WALK ON, EVEN IF YOU DO NOT REALIZE IT. HEAR NOW MY WORDS AND HEED THEIR MEANING."

As you enter this chamber, a mysterious apparition rises from the well lying at the center of the floor. Ominous and awe-inspiring, the being looms before you. After scrutinizing each one of your party with its unfathomable eyes, the apparition speaks:

"TECHNOMAGES OF THE FORGOTTEN TELLURIAN EMPIRE CREATED MANY WONDERS. AS ANY FOOLISH MORTALS, TOO MANY OF THEM WERE USED FOR DEATH AND DESTRUCTION. BUT A FEW COULD HAVE BEEN USED TO UNITE MORTALS, INSTEAD OF FOSTERING DISTRUST AND HATRED."

"SUCH WAS THE CASE OF THE STONE OF TONGUES, WHICH ALLOWS ITS POSSESSOR TO UNDERSTAND ANY LANGUAGE. SEEK THIS STONE IN THE CRADDLE OF TELLURIAN CIVILIZATION THAT LIES NEAREST TO YOUR CURRENT CENTER OF INTEREST: IT WILL OPEN MANY OPPORTUNITIES FOR YOU."

"SO HAVE I SPOKEN; IT IS UP TO YOU, FOOLISH MORTALS BUT FAVORED BY THE GODS, TO HEED MY WORDS. I SHALL SPEAK OF NOTHING ELSE UNTIL YOU POSSESS THIS KEY OF OPPORTUNITY AND OF FACILITY FOR YOUR FUTURE TRAVAILS." At that, the Oracle returns to the Beyond.

"A WOLF IN A SHEEP'S CLOTHING IS BEST FOUND WHEN CONFRONTED BY THE SHEEP IT IS TRYING TO IMITATE. FIND THE SHEEP, AND YOU SHALL KNOW WHO IS THE WOLF. THAT IS THE CASE OF THE DISEASE CURRENTLY CRIPPLING PROUD TANIRITH. BUT WHERE IS THE SHEEP, YOU ASK?"

"THE SHEEP WILL BE FOUND PRISONER OF THE CLAWS OF DEATH, ALLOWING THE WOLF FREE REIGN. SEEK DEEP WITHIN THE DARKNESS UNDER THE CITY, AND YOU SHALL FIND THE CLAWS OF DEATH, AND THUS THE SHEEP. THEN WILL THE WOLF IS FOUND, AND THEN CAN IT BE KILLED."

"SO HAVE I SPOKEN; IT IS UP TO YOU, FOOLISH MORTALS BUT FAVORED BY THE GODS, TO HEED MY WORDS. I SHALL SPEAK OF NOTHING ELSE UNTIL YOU HAVE FOUND BOTH THE WOLF AND THE SHEEP." At that, the Oracle returns to the Beyond.

"THREE WOLVES THERE ARE, WORKING UNDER THE MASTER OF THE HUNT. ONE WOLF YOU HAVE ALREADY FOUND AND DEFEATED. A SECOND ONE HIDES WITHIN THE HEART OF THE DRAGON, KILLING IT SLOWLY TO FURTHER THE ENDS OF THE MASTER OF THE HUNT. BUT TO DEFEAT THIS WOLF,
An invisible barrier prevents your passage! At the same time, you hear a booming, outwordly voice: "BEGONE, FOR YOU HAVE CHOSEN A PATH NOT FAVORED BY THE GODS. THEY WILL NOT HELP YOU."

YOU MUST FIRST FIND THE KIN OF THE DRAGON'S HEART, HIMSELF AT THE MERCY OF THE SAPPHIRE DEATH WHICH, CONVENIENTLY, HIDES WITHIN BHALAAL'S TEMPLE. FIND THE KIN, AND HE SHALL LEAD YOU TO THE KEY; IN TURN, THE KEY WILL LEAD YOU TO THE ORB: THEN YOU SHALL BE

ABLE TO FACE THE SECOND WOLF. SO HAVE I SPOKEN; IT IS UP TO YOU, FOOLISH MORTALS BUT FAVORED BY THE GODS, TO HEED MY WORDS. I SHALL SPEAK OF NOTHING ELSE UNTIL YOU HAVE DEFEATED THIS WOLF." At that, the Oracle returns to the Beyond.

"TWO WOLVES DOWN, BUT A THIRD ONE REMAINS TO DO THE BIDDING OF THE MASTER OF THE HUNT. THIS WOLF DOES NOT HIDE ITSELF, NOR IS SPORTING ANY GUISES. HE IS SIMPLY ENJOYING THE HOSPITALITY OF THE SHADOW ELVEN CENTER OF POWER, FROM WHERE HE MANIPULATES HIS

MANY PUPPETS; AND NO GREATER ONE HE HAS WITHIN HIS THRALL THAN THE WICKED MATRON OF THE RULING HOUSE OF NAAZ'TZARANEEN. DESCEND TO THE BOWELS OF THE EARTH, AND THERE YOU SHALL FIND THE SHADOW ELVES, AND THEN THE THIRD WOLF. BUT BEWARE THE DWARVES OF THE

SHADOWS, FOR THEY AIM ONLY TO KILL AND DESTROY. SO HAVE I SPOKEN; IT IS UP TO YOU, FOOLISH MORTALS BUT FAVORED BY THE GODS, TO HEED MY WORDS. I SHALL SPEAK OF NOTHING ELSE UNTIL YOU HAVE FOUND THIS THIRD WOLF." At that, the Oracle returns to the Beyond.

"THREE WOLVES YOU HAVE DEFEATED. ALTHOUGH THREE OTHERS REMAIN UNSEEN AND UNMET, IT IS TO THE MASTER OF THE HUNT THAT YOU MUST TURN YOUR ATTENTION. BUT BEWARE: HE IS NOT WHAT HE SEEMS. HE IS NOT ONE, BUT TWO. TWO MINDS, ONE BODY. ONE MORTAL CONSCIENCE,

ONE NEAR-IMMORTAL ESSENCE. IT IS THIS PARASITIC ENTITY WHICH IS THE TRUE ENEMY, AND WHICH HAS ALWAYS BEEN. ALL YOU HAVE ACCOMPLISHED IN TRUTH MEANS NOTHING TO THIS BEING. ITS WOLVES WERE DISTRACTIONS, ENACTING SECONDARY SCHEMES WHICH IT DOES NOT REALLY

NEED. BE CAREFUL TO DO ITS BIDDING UNWITTINGLY, FOR ALL WILL BE LOST ... AND THEN THE MIND LORDS SHALL RETURN FOR THE FIRST TIME YESTERDAY, RETURN FOR THE FIRST TIME TODAY, AND RETURN FOR THE FIRST TIME TOMORROW. GONE FOREVER, ALWAYS BACK."

"SO HAVE I SPOKEN; IT IS UP TO YOU, FOOLISH MORTALS BUT FAVORED BY THE GODS, TO HEED MY WORDS. I HAVE DONE THE BIDDING OF THE GODS, AND THUS I SHALL SPEAK NO MORE." At that, the Oracle returns to the Beyond.
An invisible barrier prevents your passage!

This village lies in ruins. From the discarded weapons and some skeletal remains lying around and about, this place was once a dogre village ... which must have been pillaged many months ago. You wonder who -or what- was responsible for this destruction.
The dogre village you decimated last year lies in ruins, apparently abandonned for quite a while by the few dogre survivors you left alive.

You find the body of a kobold here. From the state of decomposition, you guess that he died a few weeks ago. His body and limbs have been mangled and shredded, probably by some huge predatory creature.
Earth gnome guards are standing watch here. "If ye don't have proper business with our king, then ye best begone!" One of them intones.

Many earth gnome exploratory parties, merchant bands or warrior patrol come and go through the gates of Svirfnilbdome. Numerous guards are standing watch at the battlements, ever ready for an invasion by their underearth rivals.
This military outpost appears abandoned.
Apparently, this drow military outpost has not been reoccupied since your last 'visit'.
Surely, you don't think you could enter there with the wailsrondese contingent along with you?
You tell your warband captain to make camp outside until you pick them up later. With a salute, he goes about ordering his men.
Your warband is waiting for you, ready to march out again.
Belrion walks up to you: "We should not be wasting time here! Let us go to our true target and be done with this!"

Not wishing to waste precious time, you decide against sailing straight south to the Pirate Isles ... After all, the pirates have been rather quiet lately, and thus do not represent any immediate problem.

Not wishing to waste precious time, you decide against sailing straight west to the Pirate Isles ... After all, the pirates have been rather quiet lately, and thus do not represent any immediate problem.
At the end of this cave, you find a false rock made of wood. The rock appear to be attached to some sort of mechanism. Do you pull on the false rock?
A section of the wall before you moves.
This secret doors leads deeper underground.
One of your party members was not paying attention to where he or she was putting a foot down: stepping on a stone, your party member slips and falls down with much noise!
Just as you enter this cave, a powerful magical spell is unleashed upon you!
Reeling from this attack, you llok up to see your assailant: a large female emerald dragon. The sight of her forces you to fight a terrible dragonfear gnawing at your guts!
Obviously warned by your noisy approach, the emerald dragon now attacks!
Jewel Widow summons help!
As you enter this cavern, you find a large female emerald dragon asleep. Do you attack her?
You find Jewel Widow's hoard!

You arrive before huge, ancient gates of solid platinum. The battlements, made of obsidian, are adorned with various bas-reliefs of spiders, demons and shadow elves. In fact, numerous shadow elf warriors are standing watch along the battlements.
Stepping before you, Zeerz Nys'Raeneen displays a crest to the warriors standing before the gates. Upon seeing the crest, they all bow respectfully as the gates are opened, allowing you to pass.

"I told you that my house is the ruling house of our city." Zeerz whispers to you as you all cross the gates. "Flashing my house crest opens doors easily here; being a noble priestess of the house of Nys'Raeneen, as I am, demands and gets subservience."
Flashing the crest in your possession, the gate guards are at first suprised by this. After quick discussions among themselves, they finally open the gates and allow you safe passage.
"Begone from here, you mongrels!" One of the gate guards snarls. "Your kind is not welcome in Naaz'Tzaraneen, except as slaves!" Do you do as this guard says?
"Slaves you'll be, then!" The guard yells, as the shadow elf warriors attack!
"Zynaas hashtuut!" One of the gate guards snarls. "Bylalh ghah narash!" He adds, with obvious disdain toward you. Not understanding a word, what do you do?
Leave
"Januush eth vanaas!" The guard yells, as the shadow elf warriors attack!

"Me'll be a dumb dogre if this wall is normal!" Mumbles Braggan, strocking his beard while peering at the rocky wall to the west. Looking closer as well, you realize that it is an illusion hiding a cave entrance!
Thanks to your awareness, you realize that the rocky wall to the west is an illusion hiding a cave entrance!
A large steel plaque hangs above the gates here: "Slave Pens".
A large steel plaque hangs above the gates here. Unfortunately, you cannot make out what it means. Seeing numerous shadow elf warriors around and about the place, you walk away.
This must be where the surviving amazons are kept.
"My sisters are kept here by these foul creatures!" Snarls Scyrella Silverspear. "Let us seize this chance and free them now!"
"Why aren't we going in? We have to free my sisters from these foul creatures!" Protests an incensed Scyrella.

With much diplomacy and quiet, logical argumentation, you try to convince Scyrella that you should not rush into this, but instead gather as much information before acting. Although frustrated, the amazon Queen finally agrees with you.

"We have no time to waste." Intones Zeerz Nys'Raeneen. "Purging my noble house must remain the primary objective! Furthermore, accomplishing this will likely solve other problems." Upon her insistence, you give up.

"I have pledged that the amazons will be freed once my house is purged!" Adds Zeerz Nys'Raeneen. "Therefore, we do not need to waste time here!" In response, Scyrella throws her a murderous look. Obviously, the amazon Queen doubts such a pledge.

This is a retractable bridge, which can be extended to the small island at the center of this lake. You notice numerous figures walking about shoddy huts of mud on this island. These must be the slave pens then.
"Go about your ways." A shadow elf warrior tells you. "Go speak with the Master Slaver if you wish to purchase slaves." With a nod, you leave.
This dark, twisted tower stands a good six to eight stories high. From the numerous shadow elf warriors coming in and out, this must be a guard tower heavily manned.

"Stay back!" Zeerz Nys'Raeneen warns you. "This is an altar dedicated to our Goddess Lloth, or Tlarantale as you call her. Any one that is not a shadow elf that touches it, dies!" Wisely, you back away from this foul statue-altar.
Kobolds ambush you!

"Me'll be a dumb goblin if this wall is normal!" Mumbles Braggan, strocking his beard while peering at the rocky wall behind those shadow dwarf huts. Looking closer as well, you realize that it is an illusion hiding a cave entrance!
Thanks to your awareness, you realize that the rocky wall behind these shadow dwarf huts is an illusion hiding a cave entrance!

"Me'll be a dumb troll if this wall is normal!" Mumbles Braggan, strocking his beard while peering at the rocky wall to the north. Looking closer as well, you realize that it is an illusion hiding a cave entrance!
Thanks to your awareness, you realize that the rocky wall to the north is an illusion hiding a cave entrance!
"Khash inal vanuush" A shadow elf warrior tells you. "Lingha eh'nysh jallil dys." Not understanding a word, you nod politely nonetheless and leave.

These are the gates of a large estate. Beyond the battlements, you notice guard towers, houses and a large building. Its architecture as twisted and nightmarish as all the buildings of Naaz'Tzaraneen, its size indicate that this could be a noble house.
A large golden plaque hangs on the steel doors of the gates: "House Meer'Golorh".
"Let us not waste time here." Zeerz Nys'Raeneen interjects. "Besides, Meer'Golorh is but the 7th out of eight noble houses, and thus rather weak and of no use to our cause."

"What is your purpose here?" A shadow elf warrior calls out to you. "You best be gone fast if you do not have the proper credentials!" He warns, as other guards chuckle with malice, anticipating some 'fun' at your expense.
Flashing the proper crest for this ruling house, the guards fall silent and open the gates to allow you passage.
Shadow elf guards let you pass.
A large golden plaque hangs on the steel doors of the gates. Unfortunately, you cannot fathom its meaning.
A large golden plaque hangs on the steel doors of the gates: "House El'Carlaas".
"Let us not waste time here." Zeerz Nys'Raeneen interjects. "Besides, El'Carlaas is but the 8th out of eight noble houses, and thus rather weak and of no use to our cause."
A large golden plaque hangs on the steel doors of the gates: "House Bel'Yraaz".
"Let us not waste time here." Zeerz Nys'Raeneen interjects. "Besides, Bel'Yraaz is but the 5th out of eight noble houses, and thus relatively weak and of no use to our cause."
A large golden plaque hangs on the steel doors of the gates: "House Raz'Narath".
"Let us not waste time here." Zeerz Nys'Raeneen interjects. "Besides, Raz'Narath maybe the 4th out of eight noble houses, it is nonetheless relatively weak and of no use to our cause."
A large golden plaque hangs on the steel doors of the gates: "House No'Lareen".
"Let us not waste time here." Zeerz Nys'Raeneen interjects. "Besides, No'Lareen is but the 6th out of eight noble houses, and therefore rather weak and of no use to our cause."
Numerous sharranthine warriors are on watch at the town's gates.
Flashing your royal seal of Sharranth, the gates are opened and you are allowed to pass through.

"Stop!" One of the guards warns you. "Without the proper credentials, adventurers such as you are not allowed entry here, even if allied with our cause! So has decreed our Invincible King and Warlord!"
Sharranthine warriors on watch nod politely and let you pass through the gates.
"If only ... " He rasps, grasping weakly your hand. "But .. why ... this ... destruction?" At that, Belrion releases his last breath and passes away.
From where you stand, you see what remains of the castle ... with a heavy heart, you walk further toward the ruins.

The smoking rubbles of Lord Pyre's castle lay in front of you, their silence accusingly revealing your treachery. Was this then, the preordained fate of the city? To be sacked, and then condemned by history to disappear under earth and dust, forgotten?
You enter the foreboding mansion.

You come into a hall, its obsidian walls adorned with nightmarish scenes of spiders eating flesh and shadow elves slaughtering other surface races. Numerous fire wells are about this hall, along with demon statues and twisted columns of dark basalt.

Of course, a large altar-statue of Tlarantale stand proudly at the end of this hall, blood from a freshly-sacrificed slave still trickling along its base. Only the glow of fluorescent fungi illuminates this dark place.

Too taken by this sick and twisted decor, you finally realize that this hall is occupied ... by all too many shadow elves. "Who are you?" Demands an outraged shadow elf high priestess, getting up from her throne while pointing an accusing finger at you.
"Who dares to enter House Meer'Golorh uninvited?" She demands, as other priestesses and shadow elf warriors slowly approach you, ready to attack. What do you do?
Show Crest
Run

"How did you get that?" One of the priestesses demands, as she takes the crest from you. "We do not know you, therefore you must have stolen it from one of our own!" The high priestess interjects. "SEIZE THEM!" She bellows.
Seeing more priestesses and warriors rushing toward you, you make a run for it!
Not wishing to face more priestesses and warriors from this ruling house, you turn away from these gates while you still can.
"SEIZE THEM!" The high priestess bellows, just as you were making a run for it!
In your haste, you realize too late that you dropped the crest of this house.

As you try to flee for your lives, you are quickly overwhelmed and put in chains. Smiling cruelly, another high priestess walks up to you: "You will suffer for this afront." She snarls. "Take them to the pen!" She orders.
"Yes, Matron Mother." One of the priestesses replies. You are then stripped of all your equipment, then taken to the city's slave pens.

As you try to flee for your lives, you are quickly overwhelmed and put in chains. Smiling cruelly, another high priestess walks up to you: "Doll arh'siv uuth vegarh." She snarls. "Isht tal uuth poyarh!" She orders.
You are then stripped of all your equipment, then taken to the city's slave pens.
While rummaging around in this empty hut, you find something of interest!
The bridge is retracted, leaving you stranded on this slave pen isle.

Your search reveals somekind of mechanism underneath the bridge. You notice that there used to be a lever attached to this mechanism; it was probably removed to prevent the deployment of the bridge from this side of the lake.
Planting one of the iron spikes firmly in place of the removed lever, you then pull with all your might!

As you cross the bridge, numerous shadow elf warriors are rushing to punish you attempt at freeing yourselves. Emboldened by your courage, other slaves from the pens join you to vent their hatred at their ruthless masters!
"If only we could find a way to escape from here!" Mumbles Scyrella Silverspear, with much frustration in her words.
You find a small group of amazons huddled together in this small mud hut. Having been brutalized and violated, some of them show signs of dehydration and hunger.

You tell them that you were searching for them in order to set them free. Visibly relieved by this, they pledge to help you escape once you find a means of leaving this accursed island. With a firm nod, you leave.

"My sisters!" Scyrella exclaims with happiness, tears running down her flushed cheeks. As the amazons rush to their queen with relief and hope, amazed that she is still alive, Scyrella turns to you: "We must find a way to leave here!"
Knowing you can count on the amazons to give a helping hand to escape, you nod firmly in response.

The amazons are still huddling together here. Upon your entrance, they look at you expectantly: "Is it time?" One of them asks you. You shake your head in response, assuring them that you are trying hard to find a way to escape.
"Keep your hopes up!" Scyrella intervenes, obviously trying to maintain the morale of her warrior-sisters.
This guard tower is empty, all shadow elf warriors having rushed outside to quell the slave insurrection.
More shadow elf warriors are waiting for you and the other slaves to protect the house of the Slave Master!
Rummaging through the house, you find your equipment! Apparently, 'someone' had already paid to buy your party as slaves with your own valuables ...
With the remainder of the shadow elf warriors busy at fighting the other slaves, you profit from the chaos to sneak out!

The gates to the slave pens are closed. You notice quite a lot of military activity on the other side of the battlements. It would appear that the shadow elves have increased their forces to keep the slaves dociles ...

This looks like the house of the slave master. Numerous shadow elf nobles are here, looking over slaves on display and bargaining for a good price. You notice among the slaves many races, such as orcs, ogres, gnaths, etc.
They all look miserable, visibly having been abused physically and emotionally, as well as poorly fed.
"We better make haste!" Scyrella Silverspear exclaims. "I fear we may be yet captured again, or worse. But how do we get out of this nightmarish place without crossing gates guarded by shadow elves?"

One of the amazons then reveals that she heard talk from other slaves about a secret door allowing to leave the city unseen. With renewed hope that you may yet get out alive, you ask her to take you there.

Leaving the chaos behind, you dash and hide in the side-streets of Naaz'Tzaraneen to avoid being seen, with the amazon leading the way. In no time, she takes you to a cave where a river runs through, stating that the door lies within.
"We can't leave without my sisters!!!" An adamant Scyrella yells. "They must be in one of the huts of the slave pens!" Having no other choice, you turn around.

"My sisters!" Scyrella exclaims with happiness, tears running down her flushed cheeks. As the amazons rush to their queen with relief and hope, amazed that she is still alive, Scyrella turns to you: "Now we can leave!"
Wearily, you make a run for the gates of the slave pens.

"This is where we part company, friends." A weary Scyrella muses, a bit of sadness in her eyes. "I must now lead my surviving sisters to a new land, where we'll settle and build our nation anew. Words can't express the gratitude I feel for your help."
"Let me give you my favored weapon as a token of our deep appreciation." As the other amazons whisper their approval, Scyrella Silverspear hands you her royal amazon spear!

"Farewell, friends. I wish you safe journeys and safer returns! Perhaps we'll meet again, the Gods willing." The amazon Queen adds in parting, hugging you tightly before leaving ... with her grateful warrior-sisters following her.

"This is where we part company." One of the weary amazons muses, a bit of sadness in her eyes. "We must now find a new land, where we'll settle and build our nation anew. Words can't express the gratitude we feel for what you have done for us."

"Farewell; we wish you safe journeys and safer returns! Perhaps we'll meet again, the Gods willing." The amazon adds in parting, hugging you before leaving ... with her other grateful warrior-sisters following her.
Crossing the door, the amazon then leads all of you through secret tunnels, eventually taking you to a cave within which a secret exit to the surface lies!

You come upon large gates, their obsidian battlements adorned with nightmarish scenes of spiders eating flesh. The platinum doors are wrought into the likeleness of a large spider with a shadow elfmaid's head. This, then, must be the goddess Tlarantale.
"Let us not waste any time." Zeerz Nys'Raeneen intones with impatience. "There is nothing relevant for you to see in Lloth's Temple; I doubt she'd welcome you in any case." She adds cryptically.

"Keep in mind that our Goddess is very much present here! She sees everything and can influence events directly within our city, especially within her own temples!" Having no particular desire to suffer the whims of an evil Goddess, you leave.

Numerous shadow elves are crossing the ominous gates, walking toward a dome-shaped building made of dark basalt with raising spikes fashioned in the likeness of spider legs. You guess that this large structure must be Tlarantale's temple.

Beyond the ominous gates, you see a dome-shaped building made of dark basalt with raising spikes fashioned in the likeness of spider legs. You guess that this large structure must be Tlarantale's temple.

"No! We do not go further!" Exclaims Zeerz Nys'Raeneen, visibly afraid to go beyond these gates. "This path leads to the Sacred Cave of Lolth, where the arachnians are created! No one but high priestesses are allowed in there!"

"Me hate them fancy-footings around the forge!" Mumbles Braggan Stoneheart, with much anger and frustration. "We should just cut down them louses to shreds! Moradin knows they'd well deserve it!" Not paying attention to such dwarven antics, you move on.

"May Lugath grant me the strenght and wisdom to suffer this terrible place!" Leira Songheart whispers, obviously reluctant to go further. Expecting this from a surface elf like her, you shrug it off and move on.
Earth gnome warriors are keeping watch in front of the entrance of this large huthouse.
"Vrliss isf svwidxitl?" One of them asks you. Not understanding a word, you play it safe and slowly walk away. You wish you had the means to understand the very foreign languages of the underearth.
"What do ye want with our embassy?" One of the guards asks, quite gruff and hostile. "Begone from here, ye scum!"
"Welcome to our embassy." One of the guards intones, as you are allowed entry.
A small iron plaque nailed to the door reads: "Svirfnilbdome Embassy".
"No one's allowed in there!" A guard warns you.

"Welcome to our humble embassy." A stocky, but well dressed, earth gnome greets you. "Me be Ambassador Swvirr, at yer service. It's rare indeed that we get visitors from the surface world." He adds with a wink.

"How are ye Swvirr, ye old son-of-an-orc!" Booms Braggan Stoneheart, as he bearhugs the surprised ambassador. "Braggan? Praise be Woralduur!" Replies the earth gnome, smiling with joy. "How stand the Dwarven Halls, me friend?"

"They prosper, as they should!" Replies a proud Braggan. "Same thing fer yer surface cousins of Gnomilar!" Swvirr nods at hearing such good news. "Then our efforts at establishing trade with ye folks proved good fer all, cuz Svirfnilbdome prospers too!"

As both Braggan and Swvirr continue exchanging news and anecdotes, you remind them of your presence with a little cough. "Oh, my!" Exclaims Swvirr, embarrased. "Forgive me! Let us go back to business at hand, eh?"

"This is the embassy of Svirfnilbdome, the earth gnome undercity." Intones Zeerz Nys'Raeneen. "No use wasting our time here" she adds impatiently. "Besides," she grimaces, "they won't let us in because of the presence of shadow elves among your group."
"So, how may me be of help to ye?"
"Welcome back to our humble embassy." Ambassador Swvirr greets you, with a wink.
"No bother at all!" Replies Swvirr, with good humor. With a courteous nod, you leave.

"This place is called Undermeet, a neutral trading area for the four major races living in this region of the Underdark. Namely, there's us, the earth gnomes of Svirnilbdome, as well as the kobolds of Sseshathuur, the shadow dwarves of Greyshimmers,

and of course the shadow elves of Naaz'Tzaraneen. Undermeet is divided essentially in four zones, each one given to one of the races. In each zone live the traders and other folks, and that's where ye'll find the embassy from each city.

Roughly at the center of Undermeet stands The Lightless Gloom. This huge building is where all merchants, traders and other folks meet; this place is not only a trading center, but an inn, tavern and market as well. Although the safety of all is

guaranteed by the Undermeet treaty, there are occasional scuffles, brawls or murders. In any case, Undermeet serves to lessen the tensions between the four major races of this region; there has been no war in years, although small clashes still happen."
"Here's a map that'll help ye find your way around."

"This region of the Underearth is occupied by four major races: the kobolds of Ssheshathuur, the shadow dwarves of Greyshimmers, the shadow elves of Naaz'Tzaraneen, and us earth gnomes of Svirfnilbdome. The one and only rule ye should heed is that

to enter any of those four cities, ye best either look like the inhabitants, or have none of the other races among your group. For example, if ye wish to enter Greyshimmers, then either all of ye be shadow dwarves, or ye better have no kobold,

no gnome, no shadow elf or no other kind of dwarves among yer group. If that's not the case, then at best ye'll be turned back, or at worse ye'll be killed. The Underearth is a dark and dangerous place fer those that live within it; it becomes even more

dangerous to surface folks ... aye, even fer folks like ye! Mark me words: use yer brains and better think before ye go to one place or another! Otherwise, it will be yer funeral! Beware every corner, every creature ye encounter and that yer not sure of
their intentions! Beware all, of course, except us earth gnomes: we are the only peaceful race in the Underearth, although we can fight with the best of them to defend ourselves!"

"The shadow dwarves worship Orcas, the God of Atrocities, Terror and Undeath. The shadow elves worship Lloth, or Tlarantale as ye know her, the Goddess of Evil, Chaos and Spiders. The kobolds worship Neralkuur, God of Evil and dark ambitions."

"The shadow elf ruling noble house of Nys'Raeneen has apparently involved itself with some unkown powers from the surface world. These powerful beings call themselves the 'Overlords'. It is not known why exactly house Nys'Raeneen has done this."

"There's talk that a noble shadow elf priestess has been sold to kobold slavers. Surprisingly, the shadow elf ruling house Nys'Raeneen has not even reacted to such outright violation of the Treaty of Undermeet!"

"There are many kind of folks hanging out at the Lightless Gloom. Be careful to whom you speak, especially if ye're of a race that's adversarial to that person: things can get ugly pretty quickly! Use wisdom and prudence at all times!"
You hear strange, eerie chants coming from further down in this cave. The sounds and chants make your skin crawl. Do you go in?

As you come into this larger cave, you are witness to a gruesome site: numerous arachnians stand silently in circle around a statue-altar of Tlarantale, their white eyes shining brightly. You notice a few monstrous spiders standing among them.

Six shadow elf high priestesses are chanting dark, foreboding incantations while weaving powerful magics. A lone shadow elf warrior kneels before them, a look of dread and despair on his tired face. You see tears trickling down his ebony cheeks.
As the chanting reaches a high point, the poor shadow elf warrior suddenly screams as his features become sickeningly twisted and deformed.
He then transforms into a shadow elf arachnian!

One of the high priestesses then sees you, sounding the alarm! It would appear that you have stumbled unto some sort of forbidden ceremony, where no one else but high priestesses and arachnians are allowed!
As more monstrous spiders and arachnians rush to fight you, you decide it would be best to get out of this horrific cave!
Running through the crowd who, thankfully, pay you no heed, you seek any side-street to hide from anyone -or anything- that might be pursuing you.
Feeling safe here, you decide to lay low for a while. Thanks to your lucky stars, no one has paid attention to you.
Considering what happened the last time you came here, you decide not to tempt the fates twice and move on.

"This place is called Tuur Narish." Zeerz Nys'Raeneen intones. "It is two academies into one: a military academy, and a magic academy. Only the students and masters are allowed there. So, let us leave."
A platinum plaque nailed to the battlements reads: "Tuur Narish".
Shadow elf warriors are standing guard. "Only students are masters are allowed into the academies!" One of them warns.
A platinum plaque is nailed to the battlements, but you can't decipher its meaning. Seeing numerous shadow elf warriors standing guard and eyeing you with suspicion, you walk away.
"This is Tzaraneen Island!" One of the shadow elf warriors intones. "Only the highest nobility lives here. Rabble like you aren't welcome! Begone before we make you regret your impudence!"

This is a small slave-market. Numerous kobolds are here, looking over the slaves on display for sale. Among them you notice a shadow elf maiden. Quite beautiful, she looks proud and haughty despite being in chains and paraded for the highest bidder.

From her tattered garbs, she looks to be some kind of shadow elf nobility. Perhaps even a priestess. To your surprise, she has noticed your scrutiny: with a raised eyebrow, she appraises you in return. One has to admire such gumption and composure.
Buy her
Rescue her

An old kobold comes your way, having also seen your interest in the shadow elfmaiden: "Beautiful, ain't she?" He muses, showing rotten his teeth with a cruel grin. "Me name's Sstushi, an' me be Slave master here. Ye wanna buy her?" You nod.
"She be nobility, eh? So, she be costing a lot!" The old kobold intones, a greedy look in his eyes. "Me price's 7500 gold pieces, payable in gems. So, that'll be 75 gems in all!" What do you reply?
"What a shame." The old kobold replies, feigning disapointment. "Ah, well! If ye change yer mind, come back again, eh?"
The small slave market is still bustling with activity. You notice that the shadow elf maiden is still being displayed. What would you like to do?
"Welcome back!" Sstushi greets you, showing again his rotten teeth with his greedy smile. "The price fer the shadow elf maid is still 7500 golds or 75 gems!" What do you reply?
"What do ye take me fer?" Sstushi yells, insulted by your counter-offer. "Get outa here and don't bother me again!"
Nothing
"Oh, very well!" Sstushi replies, feigning despair. "Yer twisting me arm and sending me to the poor house, but what can me do? 5000 golds, or 50 gems, it is then! Who'll pay?"
"No money to pay? What do ye take me fer?" Sstushi yells, insulted. "Get outa here and don't bother me again!"

As Sstushi counts the gems, another kobold brings you the shadow elf maiden. As he removes her chains, she pushes him to the ground, snarling. "Take your filthy hands off of me, you dirty scum!" She warns through clenched teeth. She then turns to you.

"You may have bought me, but you'll never own me!" She spits defiantly. You then tell her that you simply need someone to take you to Naaz'Tzaraneen, in order to find out why the shadow elves allied themselves with dangerous beings called 'Overlords'.

"Lloth does favor me after all!" She replies, her hostile demeanor now gone. "I am Zeerz Nys'Raeneen, priestess and noble of the ruling house of Naaz'Tzaraneen, house Nys'Raeneen. My Matron Mother, Biella, was seduced by a mysterious man named Nyxos."

"He convinced her to embark upon this foolish path of conquering the surface lands above, in alliance with the forces this Nyxos said he commands. But I saw through him, and found out his true nature. He is a psionic demon, and he corrupted my Matron."

"But when I confronted both," Zeerz continues, "my Matron Mother instead ordered my death! That is when I knew my purpose: to depose Matron Biella as ruling Matron of house Nys' Raeneen, and end this foolish alliance that is unfavored by Lloth!"

"I managed to escape Naaz'Tzaraneen, but was captured by warriors of another noble house and sold to slavery to this filthy kobold Slave Master. But you coming here to deliver me is a sure sign that Lloth favors my purpose. Thus, I must go back."

"Back to Naaz'Tzaraneen to take power of the ruling house Nys'Raeneen! Let us go there: I will guide you once we are within the city. I will lead you to house Nys'Raeneen, and show you a secret entrance to there. And then, we will fullfill my purpose."

"I will kill Matron Biella with my own hands, a fitting punishment for her weakness, a flaw which Lloth never approves. And you, you will deal with this Nyxos!" You nod in agreement. "Where are my belongings?" Zeerz then demands.
Leaning a little on Sstushi, you manage to get Zeerz' belongings back. "Then let us go to meet with our destiny!" She intones, ready to follow your group.
Zeerz Nys'Raeneen has joined your party; check out the Allies menu.

"WHAT?" An incensed Scyrella Silverspear exclaims. "We ally ourselves with shadow elves? After what they did to my nation? This is an outrage!" Not backing down, Zeerz looks at the amazon Queen square in the eye: "I heard of what happened." She intones.

Zeerz shakes her head in disapproval: "While it was my house who was responsible for this massacre, it was done at the bidding of this Nyxos creature. But I know for a fact that many amazons survived: they are being kept in the slave pens of our city."

"Once I claim house Nys'Raeneen, and this Nyxos is dead, I will free your amazons and allow all of you to leave Naaz'Tzaraneen safe and sound. That is my deal: without me, you stand little chance of surviving a visit to my city; this you can believe!"

"Very well, shadow elf!" Scyrella replies, still fuming. "But be warned: I'll be watching you very closely. Pray to your dark Goddess that I catch you not, should you ever betray us!" Zeerz simply nods at that.

"Bah!" Braggan Stoneheart exclaims, spitting on the ground to emphasize his sentiments. "Shadow elf scum can't be trusted, especially their durn priestesses! Me not fer liking her joining us, not one bit! But we've no choice, have we?"
Shaking his head in disgust, Braggan goes on mumbling his reservations.

"Well, what an interesting twist in the story, no?" Riel Moonsong muses, half-joking and half-serious. "This situation is riddled with irony, don't you think?" He winks. "Irony is one of the preferred dishes of my Goddess." Zeerz intones, cryptically.
For once at a loss for words, Riel shakes his head, chuckling sarcastically.
The small slave market is again bustling with activity. Many slaves are on display, mostly goblins, orcs and gnats. Not particularly interested in slave trading, you walk by.
"Great!" Sstushi exclaims, grinning. "7500 golds, or 75 gems, it is then! Who'll pay?"
Annoyed by all of this raucus, the kobold King himself and his retinue come to investigate. Wrongly percieving the situation as an attempt at invading Sseshathuur, he enters the battle!
Upon the death of their King, some kobolds flee the battle in panic!
With a swift swing of your weapon, you break the elf maiden's chains. As you grab her hand to pull her toward you, the Slave Master sees what is happening and screams in alarm!
"Slave stealers!" He yells, rousing all kobolds about the slave market to teach you a lesson!
As more kobolds are rushing in to fight you anew, you grab the elf maiden and make a run out of Sseshathuur!
Finding this cave empty, you decide to hide here for a while.

"Lloth does favor me after all!" She replies. "I am Zeerz Nys'Raeneen, priestess and noble of the ruling house of Naaz'Tzaraneen, house Nys'Raeneen. My Matron Mother, Biella, was seduced by a mysterious man named Nyxos."
The moment you enter Sseshathuur, alert kobold warriors sound the call to arms!
As more kobolds are rushing in to fight you anew, you make a run out of Sseshathuur!
You tell her that you need someone knowledgeable to take you to Naaz'Tzaraneen, in order to find out why the shadow elves allied themselves with dangerous psionic beings called 'Overlords'.
"Not that I'm unappreciative for what you have done," the elf maiden muses, breaking the silence, "but I am at a loss as to why you rescued me. This is not the way of my people."
"I will kill Matron Biella with my own hands, a fitting punishment for her weakness, a flaw which Lloth never approves. And you, you will deal with this Nyxos!" You nod in agreement.
"Then let us go to meet with our destiny!" She intones, ready to follow your group.
The gates are opened upon your approach, and you are allowed to pass unbothered.
You come upon huge battlements made of solid basalt. Numerous shadow dwarves are keeping watch here, as if expecting an invasion at any moment.
Do you proceed further?
As you are about to cross the gates, the shadow dwarves sound the call to arms! It would appear that these folks are rather intolerant of races other than themselves!
As more shadow dwarves are rushing in to fight you anew, you make a run for it!
This looks like a general store.
This looks like an alchemy shop.
This looks like some sort of magic shop.
This looks like some armorer's and weaponsmith's shop.

"Here we are: house Nys'Raeneen!" Zeerz intones. "But we cannot enter through the gates, for we will be stopped immediately. I know of a secret door just to the east and north of the battlements. Let us go there instead to enter the estate."
A large golden plaque hangs on the steel doors of the gates: "House Nys'Raeneen".
Taking her house crest, Zeerz Nys'Raeneen inserts it into a little opening on the wall here. Immediately, a locking mechanism is released! "We can use this secret door, now." Zeerz muses.
Taking the crest of house Nys'Raeneen, you insert it into a little opening on the wall here. Immediately, a locking mechanism is released, allowing you to use this secret door.
This secret door is locked. You have no idea how to unlock it, especially since you cannot find any locking mechanism to alter or to pick.
"You have no business here!" One of several shadow elf guards intones. "Begone now, or suffer the consequences!"

"Here we are!" Zeerz Nys'Raeneen exclaims. "Lloth's favor is with us, for no one has recognized me or made any attempt to stop us!" You then wonder aloud how your party could take on a whole shadow elf noble house, even with her on your side.

Zeerz chuckles. "I was not the only one in my house who viewed this alliance with Nyxos as something not favored by Lloth. Our Goddess knows what is right for our people, and psionic beings such as this Nyxos are to be treated as the greater threat!"

"Therefore, many of my sisters, Lloth's priestesses each one of them, knew as I did that Nyxos' corruption of our house and of our Matron Mother had to be stopped. But only I had the courage to speak. Now, if we confront this rot together, they will

seize the opportunity and help us!" She then lowers her voice. "But once I claim the title of ruling Matron of house Nys'Raeneen, I will make certain that they be reminded of their initial cowardice, and what problems it caused me. Now, let us do this!"

You wonder how it came to be that by doing something that is right, you end up serving nonetheless the interests of a dark Goddess such as Lloth/Tlarantale, as well as serving the petty interests of someone as determined and power-hungry as Zeerz.
It would appear that irony has indeed primacy in the dark, twisted and convoluted world of the shadow elves. Trying to shrug off such disturbing thoughts, you ready your weapons and follow Zeerz.

"Greetings, Mother!" Zeerz intones menacingly as you enter a large hall. You notice numerous shadow elf warriors and priestesses, some gathered around a statue-altar of Tlarantale. One of the priestesses marches forward, her red eyes flashing hatred.

"My dear, prodigal daughter has come back." The priestess muses, her tone of voice mixed with sarcasm and dark promises of torture. "And with new friends, at that!" She adds. "But we expected that, didn't we my dear Nyxos?" She chuckles.

"We did, Matron Biella!" A man clad in armor intones, as he walks forward to stand beside Zeerz' Matron mother. "These friends of your treacherous daughter are now quite known to us." He adds with a cruel smirk, bowing his head to you in mock politeness.
"General Nyxos Uhn, Fourth Speaker of the Inner Council of Overlords, at your service." He adds derisively, his eyes pulsating with an eerie reddish glow.

"These are potent adversaries of our common goals, Matron Biella." Nyxos continues, unphased. "It is good fortune that your foolish daughter has not only returned to face your justice, but delivered these troublesome individuals into our hands as well!"

"Justice indeed!" Replies Zeerz. "It is Lloth's justice that will be served today, to an unworthy Matron, to a psionic demon, and to those who followed them! Lloth favors me, because my path lies with hers!"

"To those who agree with me, now is the time of reckoning for house Nys'Raeneen!" At that, Zeerz dashes ahead for battle. As you are about to do the same, you notice that some of the shadow elf warriors and priestesses choose to join your side!

"Victory is mine!" Exclaims an elated Zeerz Nys'Raeneen. She then turns to you, her demeanor cold and detached: "Take my house crest, it will allow you to leave Naaz'Tzaraneen in peace, as I promised. Now, our accounts are settled."
"But leave you must, otherwise you will be treated like any other mongrels. You best heed my words ..." She adds menacingly, before tossing you her own house crest.
"And what about my warrior-sisters?" Demands an outraged Scyrella Silverspear.
"Go to the slave pens to retrieve the amazons." Zeerz intones. "Show them the crest at the gates of the slave pens."
"Now leave!" Zeerz orders you. "I must now attend to the task of consolidating my power." Somewhat feeling rebuffed, you turn around to leave this madhouse.

You then spot Nyxos Uhn, lying in a pool of blood and near death. Upon your approach, he smiles: "The Sword Lands may not become ours," he mumbles, "but the Mind Lords will return nonetheless!" At that, he activates one of his rings and vanishes!

The surviving shadow elf priestesses then begin to argue with each other, with Zeerz Nys'Raeneen's voice being the most forceful. Guessing that they are now contending for the position of ruling Matron, you decide to leave them to their own devices.

Handing the crest of house Nys'Raeneen to the guards, you demand that the amazon slaves be given in charge to you. After a few minutes, the amazons are brought out. Having been brutalized and violated, some of them show signs of dehydration and hunger.

You tell them that you were searching for them in order to set them free. Visibly relieved by such news, they pledge to follow you to the surface, and face with you any danger you might encounter on this journey.

One of the amazons then reveals that she heard talk from other slaves about a secret door allowing to leave the city unseen. With renewed hope that you may yet get out alive, you ask her to take you there.

Leaving the pens, you dash and hide in the side-streets of Naaz'Tzaraneen to avoid being seen, with the amazon leading the way. In no time, she takes you to a cave where a river runs through, stating that the door lies within.

"My sisters!" Scyrella exclaims with happiness, tears running down her flushed cheeks. As the amazons rush to their queen with relief and hope, amazed that she is still alive, Scyrella turns to you: "We must leave before Zeerz changes her mind!"
A large golden plaque hangs on the steel doors of the gates: "House Duur'Nareen".

"Let us not waste time here." Zeerz Nys'Raeneen interjects. "Duur'Nareen is the 2nd out of eight noble houses, and thus an adversary to my house. They would never help, and are of no use to our cause."
"Dinas uuhl Duur'Nareen vorak?" She demands, as other priestesses and shadow elf warriors slowly approach you, ready to attack. Not understanding a word of what they are saying, what do you do?
"Who dares to enter House Duur'Nareen uninvited?" She demands, as other priestesses and shadow elf warriors slowly approach you, ready to attack. What do you do?
A large golden plaque hangs on the steel doors of the gates: "House Zan'Deezan".

"Let us not waste time here." Zeerz Nys'Raeneen interjects. "Zan'Deezan is the 3rd out of eight noble houses, and thus an adversary to my house. They would never help, and are of no use to our cause."
"Dinas uuhl Zan'Deezan vorak?" She demands, as other priestesses and shadow elf warriors slowly approach you, ready to attack. Not understanding a word of what they are saying, what do you do?
"Who dares to enter House Zan'Deezan uninvited?" She demands, as other priestesses and shadow elf warriors slowly approach you, ready to attack. What do you do?
Kobold warriors are standing watch at these gates. "Ye have no proper business here!" One of them intones. "So begone!"

"Me be orc rinds if this here wall ain't fake!" Muses Braggan, studying the wall to the north while strocking his long beard. Upon closer inspection, you realize that this wall is an illusion hiding an entrance to a cave!
Upon closer inspection of the wall to your north, you realize that it is an illusion hiding the entrance to a cave!
A sign hangs on the door of this building. The sign is written in many languages, one of which is the common tongue. It reads: "The Lightless Gloom".

The place is full! You notice all sorts of underearth races within, from orcs and goblins to gnats and dogres! You also notice that kodolds, earth gnomes, shadow elves and shadow dwarves tend to stay together at their own chosen group of tables.
Perhaps that is why you feel an almost palpable air of tension permeating this place. Or is this feeling caused by all too many glances thrown your way, glances that spell danger and death?

After the clash, you wonder why there isn't any militia patrol around. You then realize that a city such as Naaz'Tzaraneen must lack militia patrols, and that brutal acts such as this are part of everyday life in this city.

You see some kind of procession coming your way. A high priestess is sitting regally on a huge platinum-laced chair, carried by numerous goblin slaves. She is escorted by other priestesses and a retinue of warriors. She must be some sort of nobility.

All shadow elves about you quickly kneel and bow their heads, not daring to look up to gaze at her. You notice that the priestesses walking along the procession are looking around sternly, as if making sure everyone is kneeling and looking down.

"We best do like everyone!" Zeerz whispers in your ear. "According to our customs, failure by the common folk to show submission or subservience to a high priestess is punishable by death!" At that, Zeerz kneels down, pretending subservience.
Playing along with this, you do the same. In no time, the procession walks by without any incident.

Playing along, you do the same. In no time, the procession walks by. However, one of the priestesses begins to yell at a wretch, flogging him with perverse pleasure. Apparently, she did not think the poor shadow elf was showing subservience properly.

Playing along, you do the same. In no time, the procession walks by. However, one of the priestesses begins to yell at a wretch, apparently deciding that the poor shadow elf was not showing subservience properly. She then cuts his throat for all to see.
Do you do like all other shadow elves about you?

"How dare you not show proper respect for a high priestess?" One of the priestesses yells at you, incensed by your 'arrogance'. As she begins to flay at you with her weapon, she calls out to the other priestesses and warriors!
"Nazys ohl'erthum ni vaas kirack?" One of the priestesses yells at you, visibly incensed. As she begins to flay at you with her weapon, she calls out to the other priestesses and warriors!

You try to run for your lives, only to be overwhelmed. As you lay fallen and unconscious, the cutthroats strip you of all your equipment and valuables, leaving you for dead as they run away to find other victims.

Shadow dwarves are busy working their mines, while others transport the ores and stones to the processing warehouses across the street.
A shadow dwarf raiding band eye you as easy prey!
You cross paths with a shadow dwarf raiding band. Their leader nods to you, mistaking your party as a rading band like their own ... thanks to your disguises!

You cross paths with a band of earth gnomes. Although they do not bother you, they remain at a safe distance, obviously suspicious yet curious at the same time. After debating a bit among themselves, they resume their march without saying a word to you.
You cross paths with a band of earth gnome warriors. Because of your disguises, they mistake you as a raiding party from one of their enemy races of the Underearth!
You wonder if it would not be best to remove your disguises while wandering these parts of the Underearth ...
You cross paths with a band of earth gnome warriors. Because of the race of some of your party members, they mistake you as a raiding party from one of their enemy races of the Underearth!
You wonder if perhaps appropriate disguises would prevent any further misunderstandings such as this ...
You cross paths with a raiding band of kobolds!
You cross paths with a raiding band of kobolds. Upon seeing the kobold members within your party, the raiding band leader nods and leave you unbothered.
You find something intriguing worn by some of your attackers.
"My, my!" Muses Riel Moonsong. "I thought I had seen my share of sad and gloomy places, but this one steals the show!" He chuckles at that.
"Well!" Intones Zeerz while sniffing the air with disdain and pulling over the hood of her cloak to conceal her identity. "I am certain we'll blend in fine." She adds with a grimace.
"What an ... interesting place." A dubious Naryl Thezzat muses.
"I would have never imagined such an ecclectic gathering!" Athos exclaims, visibly delighted by this new experience.
"Can you guys take me home, now?" Jorale asks, half-joking and half-serious, as she looks about the place with wariness.
"I must say," Denard muses, looking somewhat distraught, "I never thought I'd find myself in the presence of such a large assembly of rogueish characters ..."
"You and me both, friend!" Belrion adds.
"If we rent a room here," Scyrella chimes in, "I'll sleep on the floor, thank you. I gather it'll be cleaner than the matresses and sheets, if the patrons in here are any indication!"

"Moradin preserves us!" Braggan exclaims, aghast. "Not only is this hole be filled with shadow elves, it's bursting with other scum too? And me can't bust any of their heads? What me has done to deserve such torture?"

"Now, more than ever," Naryl whispers between clenched teeth, "we must find the leader of the Inner Council of Overlords. He holds all the answers, and all the keys to their sinister plan. The Mind Lords must never again walk into our world, friends!"

"I know you all too well, General Uhn!" Naryl Thezzat snarls out loud. "I've been hunting you and your ilk for far too long now, but it appears that the hunt is finally over! Time for you to pay the piper, as they say!"

"I know you all too well, Master Sark!" Naryl Thezzat snarls out loud. "I've been hunting you and your ilk for far too long now, but it appears that the hunt is finally over! Time for you to pay the piper, as they say!"

"I can't put my finger on it ..." Naryl Thezzat muses, visibly perturbed. "I thought I sensed ..." She then shakes her head. "No. I must be getting tired." Not really sure what to make of this, you shrug it off.

"We meet again, Praetor Primus." Naryl Thezzat interjects, her voice as hard as steel. "Well, well; the annoying psi-knight herself." Primus replies, nonplussed. "How does it feel to be so close, but still so far?" He taunts, his voice mimicking care.

Naryl remains silent, although she is obviously fuming. "Nothing to say, little bloodhound?" Primus taunts anew. "Glad to have caught yet another prey, like the three others you helped to kill some six months past?"

You then notice tears trickling down the flushed cheeks of Scyrella Silverspear. Embarassed that you have seen her cry, she nervously wipes her tears: "Lantharond has lost a great king." She mumbles. "I always had great respect and admiration for him."
She then sighs: "It would seem that the both of us were meant to suffer as rulers of our respective nations." She then becomes silent with grief.
