"It was he," Naerun continues, "along with Strider, who were responsible for the birth of our resistance against the usurper's rule. He not only deserves to be with us on the day we march with you to Sharranth, but he'll be instrumental in our victory."

The prince sighs. "Arcantilivius' mansion lies on the small island on Cedar Lake, just north of us. An impenetrable barrier of energy surrounds the mansion, preventing any entry or exit, as well as any form of communication. He is completely cut off."

"The current Royal Warlock, Ertham Zoh, was responsible for this. In fact, he was responsible for everything we've endured for the last six years, from Storm's victory over us to my father's assassination, King Baerun II." Naerun shakes his head angrily.

"His day will come." The prince snarls. He then breathes deeply. "In any case, good adventurers, I ask you to find a means to bring down the barrier around Aracantilivius' mansion, and bring him back to us. Then, we'll talk." With a firm nod, you go.
"I wish you success!" Strider calls out, as you leave.
Prince Naerun Halgard is conferring with Strider and other advisors, probably planning some other raid on sharranthine forces. You decide it would be best not to distrub them.

"What?" Arcantilivius exclaims, feigning indignation. "I'm finally back from exile, and no festivities in my honor? I see that good sense has come and gone while I was geoled!" At that, everyone starts laughing, as Naerun rushes to embrace the old mage.

"You haven't changed one bit, you old coot!" Strider chimes in, equally happy at Arcantilivius' return. "Me, change? And deprive all of you poor, somber souls of my famous good humor?" The mage replies, starting another round of laughter.

"And look who's calling me old!" Arcantilivius retorts to Strider, with a snicker. "At least, I look my age!" The mage adds, amidst more goodnatured ribbing. While the reunion joy goes on, Naerun approaches, smiling: "Thank you so much, noble ones!"

"Go back to Tanirith," he continues, "and let them know that, of course, we gladly accept their help. We are quite touched that they think of us, to allow us to march with them as Sharranth is liberated. When you come back with your forces,

we'll be waiting near the gates of the city, well hidden! I bid you safe journeys and safer returns!" With hearty clasps of arms in parting, you leave Naerun and the rebels to their joyful reunion. "We'll win yet!" Strider calls out to you as you leave.
The trap door is locked. The unicorns are probably out on a raid against sharranthine forces.
The trap door is locked. The rebels are probably lying in wait near the gates of Sharranth, waiting for you and your forces.
The trap door is locked. The unicorns' hideout is most likely abandoned now.

"How is your progress?" The Lord Paladine asks you. You proudly announce to him that you've made contact with the rebels, or 'Unicorns' as they call themselves, and that they welcome the help of Wailsrond and Tanirith. "Superb!" He exclaims, happy.

You also tell him that the Unicorns will wait for the assault force to reach Sharranth before joining the overall attack. "Yes." He replies. "Very well then! I'll order High Commander Fireblade to provide some of his knights for an assault force."

"This force will be waiting for you at the southwest gates of the city. From there, you are to march straight to Wailsrond and meet with Lord Pyre to tell him of this: he should then provide you with a contingent of his own. And from there: Sharranth!"

The Lord Paladine then pauses, a somber look falling over his face. "If possible, try to capture Anthraxus Storm. He should stand trial for what he has done." You nod. "This will be a grand day!" The Lord continues in earnest.

"I only wish I could leave the politics of the High Council to lead this liberation attack." He sighs. "But I've much faith in you, noble ones. Safe journeys and safer returns! May Tyr guide your steps!" After firm clasps of hands in parting, you leave.
A detachment of knights of the Flame are waiting here. "Greetings, heroes!" Their commander chimes, smiling. "We are ready and willing, by Tyr's grace!" At that, they begin to follow you.

"Welcome back, heroes!" Lord Pyre greets you. You tell him that you've made contacts with the rebels and that they stand poised to make the final assault on Sharranth the moment forces from his city and from Tanirith launch an attack.

"The fates are smiling upon us!" Pyre exclaims, quite happy at such news. "Bring these news to Essain Helmfire as soon as you can! I'll wait for your return; in the meantime, I'll assemble a small force to contribute to the liberation of Sharranth!"

"The fates are smiling upon us!" Pyre exclaims, quite happy at such news. "I've already assembled a contingent of our own forces; they stand ready to march out at your orders!' With a firm nod and clasp of hands, you leave for the wailsrondese compound.
"Welcome back, heroes!" Lord Pyre greets you. You tell him that you are commanding a group of knights of Flame from Tanirith, and that you are ready to march to Sharranth.
"Safe journeys!" Belrion calls out as you walk away.

Lord Pyre and Belrion welcome you with arms open, as a small fanfare trumpets away: "And the Victors of the Battle of Sharranth are back!" Lord Pyre chimes with joy. "The news have already reached us." Belrion explains, grinning from ear to ear.

"To celebrate the end of the Great War, and its most famous Heroes, a fitting toast," Pyre continues, smiling as small glasses of what looks to be rhum are being passed around, "with the first bottle of our very first batch of rhum since our liberation!"

Everyone shout in cheers and drink to the toast, while the fanfare plays on. "Our reconstruction goes well." Pyre adds, as the celebration winds down a little. "On the morrow, I'll send diplomatic envoys to Sharranth: renewal of trade will only be

beneficial for all of us! This day will live in history forever, friends!" More rhum is passed around, as plates of food are brought in. The celebration lasts a good part of the night, a nice change on venue for all that you have had to endure of late.

Only when you are beginning to fall asleep at the table that you realize you've had your fill. Bidding your farewells to Lord Pyre and Belrion, you leave the Wailsrondese to celebrate further. And so they should, considering what they lived through!

Loud cheers and fanfare erupt when you approach the Lord Paladine. By his side, among many notables, you see Jhalor Fireblade and Jarad Noll, all smiles. Even Shalla Thrall and Nomune Ngallan are here. "Today is the dawn of a new era!" The Lord intones.

"Today, the Great War is over, with the forces of good and justice victorious!" More cheers erupt. "Despite dissentions, misunderstandings and, aye, dark conspiracies, all that we stand for prevails. And today, there is now peace in the Sword Lands!"

As yet more cheers finally wind down, the Lord Paladine continues his speech: "Also today, we honor those who have fought for our ideals. Their sacrifice will always be remembered. We can only thank the Gods that true heroes led the way, men and
women who can now be known forever more as Heroes of the Sword Lands!" Amidst another bout of loud cheering, Jhalor and Jarad bring forward a large chest that they place at your feet.

"And now, let's celebrate!" The Lord Paladine booms, at the delight of everyone. Plates of food and bottles of Tanirith wine are brought in. As everyone begins celebrating, the Lord Paladine walks up to you, along with Jhalor and Jarad.

"Well, my friends, enjoy this day, for it truly belongs to you!" He chimes, with a firm clap in your back. "And then some!" Jarad adds, raising his glass of wine. "A feat of legendary proportions!" Jhalor joins in. "That should write a song or two!"
The mention of music distracts your attention momentarily toward Riel Moonsong, who is sitting at a table, furiously scribbling away on parchment sheets between gulps of wine.

"At first light of dawn, I'll be sending envoys to Sharranth." The Lord Paladine muses, laughter in his eyes. "All in all, all's well that ends well!" He adds, raising his glass in a toast. "All's well that ends well!" Jhalor and Jarad reply in unison.

The celebration lasts a good part of the night, with every notable trying to speak with you or seeking you out to praise you. Many a toast are made: to Tyr, to you, to the Fates, to Victory, and so on. The folks of Tanirith have much to be joyous about.

Only when you are beginning to fall asleep at the table that you realize you've had your fill. Bidding your farewells to the Lord Paladine, Jhalor, Jarad and the others, you leave the good folks of Tanirith to celebrate late into the morning.

"What of you, friends?" Jhalor asks. You tell them that the Overlords are still out there, somewhere, and you aim to get them once and for all before they cause more pain and sorrow. "Hear, hear, Noble Heroes!" Jarad chimes, raising his glass again.
The Lord Paladine is busy conferring with his advisors. Upon seeing you, he smiles and asks for news about your adventures.
Seeing that he is quite occupied with affairs of state, you heartily shake his hand and take your leave.

You announce proudly to Storm that you have destroyed the Unicorn rebels. "Excellent!" The warlord chimes, quite satisfied. "Now, only one little detail remains: Ertham Zoh, the Royal Warlock. He's the one who assured my initial conquest of the city."

"He helped my army enter Sharranth and he killed the last king of the city; he even imprisoned the former Royal Mage in the poor man's own mansion, by sealing it with a powerful magical barrier. But I don't trust him." He shakes his head in frustration.

At that, you mention to him having the sense that a conspiracy might be about to undo him. You relate to him what your read from the letter you found in those assassins posing as unicorns. This seems to implicate someone named "E.Z."

You then tell him about a minotaur chiefson kept in captivity to force the minotaurs to serve in the army of Sharranth, while potentially using the captive to embarass the warlord. Once again, this seems to involve a certain "E.Z."
You then notice Grundar pulling the hood of his cloak over his face, as if fearing to be recognized by Anthraxus. Letting it go, it does however remind you of something to speak about.

"That's it!" Storm exclaims. "That's the kind of proof I was looking for to convince the nobles of the court, thus letting me off the hook! Now, I can move against that snivelling weakling! Go to his mansion and apprehend him!"
"Find me proof, any proof, that Ertham Zoh is scheming behind my back. That's all I'll need to convince the nobles of the Court, and thus allow me to finally move against him!"

"I heard the news!" Anthraxus Storms chimes upon your approach, grinning from ear to ear. "Truly, you have been of great service for me. Thanks to you, my position in Sharranth is fully secured. Also, Sharanth is now more than a lone city-state!"

"Indeed," he continues, "I know rule a veritable kingdom with its chief rival, Tanirith, well kept in check. Again, thanks to your valuable services. Did you know that Tanirith has accepted my offer for peace?" You shake your head, quite surprised.

Storms chuckles with delight. "They had no choice but to accept, especially because of my alliance with Lantharond ... once more, thanks to you! I told you that I can be generous to those who serve me without fail: today I make true my claim!"
At a snap of his fingers, servants bring out a large chest which they leave before you.

"Not bad, eh?" Storm intones, smiling. "But above all, the Overlords are gone from our lands. Yet, this could be a pyrric victory, for they could return." He pauses, taking a sip of the wine he was just given by a servant. Glasses are given to you also.

"Tanirith wine is truly the best!" Storm muses, raising his glass with a wink. "In any case, the time has now come for you to engage the Overlords on their own turf, sort of speak. Thanks to my ever efficient spy, the Raven, I have learned that they hide

somewhere in Umaldyr. Thus, I release you from my service, so that you may go there. Once in Umaldyr, find them and convey to them my 'best' regards." The warlord chuckles cruelly at that. "I do believe that songs will be made about you for that!"

"I wish you all success!" Anthraxus Storm bids you, raising his glass in a grandiose toast. After a few more glasses of wine, you take your leave, satisfied of what you have accomplished ... especially for your own improvement.
Anthraxus Storm is busy conferring with his advisors. You decide it would be best not to disturb him for naught.
"Well," Anthraxus continues, "one last thing: because you have served me so well, I enjoin you to keep the Royal seal I gave you. It will still allow you to travel freely within my domains."
Considering the current state of things, however peaceful they may be, you decide against tempting fate and back away.
A sign on the door of this building read: "Waystation of the Long and Winding Road".
A sign hanging on the door of this establishment reads: "Upper West Store".
This old worn-out sign reads: "Upper Umaldyr - West". It also points to the north for Ashkor and Koralya, to the east for Upper Umaldyr - East, and to the southeast for Umaldyr.
A sign on the door of this establishment reads: "Tavern of the Old Lighthouse".
Although the place reeks of pipe smoke and bad alcohol, it is filled with sailors, pier workers, fishermen and mariners.

"The current king is the third of a line of 'lazy kings'. He lives reclused in his palace and the governing is left entirely to the Mayor of the Palace. Folk blame these lazy kings for the goblin invasion and the break-up of our nation."

"When the goblins invaded the north six years ago, from out of nowhere, numerous nobles seized their chance to declare their holdings independent from the crown. Today, our island-nation is broken up in several baronies which compete against each other."

"Of all the barons, the one from Ashkor is the most power-hungry. The word's out that he hires adventurers to retrieve lost treasures and magic items for him. Rumors say that he made deals with some of the goblin tribes to the north to beef up his army."

"Folktales speak of ancient ruins lying around the islands of our nation. These would be ruins of the fabled empires of Macremia and Telluria. In fact, the two huge lighthouses to the east are said to have been made by either one of these lost empires."

"After invading the north six years ago, the goblin tribes have settled down. Some of them even trade now with Ashkor, Aurelian and Koralya. However, the Thasselanies, or wood elves, of the far north still wage guerilla warfare against the goblins."

"The Thasselanies, or wood elves, that live in the far north have become intolerant of races other than surface elves. This is in part because they were abandoned by the opportunistic barons who chose to stay neutral when the goblins invaded the north."

"Ever since the goblin invasion and the breaking up of our nation into independent baronies, travel about the islands has become somewhat dangerous. Many marauders and strange creatures roam the less travelled roads: ye best beware!"

"The robber barons of the northeast are stirring up trouble again. They've been attacking trade caravans between Upper Umaldyr and Aurelian. Some say the baron of Ashkor may be involved as well in this renewed maurauding of the robber barons."
"Ye're in luck, for we have plenty of this import since trade has picked up with the Sword Lands, of the Realmz continent. So, that'll be 90 gp total. Which one of ye'll pay?"

Soon enough, you are brought goblets of Tanirith wine. You are pleased to find that it carries the body and aroma that have made wines from Tanirith ever so popular throughout the Sword Lands, and now beyond.

"This import is rarer since the siege of Wailsrond. At least, that's what me suppliers told me. Me fear it'll take a long time before stocks become more available and prices fall. But fer now, that'll be180 gp total. Which one of ye'll pay?"
"That'll be 18 gold pieces total. Who'll pay?"
"Hear ye, hear ye!" Booms a paige upon your entrance into the Hall, flanked by numerous militia soldiers. "His excellency, the Magistrate Histhuur, is now ready to hear and arbiter this case!"
"Hear ye, hear ye!" Booms a paige upon your entrance into the Hall, flanked by numerous militia soldiers. "His excellency, the Magistrate Xerol, is now ready to hear and arbiter this case!"
"Hear ye, hear ye!" Booms a paige upon your entrance into the Hall, flanked by numerous militia soldiers. "His excellency, the Magistrate Vykarh, is now ready to hear and arbiter this case!"

This old sign reads: "West Coast Ship Yards Company".
Soldiers are guarding the gates of this castle. "The Baron of Lake Hold is not seeing anyone today!" One of them snarls.
A sign posted outside of this building reads: "The Parched Stingray".
Although the place reeks of pipe smoke and bad alcohol, it is filled with regular folks, sailors, pier workers, fishermen and all sorts of shady characters.

A bunch of somber, tough-looking, and cocky drunks are sitting here. One of them, a huge and brawny man, rises up to you: "Whot do ye want, ye bums?" He asks menacingly, his hand already on the pommel of his weapon.
A beautifully wrought sign of iron reads: "Umaldyr's Finest Armors and Weapons".

This temple is dedicated to Dianchuur, God of Health and Healing.
This temple is dedicated to Athor, God of the Sun, the Sky and the Weather.
Looking at your shadow elf party member, you hope that your comrade will prove a good source of knowledge and insight during your explorations of the Underearth.
As if guessing your thoughts, you comrade shrugs, stating that the region of the Underearth you have entered is completely unfamiliar, if not unknown.

The sign on the door of this establishment reads: "Inn of the Long Journey".
A sign hanging outside of this building reads: "Lake Hold Waystation".
A sign hanging outside of this small building reads: "Lake Hold General Store".

Numerous mercenary guards are keeping watch at the gates of this castle. "The Baron of Valanyr receives no one today!" One of them intones.

A sign hanging on the door of this old building reads: "The Mariner's Deck".

Critically damaged, the Guardian self-destructs!

"Me swear this here mountain wall doesn't look right!" Braggan mumbles, as he scrutinizes the mountain cliff next to you. Looking closer as well, you realize that it is an illusion covering the entrance of a cave!
As you look closer at the mountain wall here, you realize that it is an illusion covering the entrance of a cave!

As you enter this small and windy valley, you see before you ancient cyclopean ruins towering the sterile landscape. These ruins stand undisturbed and foreboding, their weathered exterior testifying to their millennia-old age.
Thanks to your previous experiences, you recognize the almost 'alien' architecture of these ruins as belonging to the lost Macremian empire.
You enter the foreboding ruins.
Considering the circumstances and your defection to Storm's side, it would be best not to tempt the Fates by walking in the High Council of Tanirith.
Rock giants are squatting here: they are not happy at seeing you!
Just as you are about to enter this room, the self-imposed of the rock giants squatting in these ruins orders his followers to attck (looks like they heard your approach ...)
The hoarded valuables of the mountain giant are now yours to take!
You run into rock giants!
An electric field bars your way.
You get to the other side of the electric field!
The field is not magical in nature.
The mounds of piled rocks give in, revealing what lies underneath them!
Bashing away at the mounds of piled rocks with your weapons don't even dent them. Not wishing to break your precious weapons, you try to find another solution.
A decrepit fountain is here. Although still functional, its water is fouled and unfit for consumption.
You notice that some of the water spilling on the ancient floor trickles north toward two large mounds of piled rocks, seemingly disappearing under them.
You get down the steps, careful not to step on the hazardous rubble covering them.
Do you pull on this old, rusty lever?
You hear something massive move in the distance.
This old, rusty lever is hopelessly jammed.
Just as you approach this eerie doorway, it opens by itself to reveal a secret tunnel, carved beyond within the hard rock.

As you enter this room, a strange mechanical construct suddenly comes to life.  Quickly moving to block a door at the other end of the room, it raises it handless arms with mutiple clicks and whirls, while a strange shield lights up to surround it.

"Zuur dox tzarakyn?" It mutters in a mechanical voice. Not understanding a word, you look to each other, unsure of what to do next. The creature, however, does not hesitate for long: without any further due, it attacks!
"Please provide the appropriate password." It mutters in a mechanical voice.
"Password received and acknowledged." The construct replies impassively, before moving back to a corner of the room and return to stasis.
The mechanical construct pays you no attention, remaining silently in stasis in a corner of the room.
"Failure to provide the password! Counter-measures program initiated!" The construct intones, as it advances forward to attack!
Among the rotten and brittle books here, you spot a fairly preserved sheet of parchment. Unable to decipher the language and alphabet, you put it back where you found it, before moving on.

Among the rotten and brittle books here, you spot a fairly preserved sheet of parchment. While most of the stuff written appear to be rules of some sort, one set of words and a set of numbers attract your attention because they were written with red ink:
"emergency priority omega"

In conjunction with those two sets of red-inked characters, what's left of the writtings make mention of a "guardian", a "power core", and an "access door". You wonder what this all meant to the people who used to live here, so long ago.
This door made of some strange alloy does not appear to have any knob or keyhole. You notice however on the right side, embedded in the granite wall, some sort of square glass plate.
Softly glowing, the glass plate is adorned with ten symbols of various shapes. Unfortunately, you cannot fathom their meaning.
Softly glowing, the glass plate is adorned with ten symbols of various shapes which you decipher as being the equivalent of the numbers 1 to 0. Do you try to press a sequence of numbers?
What numerical sequence do you press?
The door slides open!

You enter some sort of repository. The place is filled with crumbling crates filled with junk made of all sorts of metals and materials, some of which you have never seen before. But at first glance, you find nothing of value in here.

You hear a strange feminine voice inside your head: " You must find the knight of the mind, for she is the key to the end of this cycle." The voice whispers. You wonder if your imagination is not playing tricks on you.

You hear a strange feminine voice inside your head: " You must find the knight of the mind, for she is the key to the end of this cycle." The voice whispers. Could this have been an augury from Myst, the Goddess of Dreams, Illusions and Mysteries?

You hear a strange feminine voice inside your head: " You must find the knight of the mind, for she is the key to the end of this cycle." The voice whispers. You wonder what this all means, and where that voice came from ... or who spoke to you this way.

You hear a strange feminine voice inside your head: "Much remains to be done before the end of this cycle can be accomplished." The voice whispers. You wonder what this all means, and where that voice came from ... or who spoke to you this way.

You hear a strange feminine voice inside your head: "Much remains to be done before the end of this cycle can be accomplished." The voice whispers. Could this have been an augury from Myst, the Goddess of Dreams, Illusions and Mysteries?

You hear a strange feminine voice inside your head: "Much remains to be done before the end of this cycle can be accomplished." The voice whispers. You wonder if your imagination is not playing tricks on you.

Your meticulous search reveals large boxes of lead within the creates here. Most of the boxes of lead are empty or contain dull crystals of no value, but one appears to hold something inside. Do you open it?
Opening the box, you find a large orb made of solid crystal. Radiating tremendous heat, there seems to be a raging fire trapped within this orb. Do you pick the orb out of its lead box?
Wisely, you close the box of lead and decide to carry the orb while safely contained in the box.
The moment the orb is picked up, you comrade is reduced to cinders by the tremendous energies contained within it!

"This is it!" Naryl exclaims, snatching the heavy box from your hands while backing away from you. She is gazing at the box with wonderment and triumph, craddling it in her arms protectively. You look at her with confusion and surprise.
Looking back to you with a smile of pure malice, she begins to laugh ... as her voice and appearance change to that of a man's!

"We meet again." The impostor muses, bowing his head in mock respect. "Yes," he continues with a snicker of disdain, "it is I, High Praetor Primus, at your service!" You instinctively reach for your weapons, only to find that you are unable to move!

Primus chuckles. "Of course, I am preventing you from making any harsh moves, lest you injure yourselves." He chimes derisively while gently tapping the side of his head with his index finger, to indicate that he is using his psionic powers to do so.

"Like the low-life mongrels that you are, you still do not comprehend the power that we, your superiors, wield at our command!" He snarls. "I should put you out of your misery right here and now!" He then sighs at that, shaking his head slowly.

"Deceiving you was all too easy, hapless fools that you are. However, you did help me recover the power stone, albeit unwittingly. Now, nothing can prevent our return to greatness!" At that, he looks to you with kindness and pity:

"You have been rather entertaining, even if irritating at times. That is why I promise you this: you will be well-treated slaves in the New Order that is to come." He smiles indulgently: "Now, time for me to go back to Ashkor: I have much to do!"

Primus then disappears in a flash of light. At the same time, you regain your freedom. Distraught at this devastating turn of events, you are riddled with questions: where is the real Naryl? What happened to her? What does Primus intends to do?

Have you failed? Is is too late? Taking a deep breath, you calm yourselves. Looking to each other, you know that you have may have one chance to make things right: journey as fast as you can to Ashkor, hoping to stop Primus there!
Numerous carpenters and craftsmen are putting the finishing touches or making repairs to boats anchored here.
A sign hanging on the door of this building reads: "Arcane Wonders Galore".
No one is working on this unfinished boat, at this time of the day.
Numerous carpenters and craftsmen are working hard on this unfinished boat.
Nearly finished boats, or boats needing repairs, are anchored here with no one about this pier at this time of the day.
Undead creatures eye you as their next meal.
No one appears to be about this building. On the door, a sign reads: "CLOSED. OFFICE HOURS: 6 in the morning until 8 in the evening".
A sign hanging on the door of this building reads: "OFFICE OPEN". Do you enter?
A furfoot cleck sits behind an office desk. "Welcome to West Coast Shipyards!" He muses, smiling agreably. "What may we do for ye?"
The furfoot shakes his head: "We don't rent boats here. We make them and folks with enough money buy them."
The furfoot shakes his head: "Sorry. Although our boats are quite in demand, we've enough carpenters and craftsmen hired already."
"All right, then." The furfoot replies, before returning his attention to his ledgers and paperwork. Having nothing else to do here, you leave.

"Sure!" The furfoot replies, all smiles. "That's what we do here! A boat cost 10000 gold pieces, payable with 100 gems, and ready for sail in 60 days garanteed! You pay half the cost now, and the remaining half when you come pick it up. We have a deal?"
"Great!" The furfoot chimes, as he gives you forms to fill out. "You have to pay half the cost now, so that'll be 50 gems, please." Which one of your party will pay?
"Perfect!" The furfoot replies as you hand him the gems. "Come back in at least 60 days: you then pay the rest of the cost and you'll have your boat!" With a firm nod, you leave.
"Not enough money? No boat then!" The furfoot replies, angry at having his time wasted. Having nothing else to do here, you leave.

"Your boat will be ready soon!" The furfoot clerk exclaims as you enter. "Come back when our deadline of 60 days will have passed: then you pay the rest of the cost and pick up your boat!" At that, you leave.
"Ah! Welcome back!" The furfoot clerk chimes. "Your boat is ready for you to board at our pier! All that's left is for you to pay the remaining 50 gems." Which one of your party will pay?
"Perfect!" The furfoot replies as you hand him the payment. "Go to our pier and all you have to do is get on board! Thank you for doing business with us!" At that, you leave for the pier.
You boat is ready to be boarded. Sleak in design and from all appearances expertly constructed, you congratulate yourself for having made such a good buy.

This old temple stands silent within a small clearing of the forest. Roofless, it allows anyone standing inside to see the sky or the stars. From its weathered columns and walls, it must be a few millennia old at the least.
You have no idea who erected this temple so long ago, nor to what God it is dedicated to.

"This is an ancient temple of Lugath!" Leira Songheart exclaims, wonderment sparkling in her golden eyes. She turns to you with excitement: "I know what I must do, now. I must stay here and renovate this temple, so that Lugath may be honored once again!"

"That is why the Fates brought me here, through you. I thank you, my comrades, and I wish you all the best for your travails ahead." Waving goodbye, Leira gracefully enters the temple to meditate and pray.
The ancient temple of Lugath, God of Nature, has been cleared already of weeds and rubble. However, Leira Songheart is nowhere to be seen. She is probably on some sort of errand.

"The design of this roofless temple bears semblance to temples dedicated to Astrane." Master Athos muses, while gazing critically at the structure. "However, the usual symbols related to Astrane, such as the moons and the stars, are missing."

He then snaps his fingers: "Of course! This old temple must have been dedicated to Lugath, the God of Nature! Similar designs, you see." He then shakes his head: "Still ... this doesn't look like any architecture that I recognize." He shrugs at that.
You spot in the distance a trade caravan under attack by marauders. Do you help the caravan?
Callously, you walk away.
"Death to the cowardly curs!" Scyrella yells, as she rushes ahead to help the caravan.
"Justice must be served!" Denard yells, as he rushes ahead to help the caravan.
"We must help them!" Jorale yells, as she rushes ahead to meet lend a hand to the caravan.
"We must help them!" Belrion yells, as he rushes ahead to lend a hand to the caravan.
"Moradin!" Braggan yells, as he rushes ahead to help the caravan.

The caravan master comes up to you after the battle: "Well fought, good strangers, and thank ye! It is to be hoped that one of them days, travelling the roads will become a less dangerous thing! Please accept this small token of our appreciation."
"I wish ye safe journeys and safer returns!" The caravan master bids you in farewell, before ordering the caravan to move on.
This worn out sign reads: "Circle Lake Shipyards Company".

As you enter this small, windy valley, you see a towering cyclopean construction. Entirely made of crystal and metal, it looks as if it was recently constructed. But deep down inside, you are certain that it is millennia old.
You overhear a fragment of a conversation spoken in the common tongue.
It looks like they have decided to establish a permanent presence to control the traffic through Galduur's Pass.
A furfoot cleck sits behind an office desk. "Welcome to Circle Lake Shipyards!" He muses, smiling agreably. "What may we do for ye?"

"Sure!" The furfoot replies, all smiles. "That's what we do here! A boat cost 20000 gold pieces, payable with 200 gems, and ready for sail in 30 days garanteed! You pay half the cost now, and the remaining half when you come pick it up. We have a deal?"
"Great!" The furfoot chimes, as he gives you forms to fill out. "You have to pay half the cost now, so that'll be 100 gems, please." Which one of your party will pay?
"Perfect!" The furfoot replies as you hand him the gems. "Come back in at least 30 days: you then pay the rest of the cost and you'll have your boat!" With a firm nod, you leave.

"Your boat will be ready soon!" The furfoot clerk exclaims as you enter. "Come back when our deadline of 30 days will have passed: then you pay the rest of the cost and pick up your boat!" At that, you leave.
"Ah! Welcome back!" the furfoot clerk chimes. "Your boat is ready for you to board at our pier! All that's left is for you to pay the remaining 100 gems." Which one of your party will pay?
You enter the foreboding citadel.

Entering the citadel, you are awed by its majesty. The crystalline and metallic walls pulsate with a soft blue light, humming with the rythm of the pulsations. Despite the incredible age this place must have, you find it in a pristine state.

Looking up, you are startled to see that the roof of the citadel reaches hundreds of feet high, conferring a mixed sense of megalithic proportions and eerie emptiness. It seems as if you are on the only floor of the place.

A familiar voice calling out takes you out of your reverie, as numerous psi-warriors storm from all sides to face you. Behind them stand Nyxos Uhn, Taroth Sark and Zeiia No. "Never say die, eh?" Uhn snarls derisively. "Time to change that!"
The lever is hopelessly jammed.

"Says who?" Naryl interjects, hatred flashing in her blue eyes. "Surprised to see me? The all-mighty, all-knowing Overlords didn't expect this? Hah! It just shows that the lot of you are no better than anyone else!" She takes a deep breath at that.

"I swore an oath", Naryl continues with clenched teeth, "that I would give my life if necessary to stop all of you and prevent the return of the Mind Lords! I'll not rest until I see the lot of you stripped of your mental powers, or dead, or both!"

"You are a misguided fool, psi-knight!" Zeiia No chimes in. "The Mind Lords will return, because they have never been completely gone. You know that their essences are even more lasting than ours. In fact, theirs are nearly immortal!" Sark nods at that.

"Aye. That is what our people refuse to see." He adds. "The Mentarchs are the epitome of what we can become. It's already in each of us, and that is why we are superior to all other mongrel races. Our minds are more evolved, and we can become gods!"

"Well spoken, Master Sark." Nyxos Uhn intones. "That is why our ancestors created the Mentarchs so long ago: to demonstrate how far we can go as a race. All the Mind Lords ever wanted was to raise us at their level, as to achieve our true destiny!"

"Therefore, why deny this?" Uhn continues. "Why deny ourselves of our genetic heritage, and of the wise guidance of the Mind Lords, those who have already achieved what we can be? Why deny ourselves godhood?" He shakes his head in sadness.

"We need not bow to placate the inferior mongrel races, or hide from them. We should not fear our destiny, but instead embrace it! Our final evolution is inevitable and will come quicker with the help of the Mind Lords. So come, and join us, psi-knight!"

"It's you who are blind!" Naryl retorts vehemently. "Blinded by a terrible past that you percieve as grandiose and glorious. The Mentarchs were a mistake, an aberration! They are mad with power! Didn't the War of the Mind Lords showed this, long ago?"

"The Mind Lords care about nothing but their own stature!" She continues. "To them, all races are mongrels fit to be slaves; and we are just good for them as worshiping servants! That's why we joined the other races against them, those millennia past!"
"And that is why I have sworn to stop fools like you who seek to bring them back!" Uhn nods firmly in response: "So be it, then!" At that, the Overlords and their psi-warriors attack!

A battered and bloodied Naryl walks up to you: "Now that we've taken care for good of these criminals, we must find Primus before it's too late." She sighs at that, looking pensively around her: "He must be in here, somewhere!" She whispers.
The power generator of the gate is silent and inactive. Inside it, you see that the power stone has turned into a dull, worthless crystal.
The gate is closed.

You find Primus standing before a large gateway. The construct is humming and glowing wildly, obviously activated and ready to be used. Next to Primus, you see a strange machine hooked to the gate through metallic cable, clickling and whirring loudly.

As you walk ahead to attack him, you are stopped by a telekinetic field. As you bumb on the field, Primus turns around to face you, smiling grimly with his arms folded over his chest. "Still around?" He muses. "And you brought the psi-knight along!"

He chuckles. "Do you know what this place is? A giant needle! Yes. A needle that harnests the electricity and magnetism of the air, in order to empower this fantastic gate. Of course, the needle itself needs to be activated, thanks to a power stone."

He sighs, gazing upwards with a smile. "Those macremians were something else, don't you think? It is no wonder then that we, lankharhans, descend from them!" He turns his gaze back to you: "I bet you did not know that, eh?" He asks, chuckling.

"Stop this madness now, Primus!" Naryl interjects, he voice authoritative and pleading at the same time. "What can you hope to accomplish by going through a gate?" Primus begins to laugh out loud at that.

"Primus?" He bellows between laughs. "Primus, you call me?" As he goes on laughing, you look to Naryl: her mouth is now agape and a look of dread is on her face, as if realizing something terrible. "Oh no!" She whispers to herself, confirming your guess.
She turns to you with alarm and outright panic: "He is hosting the essence of a Mind Lord, like I did with Kith Khanaan's last year!"

Seeing your look of confusion, Naryl tries to explain quickly what she meant: "We keryndorhians can preserve our essences, or souls, within solid receptacles prepared for that, after we die. I carry my talisman with me always, should I need to transfer

my essence in case I meet my demise. Of course, the Mind Lords could do that as well. Last year, the late Heroes of the Sword Lands and I found the preserved essence of a good Mentarch, Kith Khanaan. He is still preserved back in my homeland. But last

year, I offered him to infuse himself into my being, so that he could help us defeat the first three Overlords that were causing the troubles. He accepted, and thus I was his host ... my body his body, my mind his mind. Do you see?"

You now begin to understand all too well. You also comprehend what Uhn, No and Sark were babbling about, concerning the 'immortal essences' of the Mind Lords, as well as the terrible possibilities ... such as the one you are witnessing now.

"In effect, it was not Primus that we've been pursuing, but a Mentarch all along!" Naryl adds between clenched teeth, her stance rigid. "Not just any Mentarch, little knightling!" Primus snarls, smiling menacingly while glaring at her.

"But THE Mentarch!" He adds, his voice triumphant. Naryl steps back, aghast. "Maximus!?!" She mouths almost silently, with a look of outright fear and terror. "Yes!" 'Primus' replies. "Xenon Maximus, first-born and anointed Hierarch of the Mind Lords!"

As Primus/Maximus laughs anew, you grab Naryl by the shoulders, shaking her out of her panicked stupor while demanding what is going on. "All is lost ... He's the most powerful ... like a god." She replies, before leaning against the wall in despair.

You turn around to face the telekinetic field, bashing against it as hard as you can, feeling frustrated and helpless. Primus/Maximus chuckles at your futile attempts at weakening the field. "Ignorant mongrels." He intones. "The game is up!"

"Time for me to go to that place where the conditions will be ripe for me to bring back my brothers and sisters, while at the same time doing away with those kin of mine who, like Kith Khanaan, turned against me all those millennia ago!"

Primus/Maximus sighs. "Of course, the proper conditions to allow me to bring about our Glorious rebirth are not always simply a matter of place, but of time as well. The journey has been long for me, but well worth it!" He nods in satisfaction at that.

"From my demise twelve thousand years ago, to living in essence alone far beyond all this time, almost going insane; then to ten years ago, when Primus found me by chance ... and accepted to be my host, allowing me to finally prepare our return."

"So you see, my little Overlords were in the end meant as red herrings." He continues, basking in this moment of his seeming victory. "To throw off fools like you. All along, this 'needle' was the true goal. To find it, then restore it to a pristine,

fully functional state, and to learn its inner workings, so that I could modify the capabilities of the gate to fit my designs!" He chuckles anew: "I wonder if the macremians were ever aware of the full potential of this gate they constructed ..."

He shakes his head. "It doesn't matter anymore. In any case, all that was left for me to do was to find a power stone, which you did nicely for me." He snickers derisively. "But you did prove quite annoying in the end, especially with your presence here,

casting a cloud over my triumphant moment as I stand poised to claim anew our birthright as deserving rulers of this world! Still, I win. So, I bid you goodbye, mongrels. If the Fates allow it, I'll see you again yesterday, today and tomorrow!"
At these words, Primus/Maximus lowers his telekinetic field to unleash a powerful mind blast at you!
In an instant, Naryl rushes ahead of you to try to block the devastating attack!
Engulfed by the tremendous psionic energies, Naryl falls down in agony. However, she could not stop completely the attack.
Before you can regain your bearings, Primus/Maximus jumps into the gate! Once he is through, all the noises and hums cease, the place becoming dreadfully silent.
Confused, you run to Naryl's side.

Naryl lies on the floor, her body being slowly disintegrated by the psionic energies still coursing through her. "Not long ..." She whispers to you, bitting her lower lip to prevent herself from screaming in agony. "My talisman ... broken." She adds.

"Both mind and body ... will be gone." Unable to touch her and feeling utterly helpless, you tell her that all will be right in the end, that you will find a way to defeat Maximus. You always do. She shakes her head slowly, tears flowing from her eyes.

"You do not ... understand." She replies, her voice trembling and fading. "You may have solved the trouble in the Sword Lands ... and survived their greatest of wars ... but can even you escape ... the wrath of the Mind Lords?" She then gasps with pain.
"Goodbye ... my ... friends." She whispers with sadness. In a final seizure of agony, her body then vaporizes to nothingness before you.

Alone, you rise to stand to your feet, gazing blankly to the floor where Naryl laid an instant before. It dawns on you that you now stand alone in this all too quiet place. Alone with the uncertain future and those questions that are now plaguing you.

Were all your accomplishments truly futile? Where exactly did Maximus went to? How will he bring about his restoration to power, and that of his god-like brothers and sisters? And what did he mean by 'see you yesterday, today and tomorrow'?

Grieving for Naryl who sacrificed herself so that you may live on to continue the fight, you get the urge to leave this place, its silence beginning to weight heavily upon your wearied souls. As you make your first steps, one more question comes to you:
Have you really won for now, or have you lost already for good?
You look to Riel Moonsong, who looks as much grief-stricken as you are: "I find myself at a complete loss for words." He mumbles, shaking his head with sadness.
"Let us lick our wounds," Athos whispers, "so tha we may become stronger after."
"Thask will honor this psi-knight." Ellai mumbles, his eyes rimmed with tears.
"May Lugath bless this psi-knight." A tearful Leira whispers.
In response, a proverb comes to your mind, providing you with little solace: "Only time will tell ..."

Numerous guards and keeping watch at the castle gates of the Baron of Aurelyan.
"Your infamous reputation preceeds you, strangers from Realmz!" The captain of the guards intones sternly. "Be warned that we will not tolerate your meddlings into our affairs!"

"Your good reputation preceeds you, strangers from Realmz!" The captain of the guards intones, smiling. "The Baron would like very much for you to see him!" At that, the gates are open to allow you entry.
"The Baron sees no one today!" The captain of the guards intones sternly.
The gates are opened to allow you passage.
You enter the castle.
"No one but the Baron and the members of his family are allowed here!" Snarls a guard.
A stout man is sitting in a comfy chair at a large table, conferring with numerous folks that appear to be his advisors. Upon seeing you, he smiles and waves you to approach him.

"Welcome, noble folks!" The man chimes, smiling warmly. "I am Baron Azarch, Lord of Aurelyan. Didn't expect anyone to know you, eh?" He winks at that. "Actually, up until last week, I was in trade negociations with representatives from Tanirith."

The Baron chuckles. "Of course, they spoke at length of the war and of your accomplishments! In any case, I made very good deals with these folks from Tanirith: our mines produce adamandine, a very rare metal, and Tanirith wants to buy!" He sighs.

"Unfortunately, our rich mines are also the reason why our sovereignty is being challenged. Many a Baron dream of acquiring Aurelyan as his own, especially the Baron of Ashkor. But politics still prevent any Baron to attack openly another Barony ..."

"Thus," Baron Azarch continues, "underhanded, devious tactics are used. Currently, our trade caravans are being plagued by attacks from the Rogue Barons of the East, and I have it on good authority that Ashkor gets a percentage of the spoils!"

"So I ask you, good heroes, if you could rid us of this problem. Of course, a generous reward will be given out, should you succeed. I do not wish to be a pest, so I'll ask you only once: what say you?"
"Superb!" The Baron chimes. "Your reputation is by no means overstated; I approve, I approve!" With handshakes to seal the deal, you take your leave.
"Bah!" The Baron replies with disdain. "I should've known you reputation was overstated! Begone from here, then!" Rebuffed, you walk away.
The Baron is busy conferring with his advisors. You decide not to bother him.

As you come to this tunnel, numerous soldiers bearing the banners of Ashkor ar waiting for you: "There they are, as we were warned! Protect Baron Zuroz!" The captain of the guards bellows. At that, they attack!
More soldiers of Ashkor are waiting for you here!
Numerous guards and keeping watch at the castle gates of the Baron of Ashkor.

Just as you storm into the castle, you find yourselves facing a large number of soldiers. Among them you see Nyxos Uhn, smiling to another man: "See, Baron Zuroz?" The Overlord intones. "Like I told you: vicious mercenaries at the pay of Aurelyan!"

The Baron glares at you with hatred. "I knew Baron Azarch was wary of my activities, but I never thought him capable of making such a bold move. My thanks to you, and to Lord Primus, for warning me of this." He bows politely to Uhn at that.

"Our pleasure." Uhn replies amiably. "You have been a valuable ally to us, so it is only proper for us to render you such a service. I must go, now: I trust you can take it from here?" Baron Zuroz nods firmly, smiling grimly at you.

"But what of the other?" The Baron adds, jerking his head to a corner of the hall. Looking in that direction, you see Naryl Thezzat lying on the ground, in chains and wearing a strange helm over her head. "Do with her as you do to them." Uhn replies.
At that, the Overlord teleports away. At the same time, Baron Zuroz oders his men to attack!
Baffled by such outrageous lies and obvious machinations, you don't even attempt to deny Uhn's words.

You rush immediately to free Naryl from her chains. Once freed, she quickly removes the helm on her head, throwing it away. "It's a psi-nullifier that they forced on me." She snarls, in explanation as to why she was wearing it. She then turns to you:

"But how did you-, could you-?" She asks baffled, yet smiling with relief and happiness at seeing you. You quickly put her up to date on the latest developments. "By the Stars!" She exclaims, aghast. "Primus kidnapped me one or two sevendays ago!"

"He did it while we were camping. I never saw it happen; in fact, I remember falling asleep, then awakening here, bound in chains and my psionic powers inhibited!" You reply that none of you ever caught on to the switch either. Naryl shakes her head.

"I would've never guessed Primus capable of such a level of discipline, of power ... I don't like this." She muses pensively. "In any case, my friends, we must get out of here with haste! I heard Uhn mention something about joining Primus and the others,
who were waiting in some macremian ruins! I fear that, with the power stone in their hands, they will be able to do what they have set out to do all along: bring back the Mind Lords!"
As you hear some mercenary soldiers and locale populace of the Barony beginning to loot the place, you run as fast as you can to get out of the castle and the castle grounds!
"Now," Naryl adds, as much as out of breath as the rest of you, "we must find the macremian ruins where the Overlords have gone to!" You nod with determination.

Numerous soldiers bearing the banners of Aurelyan and Koralya are patrolling the castle gates of Ashkor. A large sign has been nailed on the wall: "Due to lawlessness, the Baronies of Aurelyan and Koralya have taken Ashkor under their protection."
A sign hanging on the door of this place reads: "Aurelyan General Market".

Soldiers paid by the Baron of Koralya come in and out of the barracks; some are heading of for guard duty, others are going out on training.

The whole goblin tribe has entrenched itself around the hut of their chief, waiting for you. Hundreds of goblin warriors stand poised to attack. "Begone from our lands!" The goblin chief bellows, as his warriors begin to snarl and grumble menacingly.
At your insistence on invading their lands, the goblin chief orders his archers to launch a volley of arrows at you!
The chief orders a first wave of warriors to attack!

You tell him that you will leave only with the daughter of the Baron of Koralya. The ransom was paid and therefore she should be freed. "Me want more money!" The chief replies, as his warriors mumble and grumble in agreement. "Me want 500 more gems!"

The chief himself and his best warriors now enter the fray!

At the defeat of their chief, the rest of the goblin tribe scatters out in panic. You know this will be only temporary, given their large numbers. Searching quickly the chief's hut, you find the baron's daughter bound and gagged.
With reassuring words, you free the frightened girl. With great determination, you rush her out of the hut and make haste to return her safe and sound to her father.

Baron Korol goes into a fit of grief and despair upon seeing you carrying the limp body of his daugther. Snatching her away from you, he lays her on the floor, crying. As aides rush to his side to comfort him, guards silently motion you to leave.

"Syphalle!" Baron Korol shouts with happiness and relief, as his little daughter runs into his arms. As they hug each other, Korol looks at you, tears welling up in his eyes: "Thank you so much for returning her to us!" He mumbles emotionally.
As father and young daughter continue hugging each other, one of the Baron's aides brings you a small chest, smiling.
Leaving the grateful father and daugther to their happy reunion, you take your leave, glad to have done yet another good deed. You are certain that all will be fine from now on in Koralya.
The baron is busy conferring with his aides and advisors. You see little Syphalle happily playing with other children of the castle. Having no particular reason to bother the Baron, you leave.

Work in the mines of the town appears to be carried on undisturbed.

"How eager he was to accept me!" Maximus muses, gazing over the hands of his host body, Primus' body. "And he helped me find eight others of like-mind as his, so as to honor my eight brothers and sisters who, with me, formed the Glorious Council of

Mentarchs! Of course, this so-called Inner Council of Overlords that we formed was but a tool, and what great tools these lackeys have been!" He chuckles with satisfaction. "They were also very eager to help me find this macremian needle,

and so I ingratiated them with this diversion of establishing a power base in the Sword Lands for the purpose of restoring the Lankharhan empire. But knowing what I truly needed to do to restore the glory of us Mentarchs,

it never really mattered whether they succeeded or not!" He sighs, smiling with self-indulgence. "But they were so loyal and useful, that I had to play the part of Primus as First Speaker of our little Inner Council, even devising most of their 'plans'."

"Twelve Mentarchs arose in all, forming together a Council. Of these twelve super-beings, not much else is known. However, legends often mention the name of Xenon Maximus as the Hierarch, or leader, of this Council of Mentarchs."
"In any case, the evil Nine were eventually defeated and destroyed, leaving the Empire of Lankharh ruined and fragmented in the wake of their madness."
With much urgency, you then proceed to tell the Lord Paladine how you have uncovered a plot to assassinate him.
With a firm nod, you take your leave.
Having much more urgent things to do, you decide you should not be waisting time here and back away.
He nods pensively: "Well, then! I will give news to the High Council of this auspicious turn of events!"

"In the meantime, we need you to find out who or what is behind the subversion of those councilors! If you haven't spoken yet to Jarad Noll about this, then do it now! The situation is becoming critical! Until then, there's nothing else I dare do."
"This force will be waiting for you at the southwest gates of the city. From there, you are to march straight to Sharranth and give them the regards of our late wailsrondese friends!"

You find Red Dragonsbane sitting here, quietly sipping a tankard of ale, careful not to be recognized by anyone. "You are out!" He greets you, with a smile. "Let us resume our travails then!" At that, he picks up his gear to rejoin you.
You find Naryl Thezzat sitting here, quietly sipping a tankard of ale. "You are out!" She greets you, with a smile. "Let us resume our travails then!" At that, she picks up her gear to rejoin you.
You find Scyrella Silverspear sitting here, quietly enjoying her meal. "You are out!" She greets you, with a smile. "Let us resume our travails then!" At that, she picks up her gear to rejoin you.
Surely, you don't think you could enter there with the armed contingent that is accompanying you?

Weary and tired knights of the Flame are standing guard here. They do not look very well. "Stay back!" One of them urges you. "It is good that you are not ill, but I fear the plague has even reached us and the Lord Paladine as well."

"By all that is blessed!" He exclaims, gaping at the Icon. "Who needs Gods, when we have you, eh?" Laughing with joy and relief, the knight takes the Icon: "Tanirith is saved! I'll bring this to the Lord Paladine!" He chimes.

Amidst the cries of joy and happiness from the other knights, the knight hands you a small coffer: "As promised, a well deserved reward! We now have much to do, for we must coordinate the use of the Icon with all our temples to cure those afflicted."

"It'll take a while," the knight adds, with determination, "but this plague will be wiped out! Thanks to the Icon, and you! Once this plague is dealt with, come back to see the Lord Paladine!" As he runs off to the castle with the icon, you leave.

Weary and tired knights of the Flame are standing guard here. "Stay back." One of them urges you. "It is good that you are not ill, but no one's to enter the castle grounds until this terrible plague running in our city is fully eradicated."
Denizens of these ruins eye you for lunch!

Your thorough search of the area reveals some ancient, crumbling ruins buried by trees, grasses, branches and roots. Hacking away at the growth with your weapons, you expose the ruins as they remain: from the architecture, these look like elven ruins.
Inside the open-air ruins, you find a flight of crumbling stairs going underground. Do you take the stairs?

"I don't think we should venture down there." Riel muses, obviously worried. "I suspect we've just stumbled upon ruins of the old elven Forest-Kingdom of Aurystan. These ruins are said to be sacred and should remain undisturbed, lest we be cursed!"

"Me friends." Braggan chimes in. "We mustn't enter them ruins. Them are of the lost elven Forest-Kingdom of Aurystan, which was destroyed centuries past by Ptaraz the Mighty. Me've heard stories that them ruins be cursed and all!"

"These ruins belong to the lost elven Forest-Kingdom of Aurystan!" Leira exclaims, outraged. "These ruins are sacred to us elves, and they should not be violated in any manner! We leave these ruins undisturbed NOW!"
You return to the surface.
You find a loose marble plate at the base of th stairs. Removing the plate, you uncover a small lever. Do you pull on it?
Do you pull on the small lever hidden in the base of the stairs?
A strange sound emanates from the doors within this hall.
A strange, shimering field of energy surrounds this door. The field does not appear magical in nature.

Just as you pass through this door, disembodied spirits of elven maiden appear before you, eyeing you sternly. "Begone from here!" One of them intones. "These ruins are sacred to elves and should not be violated!" At that, the spirits disappear.

From the skeletons of elves and humans strewn about this place, a savage clash must have occured here ages ago. What remains of the warriors' uniforms, armors and weapons is now mostly useless, testifying to the centuries gone since this happened.
A disembodied feminine voice suddenly booms throughout the hall: "INTRUDERS ARE NOT WELCOME HERE. THIS SACRED PLACE MUST BE PROTECTED!" At that, some of the elven skeletons rise up!
"DO YOUR DUTY!" The disembodied voice adds, before the skeletons rush to attack.
It would seem that the "residents" of this place are not of the welcoming kind indeed ...

"I told you." Muses Riel, with a distinctive edge of anger in his voice. "We should leave this place well enough alone. Powerful spirits, and righteous ones at that, are guarding these ruins!" He shakes his head in exasperation.
"YOU WERE WARNED!" The disembodied voice suddenly booms, as more elven skeletal warriors materialize before you!
More spirits appear!
You enter a large hall filled with book shelves. This place must have been some kind of library.

After the battle, you glance over to Riel. Your comrade is fuming but otherwise remains silent. Obviously, he is convinced that you should leave this place. The spirits are certainly trying their best to convince you of that.
A strange field of energy blocks access to the library. The field does not appear to be magical, and seems to englobe all of this area of the place.
This is a statue of Lore, God of Knowledge and Wisdom.

This is an old and rusty ceremonial urn, often used for burning incense. You notice half-burnt scraps of parchment sheets within the urn, amdst what looks like fresh ashes. Someone recently burned parchement in this urn ... but to what purpose?
You drop a few sheets of parchment in the urn.
Having put parchment sheets in the urn, what do you want to do next?
You pour the contents of one of your flasks of oil over the parchment sheets.
Having doused the parchment sheets with flammable oil, what do you want to do next?
Hitting your weapon against the rim of the urn, you create sparks that ignite the oil-doused parchment sheets!
You ignite the oil-doused parchment sheets!
Shortly after you have lit the urn, a spirit appears next to the old throne.
This spirit bear the likelyness of an old elven scholar. He hovers a few inches above the florr, looking at you while motioning you to walk over to him.
The urn is alit still.
Without further due, the High Keeper disappears back whence he came.
At the same time, the fire in the urn dies out.
"DO NOT BOTHER TO SUMMON ME A SECOND TIME." Booms the disembodied voice of the High Keeper, in final parting.
The ashes of your fire lie within the urn.

"I am the High Keeper of the Lord Halls of Aurystan. Upon the fall of our peaceful kingdom at the hands of men, we swore that they would never acquire that which is our most cherished and valuable possession: our knowledge." He nods.

"That is why our books are not accessible to no one but other elven lore keepers, and so it shall be until the end of time. However, you have proven your mettle as well as your intelligence: therefore, I am willing to impart some of my knowledge."
What do you reply?

"We established the Forest-Kingdom of Aurystan some fifteen hundred years before the first men came to this region. Our home was located in what you call today the Harrow Woods, which surround the town of Aranys in these current times."

He chuckles dryly. "In our time, the forest of Aurystan was easily twice the size of its current state. When men began to arrive in the region some twelve hundred years ago, we befriended them. We even allowed eventually the construction of a road

passing through our kingdom, so that their cities may be linked for trade and free travel.  They had given us assurances that the villages and sacred places of our kingdom would never be trespassed. But then came the Scourge, the one you call Ptaraz."

He shakes his head in disgust: "The Scourge's army of bloodthirsty killers, aided by hordes of demons summoned by his consort Tanira, overran our forest-kingdom to pillage and lay it to waste. Thus, some seven centuries past, our kingdom fell and
my people fled the Sword Lands, in order to find a better place to live." The High Keeper hangs his head low at that.

The High Keeper lifts his head with pride: "While we were fighting the Scourge's armies, we managed to place seals -both magical and otherwise- to protect our most sacred places, such as our temples or our Hall of Lore. And those of us who died

while defending our positions or placing the seals, we pledged our souls to protect our sacred places even after death. Thus the ruins of our kingdom of Aurystan remained for centuries untouched and unexplored, unsoiled by looters and other pillagers."

"But some four centuries past came the Great Quake, which toppled to the ground nearly all that remained of our ruins. Then the year right after came a terrible battle within the forest, where powerful magics were used, obliterating our ruins as

well as most of the forest. In time, the trees, grasses and ferns came back, covering what little was left of our ruins, of the testimony of our past presence in this region. As you saw for yourselves, even constructions underground did not fare well

after such consequent disasters. Likewise, many of our seals were dissipated. I know for a fact that our Lore Hall is somewhat of an exception, however battered and crumbling as it is. In any event, we remain to guard our sacred places."

He chuckles: "I knew you would ask me such a question, for I am aware of the path you are currently walking upon. When my people settled in the forest of Aurystan of old, we found a strange, millennia-old man-made construction within the forest. This was

odd since men had not arrived yet to settle the Sword Lands. Eventually, some of us lost to their curiosity and dared to enter the ruins. Within, they found the remains of a man still dressed in his gear, lying next to a small, glowing talisman. His name

was Kith Khanaan. His living spirit, or essence, spoke to us through the talisman. He spoke of the War of the Mentarchs, or Mind Lords, and how it destroyed an empire of wonders. He told us about the Nine who were opposed by himself and two others,

and how five of the Nine were destroyed. He then told us of the ability of his kin to preserve one's essence, and that the last four of the Nine had done so. Fearing their eventual return, he crossed the oceans to hide the talismans that held their

essences. His nobility touched us, so we placed him in a shrine of his own in a remote place. I can tell you that his ruins, and even the four talismans, have been destroyed by the devastating quake and battle that decimated our own ruins also."

"So that is why Kith Khanaan left us and came here, nine thousand years ago." Naryl muses. "Even to this day, he refuses to answer this question. Now we know: he secreted the talismans of the last four surviving Mentarchs so that they never be found!"
She then chuckles: "And we now know who buried him in the Volcanic Rockies: the elves of old!" She shakes her head in amazement.

A half-drunk adventurer accosts you: "Hey, ye! I've got a map to some interesting ruins. My party is either gone or dead, and I don't feel like adventuring anymore. So I'll sell the map to ye fer 5 gems. Deal?"
"Don't want to spend or not enough money, eh? Then stop bothering me!"
He pockets the gems and hands you the map, before going back to his drink.
